body:
Status: DRAFT for Marc's approval · Nov 9, 2026 · Owner: Marc

Covers: the list of canon documents, which one wins when they disagree, and how a rule is added or changed. Does not cover: any rule itself (each lives in its own canon document).

What canon is

  1. Canon is the set of rules for how Endless Tales works. If code, an older document, an agent's memory or a chat disagrees with canon, canon wins and the code or document is fixed to match.
  2. Every rule lives in exactly one canon document, the one for its step. Other documents point to it; they never repeat it.
  3. Every rule is marked one of three ways:
    • Agreed: Marc decided it. The source and date are shown.
    • In force (code): the code does this today, but Marc never decided it. It needs Marc's OK to become Agreed.
    • Proposed: a rule the audit thinks is needed. It is not in force until Marc approves it.
  4. Every canon document starts with a "Where Marc decides" list, and each of those rules carries a tag: MARC DECIDES (Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK) or MARC DOES (something only Marc does himself, such as testing on his phone, listening, or entering a key). Agents never act in Marc's place on a tagged rule. CANON-98 lists every one of them in one place.
  5. A document marked DRAFT is not law yet, except the rules in it already marked Agreed. When Marc approves a document, its status changes to APPROVED with the date.
    • Nov 9, 2026: Marc approved CANON-01 to CANON-15. Every rule in them is law, including rules marked In force (code) or Proposed that a decision did not change; a Proposed rule that Marc wants changed goes through CANON-99.

The canon documents

#DocumentThe step it governs
00Canon Index (this document)How canon works
01Story Production ProcessThe whole path from idea to live story; who does each step
02Story Ideas, Series Planning & BriefsGenres, authors, premises, series length, series bible, hook series
03The WriterEverything about writing the script, including text the voices will speak
04Belle & PersonalizationBelle's intros and outros, the listener's name
05VoicesCasting, narrators, voice reuse, ElevenLabs
06Sound EffectsSound library, licenses, spot and background sounds, screening
07Music & Final MixThe six-channel mix drawing, levels, sting, fades, loudness
08Quality Checks & ReviewEvery check from brief to publish, and what Marc reviews
09Publishing & ReleaseThe publish switch, publishing all episodes together, hiding, unpublishing
10Covers & eBooksCover images and eBook text
11The PlayerHow playback, saving, auto-continue and the end of a story work
12The Listener AppSign-up, trial, prices, library, playlists, ratings, paywall, settings
13Marketing & AdsMeta rules (Amendment 1), hook ads, budgets, testing, stop rules
14Finance & ReportingThe finance statement, revenue, costs, plow back, LTV and CAC
15Agents & OperationsAgent rules, merges, deploys, security, who does what
98Every Marc Decision PointOne list of every rule that needs Marc's decision or action
99Decisions NeededEvery open conflict and question, with a recommendation

Which document wins

  1. When two canon documents seem to disagree, the one that owns the step wins (for example, the Player wins on playback; the Writer wins on script text). If it's still unclear, ask Marc. Never guess.
  2. A newer decision by Marc beats an older one. The date on each rule shows which is newer.
  3. The files the story writer loads into its prompts (Bible/CANON_REGISTRY_STORY_RULES.md, Bible/ET_Story_Rules_v3_2_CANONICAL.md, docs/STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT.md, docs/BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md) must say the same thing as CANON-03 and CANON-04. When they differ, the canon document wins and the prompt file is updated.
  4. Any document not on this list is history or reference, not law.

How a new rule is made (the only way)

  1. Anyone may spot the need: Marc, Claude, or an agent. An agent that meets a situation no canon rule answers, or two rules that disagree, stops that step and reports "RULE NEEDED:" with the situation in one or two sentences. It never guesses or invents a rule.
  2. Claude drafts it. Claude picks the one canon document that owns the step, writes the rule in plain words, checks it against every canon document for conflicts and gaps, and adds a recommendation (and the options, when there is a real choice).
  3. It goes on CANON-99 as the next numbered item, marked Proposed, naming its document, the rule text, why it is needed, any conflict it settles, and the code it would change.
  4. Marc decides. Marc replies "approve N", "change N: …", or "reject N". Several at once are fine ("approve 125–130"). Nothing is law until Marc says so.
  5. Claude writes it in. An approved rule goes into its document marked Agreed (Marc, date), with a MARC DECIDES or MARC DOES tag where it needs Marc, and its CANON-99 item is marked APPROVED. Admin is rebuilt in the same pull request. Claude lists any code that must change to match; those changes are separate pull requests that Marc merges.
  6. Changing or removing a rule follows the same path: Claude proposes the change on CANON-99, Marc decides.
  7. Only Marc adds, changes or removes a rule. Agents never edit canon.
  8. Every canon document can be read in Admin → Documentation → Canon (rules). The files live in the code repository at docs/canon/. CANON-99 always shows what is waiting for Marc.
  9. The canon's numbers live in one code file, lib/canon/numbers.ts, and an automatic test (CANON-GUARD-001) fails whenever the code or a writer prompt file disagrees with them. When Marc approves a changed number, the canon document, that file and the code change together in one pull request. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 item 126)

Earlier canon this set brings together

  • docs/PLAYER-RULES.md: copied into CANON-11 word for word. CANON-11 was approved Nov 9, 2026, so CANON-11 is now the rule; PLAYER-RULES.md carries a banner pointing to it.
  • docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md: its rules are in CANON-01, 03, 04, 08, 09 and 10, approved Nov 9, 2026. Those documents are now the rule; PIPELINE-CANON.md carries a banner pointing to them.
  • AGENTS.md keeps a short Canon index that points here.

body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: every step from idea to live story, in order; who runs each step; job states; retries; stuck and failed jobs; restore points and recovery. Does not cover: the detailed rules inside each step. Those live in CANON-02 (ideas and briefs), CANON-03 (writer), CANON-04 (Belle), CANON-05 (voices), CANON-06 (sound effects), CANON-07 (music and mix), CANON-08 (quality gates), CANON-09 (publishing), CANON-10 (covers and eBooks).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 14 MARC DECIDES: Publish switch. The switch is read at this moment. Review: Marc listens and approves. Direct: the story goes live with no review. Owner: CANON-09.
  • Rule 20 MARC DECIDES: Marc decides: merges outside Claude's own pipeline PRs, every database migration, the publish switch, the release of the publication hold, and…
  • Rule 32 MARC DECIDES: Adding episodes never re-plans or rewrites existing episodes. Use scripts/series/continue-series.ts (dry run, Marc approves the plan). Never run…
  • Rule 35 MARC DECIDES: Never merge a PR without Marc's word (except rule 18), and never run a migration without Marc's OK.
  • Rule 56 MARC DECIDES: Stop and ask Marc when any step could overwrite or hide live content.
  • Rule 57 MARC DECIDES: Author-written series (Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten by the pipeline. On a failed check it stops and reports; only approved…
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. The steps, in order

Each line gives: step name, what runs it, and which canon doc owns the rules for that step.

  1. Idea or queue item. A story starts as a row in story_queue_items (status queued) or as a series plan from Strategos (series blueprint, steps 1–2 of the 14-step map). Owner of rules: CANON-02. — In force (code) (supabase/migrations/20260515144738_update_story_queue_lifecycle.sql; memory /projects/…/areas/agent-fleet.md, Strategos owns the blueprint)
  2. Brief. The story gets a brief (brief_json; story row status = brief_complete). For a series, a whole-series plan comes before Episode 1. Owner: CANON-02. — Agreed (Marc Oct 29, 2026: "a whole-series plan before episode one … permanent", memory /projects/…/areas/story-pipeline.md)
  3. Dispatch. The dispatch-queue cron (every 1 minute) turns queued stories into one production_jobs row per standalone story or per series. At most 8 new jobs per run. — In force (code) (vercel.json crons; app/api/cron/dispatch-queue/route.ts, MAX_DISPATCH_PER_RUN = 8, Marc GO Jul 10 for ATL-IO-CAP-001)
  4. Runner. Four production-runner workers (every 1 minute) call run-next, which runs one step of one job at a time. — In force (code) (vercel.json; app/api/cron/production-runner/route.ts; app/api/admin/production-jobs/run-next/route.ts)
  5. Script. Standalone step generate_script; series step generate_episode_script. Owner: CANON-03. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts lines 223–252)
  6. Script checks. Standalone: validate_voice_conformance → validate_script → validate_story_resolution. Series: score_validate_package (includes the series continuity check and the Gemini script read, report-only). Owner: CANON-08. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts; lib/geminiStoryRead.ts)
  7. Story clarity check runs before any voicing money is spent. Until the gate is built, a reviewer applies it by hand. Owner: CANON-08. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY RULE, Marc Nov 8, 2026)
  8. Voice check and voices. voice_preflight / series_voice_preflight, then generate_voices / series_generate_voices. Owner: CANON-05. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts)
  9. Belle. generate_belle_assets → validate_belle_assets → validate_belle_quality (repair step repair_belle_quality); series: series_generate_belle_assets. Owner: CANON-04. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts)
  10. Sound effects. Placed from the approved sound catalog during the mix. Owner: CANON-06. — Agreed (Marc Oct 31: closed catalog, no AI fallback, memory story-pipeline.md)
  11. Music and final mix. generate_music / series_generate_music, then render_final_mix / series_render_final_mix. Owner: CANON-07. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts)
  12. Package. complete_story_package fills author, narrator, cover, description and eBook text (prose_text), then sets the story hidden at status = audio_ready. Owner: CANON-10 for cover and eBook. — In force (code) (app/api/admin/complete-story-package/route.ts)
  13. Ready for review. Job ends at step ready_for_review; story workflow_state = ready_for_review. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts NEXT_STEP_AFTER_STANDALONE_PACKAGE)
  14. MARC DECIDES Publish switch. The switch is read at this moment. Review: Marc listens and approves. Direct: the story goes live with no review. Owner: CANON-09. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md "What listeners can see" 4, Marc Nov 8)
  15. Live. The story is live only when status = published, is_hidden = false and published_on is set, and it shows in library-new. Owner: CANON-09. — Agreed (AGENTS.md production success criteria; lib/directPublish.ts isListenerVisible)
  16. A story is done only when the correct script was used, Belle intro and outro are correct, the sting and music are present when expected, the final mix is exported and imported, the story publishes, and it appears in library-new. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "Production success criteria"; DONE_CHECKLIST.md)

B. Who does what

  1. Claude (the pipeline writer) writes every script. No agent, including Hal and Orion, writes or edits scripts. — Agreed (AGENTS.md agent rules; Marc Nov 8, 2026, memory agent-fleet.md)
  2. Claude delivers code changes as PRs on main. Claude may merge its own pipeline PRs only after tests, the Vercel build and mergeability pass. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md, Nov 6 rule)
  3. Orion is the only EC2 deployer. He deploys merged main from a handoff Marc pastes. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)
  4. MARC DECIDES Marc decides: merges outside Claude's own pipeline PRs, every database migration, the publish switch, the release of the publication hold, and anything that could overwrite or hide live content. — Agreed (AGENTS.md agent rules; PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4)
  5. Marc is left out of routine production. He steps in only when he chooses or a rule requires it (for example Review mode). — Agreed (Marc Nov 7, 2026: "leave me out of the process", memory story-pipeline.md)
  6. Marc no longer approves voice casts for each story, once voices are screened into the voice database. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4, 2026, memory story-pipeline.md)
  7. Every status claim is verified by the one reporting it (a database query, file line, or command output in hand). Anything not checked is called "unverified". — Agreed (AGENTS.md "Verify results field by field"; Atlas/Orion reporting standard Oct 16, memory pipeline-dispatch-recovery.md)

C. Job and story states

  1. Job status values (production_jobs.status): queued (waiting for a runner), running (a runner holds it), waiting_for_external (waiting on an outside service), complete, failed, cancelled. Only queued and running may show as "active" on any screen. — In force (code) (lib/dispatchGuards.ts)
  2. One active job per story or series. A new job is never created while one is queued, running or waiting_for_external. — In force (code) (lib/dispatchGuards.ts; migration 20260709100000 unique indexes)
  3. Story workflow_state values and meaning:
    • stories_in_queue: waiting to be produced.
    • scripts_ready: script written, not yet produced.
    • ready_for_review: produced and hidden; waiting on the publish switch.
    • approved_ready: approved; next step is publish.
    • published: live (only when also unhidden with a publish date).
    • unpublished_library: was published, now hidden.
    • repair_queue (shown as "Production Holds") and being_repaired: held for a fix.
    • failed: production failed.
    • cold_storage: retired; never produced or shown. — In force (code) (lib/workflowTransitions.ts WORKFLOW_STATES)
  4. Only allowed state moves are used, per the table in lib/workflowTransitions.ts. Every move records who, when and why (workflow_state_changed_by/_at/_reason). — In force (code) (lib/workflowTransitions.ts; ORION-GOV-006)
  5. Queue item status values: queued, in_v2, ready_for_asc, dispatched, producing, complete, published, failed, archived. — In force (code) (migration 20260515144738)

D. Strict ordering (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3)

  1. Episodes run strictly in order, one at a time. Episode N starts only after Episode N−1 passes. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3, Marc Oct 4, 2026)
  2. A problem affects only the episode now running. It never pulls back earlier episodes and never jumps ahead. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3)
  3. A passed episode is locked. It is never re-checked or re-run because of a later episode. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3 scope)
  4. MARC DECIDES Adding episodes never re-plans or rewrites existing episodes. Use scripts/series/continue-series.ts (dry run, Marc approves the plan). Never run /api/v2/series-package on a series that already has episodes. — Proposed (PIPELINE-CANON SERIES-CONTINUATION RULE, still PENDING Marc sign-off)

E. Code changes and dispatch

  1. No dispatch before PR merge. A story that needs a code fix is not dispatched until that fix is merged and deployed. — Agreed (Sequencing Rule, Marc Jul 22, 2026, PERMANENT, cited in PIPELINE-CANON header)
  2. Before merge, check any renamed or replaced component with a diff. — Agreed (Pre-Merge Check, Marc Jul 23, 2026, PERMANENT)
  3. MARC DECIDES Never merge a PR without Marc's word (except rule 18), and never run a migration without Marc's OK. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  4. One task at a time. One change per deploy, so any break points to one change. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "One objective per cycle"; Story Production Spec §9.3, Nov 7 draft)
  5. Never deploy during a mix or voice job. Orion deploys at a safe gap between jobs. — Proposed (practice in deploy handoffs, Oct 27–Nov 5 chats; never stated as a rule by Marc)

F. Retries, stuck jobs and failed jobs

  1. Classify before fixing. Every stuck story is labeled A (pipeline defect: fix the code and add a guard) or B (story defect: send it back for an automatic fix and re-run). Every block report states A or B. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 1; CLASSIFY-BEFORE-FIX LOOP, Marc Oct 3)
  2. Quality checks stop the run. They never warn and continue. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 2) — details in CANON-08.
  3. Network blips resume automatically at the same step, up to 6 times. — In force (code) (lib/transientResume.ts MAX_TRANSIENT_RESUMES = 6, RETRY-NET-001)
  4. A job that stops moving is a "zombie" after 15 minutes (running, no lock, no update). It is failed with a clear report and can be safely retried from its step. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts ZOMBIE_STALE_MS)
  5. Failure circuit: 3 failed jobs for the same story or series within 2 hours stops new dispatch and moves the stories to Production Holds. — In force (code) (lib/dispatchGuards.ts DISPATCH_FAILURE_THRESHOLD; ATL-DISPATCH-DEFECTS-001)
  6. Retry cap: 5 failed jobs in 7 days stops re-dispatch. A series with the same failure 3 times stops. — In force (code) (lib/dispatchGuards.ts RETRY_CAP, SERIES_IDENTICAL_FAILURE_CAP)
  7. Outside failures (API key, balance, provider): 4 in 12 hours pauses dispatch for 30 minutes; 12 in 48 hours flags needs_attention. Episodes are not moved. — In force (code) (lib/dispatchGuards.ts; dispatch-queue/route.ts)
  8. Step retry limits: Belle blocked 2 repair cycles; series Belle 3; music 3; segment voices 3; script rewrite 2; ready-for-review 2; series render 5. When spent, the story is flagged needs_attention and the job stays failed. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts MAX_* constants)
  9. One repair pass only. A story that fails production a second time after a repair goes to cold storage. — Agreed (Marc ruling Jul 9, 2026; lib/workflowTransitions.ts ONE_REPAIR_PASS_REASON) — see Conflict C2.
  10. needs_attention stops dispatch for that story or whole series until cleared. — In force (code) (dispatch-queue/route.ts Gate A)
  11. Spending cap: a paid step does not start when the routine production spend cap is reached. — In force (code) (run-next/route.ts SPEND_CAP_BLOCKED)
  12. Kill switch: PRODUCTION_RUNNER_PAUSED=true stops all runners with no code change. — In force (code) (production-runner/route.ts)
  13. A paused or failed job is never restarted by hand without saying why in the job log, and a manual re-queue resets that step's retry counter. — Proposed (fills gap: manual requeues are common in chats but not written down; music counter reset is in code)

G. Restore points and recovery

  1. Never change the live production path without a restore point first. — Agreed (AGENTS.md hard guardrails; DONE_CHECKLIST.md "Safety")
  2. Never replace a working path with a simpler fallback. Keep working behavior before improving it. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  3. A restore point is: the last good commit on main named in the PR, plus the previous build folder kept on EC2 (.next.bak-<date>). A failed deploy restores that copy and restarts. — Proposed (matches Orion deploy handoffs Oct 27; .restore/ folder exists but has no rule)
  4. Recovery of a broken file is from git, never by patching on top of a broken file. — In force (doc) (MASTER_RULES.md "Restore from Git") — Proposed to confirm as canon.
  5. Production jobs are history. Old failed job rows are never deleted or rewritten when a story is recovered. — Proposed (docs/CONTENT_APPROVAL_PROVENANCE.md, planning doc only)
  6. MARC DECIDES Stop and ask Marc when any step could overwrite or hide live content. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)

H. Author-written stories

  1. MARC DECIDES Author-written series (Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten by the pipeline. On a failed check it stops and reports; only approved mechanical edits are made. It skips Belle style checks and the runtime floor; all technical checks still apply. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3, 2026, memory sunset-of-competition.md)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 12: Retire old manual documents as history: STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS v1.2, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, STORY_GRADING_RUBRIC.md, STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, NEDS scoring, character-attachment scoring, MASTER_RULES.md, DEPLOY.md, DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md, MIX_SPEC.md and MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md level tables, et_mix_assembly.py, ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001 Parts A, D, E. Decided: yes, all. (01 C1, 02 C4, Q5, Q6, 03 Q7, 07 C4, C6, 13 C9, 15 C3–C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 18: Repairs. Decided: text problems go back to the pipeline writer automatically (never an agent); a whole failed production gets one repair pass, then cold storage. "Hal rewrite" in PIPELINE-CANON becomes "pipeline writer rewrite". (01 C2, C3, 08 C7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 19: Restarting failed jobs. Decided: Claude or Orion may restart a job once with a written reason; a second restart needs you. (01 Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 20: One episode fails mid-series. Decided: the whole series holds and you're told; nothing in it publishes. (01 Q4, 09 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 24: Gemini's final read. Decided: report-only until it agrees with you on 9 of 10 series, then it must pass before a Direct publish. (01 Q2, 09 C2, Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 61: Series checks run per episode once built (decision 21); until then, record it as not fully enforced. (01 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 62: The Nov 7 Story Production Spec: only the Gemini read (report-only) is approved; the rest is replaced by this canon. (01 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] docs/STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS.md v1.2 (June 10) describes a manual flow: Marc fills the brief, pastes prompts into Claude chats, sends scripts to Hal on Telegram, grades every story out of 30 before publishing, and uses the Series Release Rule. Today's flow is automatic (dispatch → run-next → publish switch), Hal writes nothing, and the Series Release Rule is retired. Recommendation: this canon wins; mark v1.2 as history. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 18, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Repairs: Marc Ruling 1 (Jul 8) said failed stories go to cold storage with no repairs (app/api/cron/repair-queue/route.ts). Marc ruling Jul 9 allows one repair pass. PIPELINE-CANON Rule 1 (Oct 4) requires automatic send-back and retry with no human step. Recommendation: Rule 1 governs content fixes (automatic rewrite, retry limits in rule 45); the one-repair-pass rule still applies to whole production failures. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 18, Marc Nov 9, 2026] PIPELINE-CANON Rule 1 says Class B text fixes go to "Hal rewrite". Marc Nov 8 and AGENTS.md: no agent writes scripts; the pipeline writer does. Recommendation: replace "Hal rewrite" with "pipeline writer rewrite" in PIPELINE-CANON. Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 61, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Rule 3 says per-episode gates are the "intended shape … implementation is a separate track". Code still runs one production_jobs row per series (shared fate). Recommendation: record as not fully enforced (below), not a rule change.
  • C5. [RESOLVED: fact checked or done, Nov 9, 2026; see CANON-99 Part 2] Memory (Oct 16) says no cron drove run-next; vercel.json now has 4 runner crons, but production runs on EC2 (Caddy → PM2), not Vercel (chat "AWS EC2 setup"). Which scheduler is live is unverified. Recommendation: Orion confirms which runner is live and canon names it.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 19, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who may restart a failed job by hand (Claude, Orion, or only after Marc's word)? Suggested answer: Claude or Orion may re-queue once with a logged reason; a second re-queue needs Marc.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 24, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should the Gemini read move from "report only" to a gate? Suggested answer: keep report-only until it agrees with Marc on 9 of 10 series (Story Production Spec §9.2, still a draft).
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 62, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is the Story Production Spec (Nov 7 Claude Doc) approved or still a draft? Code cites "approved by Marc Nov 7" for the Gemini read only. Suggested answer: only the Gemini read (report-only) is approved; the rest stays draft.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 20, Marc Nov 9, 2026] What happens to a series when one episode lands in cold storage mid-production? Suggested answer: the whole series holds and Marc is told; no later episode starts.

Enforcement status

  • 1–6, 8–9, 11–13, 24–28, 40–45, 47–49 → enforced in code at the paths given.
  • 7 → not enforced (gate not built).
  • 10 → partly (sound effects were turned off for all stories Nov 1 until a professional library is in place).
  • 14 → enforced: lib/publishMode.ts, lib/directPublish.ts; current setting direct (atlas_settings, set Oct 11); publication hold released Oct 27.
  • 29–31 → partly: lib/dispatchGuards.ts and one job per series; per-episode lock not built.
  • 32 → script exists (scripts/series/continue-series.ts); rule pending.
  • 33–37, 51–56 → by agent practice, not code.
  • 46 → enforced: lib/workflowTransitions.ts failureDestinationForStory.
  • 57 → enforced in part: lib/story-gates.ts AUTHOR-WRITTEN-RELEASE-001.

body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: everything decided before a script is written — genres, authors, premise, hook, series type and length, series bible, cast and fact sheet, hook-first series, Pocket FM opt-in, series continuation, runtime targets in the brief, the brief itself. Does not cover: writing the script (CANON-03 The Writer); Belle intro/outro wording; sound, mixing, voices, covers, publishing and the player (their own CANON docs).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 8 MARC DECIDES: No story is written for an author who lacks a style model or a complete style sheet. The job stops and asks Marc.
  • Rule 19 MARC DECIDES: A colliding brief is bounced for rework, never retried automatically. Only Marc can let it through, by a recorded override with his name and…
  • Rule 20 MARC DECIDES: A premise near a known-adjacent cluster gets a warning but proceeds. Only Marc adds or retires a cluster.
  • Rule 28 MARC DECIDES: Preferred series lengths are 3, 5, 7 or 13 episodes. Any other length needs Marc's explicit approval.
  • Rule 30 MARC DECIDES: Long Pocket FM series (e.g. 30 episodes) are allowed when Marc orders them, planned in arcs of 10, with one big turn every 10 episodes.
  • Rule 31 MARC DECIDES: When Marc or Maya sets an episode count, the story has exactly that many episodes.
  • Rule 39 MARC DECIDES: Pocket FM–style writing is used only when Marc says "use the rules for Pocket FM type stories."
  • Rule 53 MARC DECIDES: After a series finale, the series is scored for character attachment (0–8); 5+ = recommend a new season to Marc. New seasons must raise stakes,…
  • Rule 54 MARC DECIDES: Adding episodes never re-plans, rewrites, re-titles, re-hides or re-voices episodes that already exist. New episodes are planned only for the…
  • Rule 63 MARC DECIDES: When Marc or Maya sets a per-episode length, each episode lands within ±20% of it.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. How a story starts

  1. Every story starts from four inputs: genre, series type (closed or ongoing), number of episodes in this batch, and style mode (standard drive-time, or Pocket FM). The requester sets them. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3, approved by Marc Nov 7, 2026; Claude Doc "Endless Tales — Story Production Spec")
  2. Planning comes before writing, in this order: hook, master premise, cast, fact sheet, series outline. No episode script is written until all five exist. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §2–§4; Marc Oct 29: "a whole-series plan before episode one … permanent", memory /projects/…/areas/story-pipeline.md)
  3. All story writing goes through the pipeline. No agent (Orion, Hal, Atlas, Claude in chat) writes or edits a script. Agents may draft plans (hook, premise, bible) for Marc. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "Agent rules (Marc, standing)"; PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY RULE, Defaults)
  4. Each step of planning has exactly one owner. No "Claude or Strategos." — Agreed (Story Production Spec §1)

B. Genres and authors

  1. The genre comes from the genres table. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3 input table)
  2. Each genre has exactly 3 ET pen-name authors. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "Data rules", canon index merged Nov 9)
  3. Every ET author has: one assigned narrator, one real author as a style model (style_reference), and a complete style sheet (authors.style_sheet) that includes an ending type. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY STYLE-001, Marc Nov 1, 2026; AGENTS.md data rules; memory story-pipeline.md Nov 1)
  4. MARC DECIDES No story is written for an author who lacks a style model or a complete style sheet. The job stops and asks Marc. — Agreed (STYLE-001)
  5. Each series is assigned one ET author. The writer follows that author's style sheet for every episode in the series. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.5)
  6. The style model governs voice only (rhythm, tone, word choice). Never copy the real author's text, plots, characters, settings or titles. — Agreed (STYLE-001 copyright note)
  7. Each author's narrator is fixed. The brief names the author; the narrator follows from the author, never chosen per story. — Agreed (STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT v2.4 "Narrator lookup table"; STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2 Part 2)

C. The hook (planned first)

  1. The hook is written first. It is the first spoken line of Episode 1. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.1; hook-first ads decision Nov 4, project doc claude/hook-first-ads-2026-11-04.md)
  2. The hook is a shocking situation in under 15 words, in first person when possible, that names an engine (a wish or a fear) a listener understands in one hearing. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.1; HOOK-FIRST-001, Marc ruling Jul 24 per lib/hookGate.ts) — see Conflict C2
  3. The hook's words work as ad copy with no rewrite. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.1)

D. Master premise and uniqueness

  1. One master premise paragraph flows from the hook. It holds the engine, the lead's want, wound and secret, the villain, the central question, and (closed series) the shape of the ending. Every later step is checked against it. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.2)
  2. The brief's premise is 2–5 sentences and leads with the inciting situation (the first sentence is the hook). — Agreed (STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2 Part 3; PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001 core-hook rule)
  3. No new brief goes to script writing if its premise is substantially similar to any story that is published, ready_for_review, repair_queue or approved_ready. "Substantially similar" = same core hook (≥0.6 overlap) AND same central situation (≥0.5 overlap). Same genre or setting alone is fine. — Agreed (governance/PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001.md, Marc ruling Jul 18, 2026)
  4. Cold-storage premises are free to reuse. — Agreed (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001)
  5. MARC DECIDES A colliding brief is bounced for rework, never retried automatically. Only Marc can let it through, by a recorded override with his name and reason. Agents never self-approve. — Agreed (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001 "Override procedure")
  6. MARC DECIDES A premise near a known-adjacent cluster gets a warning but proceeds. Only Marc adds or retires a cluster. — Agreed (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001 amendment, Jul 18)
  7. Episodes of the same series never collide with each other. — Agreed (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001 "Sibling exclusion")
  8. Episodes in a series never reuse the same central object, discovery or secret device (no second hidden clock, no second note inside something). — Agreed (Marc Oct 28, memory story-pipeline.md; EPISODE-VARIETY-001 in writer prompt)
  9. Character names are not reused from the last 10 series, and no two main characters have names that sound alike. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §4.1; Pocket FM rules Nov 4)
  10. Surnames are not reused across the catalog without a deliberate reason. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY NAMES-001, Aug 29) — rule 23 is the newer, stricter version
  11. The planner gets a list of recent premises, settings and names to avoid (today: developer/land deed/erased records; the ex who returns or buys the business; small Carolina water town, bridge or ferry; names Brennan, Claire, Cole, Merritt, Bennett, Vivian, Harlow). — Proposed (claude/cover-and-theme-repetition-2026-11-04.md found 9 deed/developer series; Marc deferred a general check until after Stabilization Week; nothing decided since)

E. Series types and lengths

  1. Endless Tales is series-first. A standalone needs a stated purpose: discovery, onboarding, testing, or variety. — Agreed (ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 Part V)
  2. A series is either Closed (a real ending in the last episode) or Ongoing (built in seasons). — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3)
  3. MARC DECIDES Preferred series lengths are 3, 5, 7 or 13 episodes. Any other length needs Marc's explicit approval. — Agreed (ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 Part V; code SERIES_EPISODE_COUNTS in lib/series/continue-plan.ts)
  4. New standard series are 5 or 7 episodes (romance, heartwarming, western, thriller, sci-fi). The old 3-episode queue is retired. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1, memory story-pipeline.md) — see Q1
  5. MARC DECIDES Long Pocket FM series (e.g. 30 episodes) are allowed when Marc orders them, planned in arcs of 10, with one big turn every 10 episodes. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3 and Nov 5, memory altar-romance-series.md; Pocket FM rules; Story Production Spec §7)
  6. MARC DECIDES When Marc or Maya sets an episode count, the story has exactly that many episodes. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY LENGTH-001)
  7. Every episode header carries the same planned total for the season in production. A mismatch (Rerouted EP1 "5", EP2–3 "7") is a failure. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §7)
  8. A closed series leaves at most one open thread at its end (one named villain may escape for a sequel when the brief asks). "The Man I Left at the Altar" may leave three. — Agreed (SERIES-NEMESIS-001, Marc Oct 30; Altar exception Nov 3, lib/seriesSequel.ts; Story Production Spec §5)
  9. An ongoing series: each season closes its own arc and leaves exactly one bigger question open. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.3, §7)

F. Hook-first series

  1. A hook-first ad series starts from a tested ad hook. The hook is the first spoken line of Episode 1. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON HOOK-SERIES RULE, Nov 5)
  2. Each hook series launches as a 7-episode "Season 1" with threads left open. All 7 episodes publish together. — Agreed (HOOK-SERIES RULE; memory hook-series.md Nov 5 and Nov 8)
  3. Winners are extended to 20–30 episodes, judged by cost per trial and the share of trial users who reach Episode 3 or later. — Agreed (HOOK-SERIES RULE) — the numbers that make a "winner" are not set; see Q3
  4. The five Nov 2026 hook series: The Widow Who Watched, Second Rise, Weekend Wife in Miami (Pocket FM rules); Rerouted, Don't Go Home (standard rules). Though made for ads, they are real library stories. — Agreed (HOOK-SERIES RULE; memory hook-series.md Nov 8)

G. Pocket FM style (opt-in)

  1. MARC DECIDES Pocket FM–style writing is used only when Marc says "use the rules for Pocket FM type stories." — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE, Nov 5; memory story-pipeline.md Nov 4)
  2. It sits on top of every normal pipeline rule. When they conflict, the pipeline rule wins. — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE)
  3. A Pocket FM series names one engine in its plan (secret fortune, revenge, contract marriage, secret child, enemies to lovers, the cold one thaws, rags to riches, forbidden love), not the engine of any of the last 3 series. — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE; project doc claude/pocket-fm-style-rules.md)
  4. Pocket FM cast: a lead wronged in Episode 1, a clear villain, a love interest with a secret, names not used in the last 10 series. — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE)
  5. Pocket FM episodes run 12–15 minutes (2,000–2,400 spoken words). — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE; Pocket FM rules text sent to Orion Nov 4)

H. Series bible, cast and fact sheet

  1. Every series has a written series bible before any episode script. The bible holds the cast, timeline, central conflict and finale direction. — Agreed (Marc Oct 29 whole-series plan; PIPELINE-CANON SERIES-CONTINUATION Defaults) — code checks only that series.description is not empty (SERIES-BIBLE-GATE-001)
  2. The series design states: the central question (one sentence), the protagonist's arc, how stakes rise each episode, the type of finale resolution, and one specific cliffhanger per non-final episode. A series without its cliffhanger chain is not ready to produce. — Agreed (ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 Part V; STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE Part 6)
  3. The series outline fixes every character's one speaker label and full name, the story threads, and the one episode where each thread is resolved. Every episode writer gets the outline. — Agreed (SERIES-OUTLINE-001, Marc Oct 29 "permanent for all future stories"; lib/seriesOutline.ts)
  4. Cast: one lead to root for (wronged or underestimated in Episode 1), one clear villain, one ally or love interest with a secret. Each main character has a want, a wound, a secret, an age, a gender, an accent and one line of voice description. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §4.1)
  5. Long series introduce a new character every few episodes, each bringing a new problem. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §4.1)
  6. A fact sheet is written with the cast: who is related to whom, whose contact is whose, jobs, places, who is dead or missing. Writers get it as hard rules. New seasons add to it; nothing is deleted without a story reason. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §4.2; SERIES-FACTS-001, Marc Nov 7)
  7. A recurring hero keeps his exact name, speaker label and voice across series (Nick Brennan, label NICK). — Agreed (Marc Oct 27–28, memory story-pipeline.md)
  8. In a short series (6 episodes or fewer), every episode after Episode 1 shares at least one speaking character with Episode 1 and with the episode before it. — In force (code) (SERIES-CAST-CONTINUITY-001, lib/scriptReadiness.ts)
  9. The planned brief gets a Next Episode Desire Score (NEDS). Below 7 = revise the brief before writing. — Agreed (ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 Part VII; STAGE2 r37) — see Q5
  10. MARC DECIDES After a series finale, the series is scored for character attachment (0–8); 5+ = recommend a new season to Marc. New seasons must raise stakes, grow the lead and add one major new element. — Agreed (ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 Part IX) — see Q6

I. Adding episodes and new seasons

  1. MARC DECIDES Adding episodes never re-plans, rewrites, re-titles, re-hides or re-voices episodes that already exist. New episodes are planned only for the missing numbers, from the full scripts of the existing ones, with scripts/series/continue-series.ts: dry run first, Marc approves the plan, then save. — Proposed (PIPELINE-CANON SERIES-CONTINUATION RULE is PENDING Marc sign-off; code SERIES-CONTINUE-001 exists)
  2. The whole-series planner (/api/v2/series-package) must never run on a series that already has episodes. — Proposed (same pending rule; Nov 9 near-overwrite of a live Episode 1)
  3. Published episodes are frozen. A new season never rewrites, re-voices or re-renders them. — Agreed (PHASED-SERIES-001, Marc Nov 6; Story Production Spec §7)
  4. Before writing a new season, the writer reads the master premise, the fact sheet, all season outlines so far, and the full text of the last 3 published episodes. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §7)
  5. Each season has its own outline: its arc, what it resolves, and the one bigger question it opens. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §7)
  6. A real series bible is written before any new episode script of a continued series. — Proposed (SERIES-CONTINUATION Defaults, pending)

J. Runtime targets in the brief

  1. Series episodes target 12–18 minutes. 20–25 minutes is only for standalones, finales and episodes that earn it. — Agreed (STAGE2 v2.3; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC v1.5; Marc Oct 26 option 2, memory story-pipeline.md)
  2. Every episode of a series is about the same length. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.3)
  3. A brief may not ask for less than 12 minutes. Code refuses briefs of 10.8 minutes or less because they can never pass both the floor and the ±10% check. — In force (code) (briefRuntimeImpossible, lib/scriptReadiness.ts)
  4. MARC DECIDES When Marc or Maya sets a per-episode length, each episode lands within ±20% of it. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY LENGTH-002) — see Conflict C5
  5. Author-written series (Sunset of Competition) are exempt from the runtime floor; the finale stays at its written length. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3, memory sunset-of-competition.md)

K. The brief

  1. A brief contains: type (standalone/series), series name, episode number, total episodes, finale yes/no, author, genre, premise, setting, runtime, and (Episode 2+) a summary of the previous episode and its cliffhanger. — Agreed (STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, approved June 10)
  2. The brief template is rewritten to match today's rules: the four inputs (rule 1), hook, master premise, cast, fact sheet, outline; and the stale items in Conflict C4 are removed. — Proposed (template still carries retired rules)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 3: Hook length. The rules say 15 words; the code passes up to 30. Decided: 15 words, blocking, for every new Episode 1. The 5 live hooks keep their wording. (02 C2, 03 C2, 08 C1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 4: Episode length. Decided: standalones within ±10% of target; series episodes between the 12.5-minute floor and 1.35 × the brief; speaking rate 160 words per minute everywhere. Publish code uses the same numbers (today it only allows 15–20 minutes). (02 C5, 03 C3, 08 C2, 09 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 5: Series lengths. Decided: 5, 7 or 13 episodes, or any length you order (like Altar's 30). 3-episode series only when you ask. (02 C3, Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 9: Endings. Decided: about 1 in 5 standalones may end open; a series finale always answers its central question; one escaped villain is allowed; Belle never teases a sequel. (02 C6, 03 C8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 12: Retire old manual documents as history: STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS v1.2, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, STORY_GRADING_RUBRIC.md, STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, NEDS scoring, character-attachment scoring, MASTER_RULES.md, DEPLOY.md, DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md, MIX_SPEC.md and MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md level tables, et_mix_assembly.py, ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001 Parts A, D, E. Decided: yes, all. (01 C1, 02 C4, Q5, Q6, 03 Q7, 07 C4, C6, 13 C9, 15 C3–C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 13: Author roster. Decided: the database authors table is the only roster; remove the lists in the Bible and the writer prompt. (02 C1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 16: Avoid-list of recent premises, places and names. Decided: build it now, as a warning. (02 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 17: Series bible for a continued series. Decided: the pipeline writes it; you approve it only for series running in ads. (02 Q7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 63: Each series carries its own "style" setting (standard or Pocket FM). The canon list of Pocket FM series is examples only. (02 C7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 64: Standalone single stories stay allowed. "No 1-episode stories live" means no series showing only some of its episodes. (02 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 65: A hook series is a "winner" when its cost per trial is at or under the $26–31 target and at least 40% of its trial users reach Episode 3. (02 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 133: Emotions in the series plan. For each episode the plan names one main emotion and up to two supporting ones from the CANON-03 palette, starting from its genre's set (thriller or mystery: worry, fear, glee; romance: love and warmth, longing, jealousy, hope; horror: dread, fear, relief; family or grief drama: grief, love and warmth, hope; revenge: hate, bad feeling at a villain win, glee; betrayal or con: betrayal, worry, glee; comedy or light drama: amusement, warmth, relief; science fiction or adventure: awe, worry, glee). Liking the protagonist is required in every story; feelings change across a series. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026, CANON-99 item 133)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 13, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Author roster: ET_Story_Rules_v3_2 lists 10 authors; STAGE2 v2.4 lists 31; STYLE-001 (Nov 1) says 50 active authors; AGENTS.md says exactly 3 per genre. Recommendation: the database authors table is the roster; delete the static tables from the Bible and STAGE2 prompt. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 3, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Hook length: Spec §3.1 and HOOK-FIRST-001 say under 15 words; the 5 approved ad hooks (Nov 4) run up to 21 words ("15–25 word hook" in the Nov 5 chat summary); lib/hookGate.ts passes a hook up to word 30 (comment still says 15). Recommendation: 15 words for all new Episode 1s (newest, Nov 7); leave the 5 live hooks as they are; fix the code to 15. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 5, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Series lengths: Bible says 3/5/7/13; Marc Nov 1 chose 5 and 7 for new standard series; hook series are 7; Altar is 30. Recommendation: allowed lengths = 5, 7, 13, plus any length Marc orders; 3 only on Marc's word. Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2 is stale: it still cites the retired Series Release Rule, 3–6 anchor SFX (Marc removed the cap Oct 31), a 24-word description (Marc Nov 5: fills two card lines), "Belle never mentions the author" (BELLE-004 says Episode 1 names the author), a 10-minute runtime option (below the 12.5-minute floor), and PIPELINE_MODE transition/full. Recommendation: retire the template and replace it per rule 66.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 4, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Length tolerance: LENGTH-002 says ±20% of target; RUNTIME-GATE-001 (code) says ±10% on the final mix; the series ceiling is brief × 1.35. Recommendation: one rule — standalone ±10%, series between the 12.5-minute floor and brief × 1.35. Marc decides.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 9, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Open threads: ENDING-001 and Bible Part XVII say a finale resolves all major threads and never teases a sequel; SERIES-NEMESIS-001 (Oct 30) allows one escaped villain, Altar three. Recommendation: newer rule 33 wins; the sequel thread is never teased by Belle.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 63, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Pocket FM list: PIPELINE-CANON names only Widow, Second Rise and Weekend Wife as Pocket FM; Marc also chose Pocket FM for "The Man I Left at the Altar" (Nov 3) and a second 30-episode series (Nov 5). Recommendation: keep a per-series style_mode field; the canon list is examples only.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 5, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Are 3-episode series still allowed for new work? Suggested answer: only when you ask for one.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 64, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Does "no 1-episode stories live" (Nov 8) also ban standalone single stories, or only a series showing one episode? Suggested answer: only the series case; standalones stay allowed for discovery and tests.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 65, Marc Nov 9, 2026] What numbers make a hook series a "winner" to extend to 20–30 episodes? Suggested answer: cost per trial at or under the $26–31 CAC target band and at least 40% of trial users reaching Episode 3.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 16, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should the avoid-list of recent premises, settings and names (rule 25) be built now? Suggested answer: yes, now that Stabilization Week is over; warning only, like known-adjacent clusters.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] NEDS (rule 52): the scorers named in the Bible (Hal, Vega) no longer do this job, and no code checks it. Keep it? Suggested answer: drop NEDS; the Story Clarity check and Gemini's script read replace it.
  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Character-attachment scoring after each finale (rule 53): keep? Suggested answer: replace with listener data (completion rate, Episode 3 reach) in the weekly report.
  • Q7. [RESOLVED by decision 17, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who writes the series bible for a continued series, and does Marc approve every one? Suggested answer: the pipeline writer drafts it; Marc approves only for series in active ads.

Enforcement status

  • Rule 1–2, 12–15, 47, 57–58 → not enforced yet (Spec "planning package" is phase 3 of the rollout).
  • Rule 3 → not enforced in code; agent rule only.
  • Rules 7–8 → enforced (AUTHOR-STYLE-001, AUTHOR-STYLE-SHEET-001; authors table).
  • Rule 13 → partially: lib/hookGate.ts allows 30 words.
  • Rules 17–21 → enforced: lib/premiseGate.ts, lib/premiseIndex.ts, at all four Stage 2 entrances.
  • Rule 22 → prompt only (EPISODE-VARIETY-001 in run-next writer prompt); no check.
  • Rule 23 → not enforced; lib/story/namePalette.ts suggests names but does not check the last 10 series.
  • Rules 28, 31–32 → partially: continue-plan uses 3/5/7/13; no header-total check found.
  • Rule 33 → enforced in package validator (lib/seriesSequel.ts nemesisOpenThreadLimit).
  • Rule 44 → partially: SERIES-BIBLE-GATE-001 only checks series.description is not empty (app/api/v2/generate-script/route.ts, series-package/generate-scripts).
  • Rule 46 → enforced: lib/seriesOutline.ts (on by default).
  • Rule 49 → enforced: lib/seriesFacts.ts (SERIES-FACTS-001).
  • Rule 51 → enforced: lib/scriptReadiness.ts checkSeriesCastContinuity (dispatcher).
  • Rule 52–53 → not enforced (no NEDS code).
  • Rule 54–55 → tool exists (scripts/series/continue-series.ts); series-package has no guard against existing series.
  • Rule 56 → enforced: PHASED-SERIES-001 in run-next.
  • Rule 62 → enforced: briefRuntimeImpossible.

title: CANON-03 — The Writer (Script Rules)
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: everything the pipeline script writer must do — who may write, maps before drafting, hook and opening, structure, cliffhangers and endings, clarity, script format, speaker labels, text the voices will speak, length, and the writer's own checks. Does not cover: planning and briefs (CANON-02); Belle intro/outro wording (Belle CANON doc); sound effects, mixing, voices, covers, publishing and the player (their own CANON docs).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 2 MARC DECIDES: Author-written series (today only The Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten or regenerated. On a failed check the pipeline stops and reports;…
  • Rule 58 MARC DECIDES: NARRATIVE_VOICE is declared (first_person, third_limited, third_omniscient) and held on every narrator line. second_person needs Marc's approval.
  • Rule 59 MARC DECIDES: NARRATOR_IS_CHARACTER: true needs Marc's approval and a non-platform voice.
  • Rule 90 MARC DECIDES: Gemini reads the scripts before voicing (continuity, easy listening, logic, promise, credibility) and lists exact fixes. Report-only until Marc…
  • Decision 133 MARC DECIDES: The emotion check is report-only until Marc reviews three stories with it; then Marc decides whether it blocks.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Who writes

  1. Only the pipeline writer writes or edits scripts. No agent (Orion, Hal, Atlas, Claude in chat) writes or edits a script, even to fix one line. A failed check sends the script back to the pipeline writer. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "All story writing goes through the pipeline; no agent writes or edits scripts"; PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY RULE Defaults, Nov 8)
  2. MARC DECIDES Author-written series (today only The Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten or regenerated. On a failed check the pipeline stops and reports; only mechanical edits Marc approves are made. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3, memory /projects/…/areas/sunset-of-competition.md)
  3. The writer writes from the author's database record and style sheet every time, never from memory. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY STYLE-001, Nov 1)
  4. Lines using Claude's stock phrases ("a testament to", "something shifted", "the silence stretched", "a breath she didn't know she was holding" and the rest of the list) are sent back for a rewrite in the author's voice. — Agreed (STYLE-001; list in lib/authorStyle.ts STOCK_PHRASES)
  5. When a check fails, the writer gets the exact problem and the exact lines, and rewrites — at most 2 rewrites per episode. After that the story stops with one plain reason. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §1 and §5, approved Nov 7)
  6. A rewrite revises the previous draft (keeps what works); it does not start over. — In force (code) (WRITER-REVISE-001, lib/scriptReadiness.ts)
  7. Every rewritten script goes back through all script checks before voicing. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §8.1 gap 2)

B. Before drafting

  1. The writer first makes a Story Resolution Map with six parts: main hook/problem, why the solution seems hard, middle movement, final solution (stated specifically), why the ending is earned, and how this story differs from recent ones. It goes in a comment block (<!-- … -->) that is removed before audio. — Agreed (STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT v2.3, approved June 10)
  2. The map fails if: the hook is generic, the difficulty is not stated, the middle does not shape the ending, the solution could happen in minute two, or "earned" is explained with vague words like "because of the journey." — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 decision 69; was: docs/STORY_RESOLUTION_MAP_RULES.md, Marc-owned doctrine with no approval record)
  3. Production notes live only in the map comment block or the header. Nothing else above or inside the story body. — Proposed (the cover maker read the map block and drew maps on ~30 covers, Nov 4)
  4. Write the cliffhanger first; write or revise the opening after the rest of the episode. — Agreed (STAGE2 r38, r42)
  5. Variety: do not lean on worn shapes — "the trusted authority was the villain", "the narrator was dead all along", "the monster was grief", last-minute villain confession, final newspaper/radio/voicemail reveal. — Agreed (STAGE2 map "Variety guardrail") with the list Proposed (docs/CLAUDE_STORY_ARCHITECTURE_BIBLE.md)

C. Hook and opening

  1. The first spoken story line after Belle is a hook in under 15 words. For a hook-first series, Episode 1's first line is the approved hook, word for word. — Agreed (HOOK-FIRST-001, Marc Jul 24; Story Production Spec §3.1 and §5; memory profile "hook within 15 words")
  2. Every episode opens with tension, a question or stakes — never weather, waking up, or backstory. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY HOOK-001; STAGE2 r8)
  3. Within 60 seconds the listener knows who the main character is, where we are, and what is happening. The hook comes from clarity, not confusion. — Agreed (STAGE2 v2.3 clarity rule; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC v1.5)
  4. By minute 3 (about 480 spoken words) the listener knows: who we follow, what is happening, what they want or fear, why it matters, and what we are listening to find out. — Agreed (STAGE2 r42 Early Investment Rule; STORY-CLARITY check 2, Nov 8)
  5. Episode 2 and later: within the first 30 seconds after Belle's intro, one line says where things stand. — Agreed (STORY-CLARITY check 6; Story Production Spec §3.4)
  6. Each episode starts within one line of where the last one ended. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.3)
  7. Pocket FM mode only: the lead is wronged within the first 2 minutes of Episode 1, and something big happens every 2–3 minutes. — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE, Nov 5)

D. Structure

  1. Something changes every 3–4 minutes (about 480–640 spoken words): a reveal, reversal, new threat, or decision with consequences. No scene ends in the same state of knowledge it began. Stories of 20+ minutes have a midpoint reversal. — Agreed (STAGE2 r33 Turn Rule)
  2. Each episode has one small conflict that opens and closes inside it, one high point, and a hard ending. Episodes 2 and 3 each raise the stakes again. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.3)
  3. Every scene moves the goal, the obstacle, or a relationship forward. Two or more scenes that don't = fail. — Agreed (STORY-CLARITY check 5)
  4. At least one major development from each episode is felt in the next. Characters are never reset. — Agreed (STAGE2 r41)
  5. Do not replay earlier scenes except as brief context. Do not reuse an earlier episode's central object, discovery or secret device. — Agreed (Marc Oct 28; EPISODE-VARIETY-001 in writer prompt)
  6. After every scene break: name the character within the first narrator lines, make the scene's stakes clear within 30 seconds, and mark the new place or time. — Agreed (STAGE2 r40)
  7. No critical fact lives in one throwaway line. Important reveals get one callback. — Agreed (STAGE2 r40; Bible Part XV)
  8. Each scene grounds its place with two concrete sensory details in its first three narrator lines. — Agreed (STAGE2 r34, June) — see Conflict C7
  9. Action stories (style "action"): move faster, describe less, keep it easy to follow by ear. — Agreed (Marc Oct 29, memory story-pipeline.md; SERIES-STYLE-ACTION-001, lib/seriesStyle.ts)
  10. Believable: every event and conclusion follows from what the story has set up, judged by the story's own rules. No character knows something the story never told them. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4 and §6.3; Bible Part XI)
  11. A character never contradicts their own instruction or plan within a scene. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4, Rerouted EP2)
  12. Stakes may grow, but the type of threat stays inside what the premise set up (no small-town fraud turning into a global conspiracy without setup). — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 decision 69; was: CLAUDE_STORY_ARCHITECTURE_BIBLE "Escalation Ceiling", no approval record)
  13. Protagonists are good at something; the problem exceeds their skill. — Agreed (Bible Part VIII)
  14. Story first. Never stop to teach a lesson; no character speaks for the author. The last narrator line is a concrete image or action, never "She had learned that…", "He understood now that…", "The truth was that…". — Agreed (Bible Entertainment First Rule; STAGE2 r39)

E. Cliffhangers and endings

  1. Every non-final episode ends on a hard cliffhanger: a revelation, danger, betrayal, discovery, or irreversible decision. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY CLIFFHANGER-001; STAGE2 r38; memory profile "hard cliffhangers")
  2. The cliffhanger must be writable as a specific question the next episode answers. Banned: "things will get worse", the same kind of danger again, a cliff solved in the next episode's first 60 seconds, an ominous stranger, "little did she know", weather or breakdowns as stakes, "to be continued". — Agreed (STAGE2 r16, r38)
  3. A non-final episode resolves its own episode problem first, then strengthens the series question. — Agreed (STAGE2 map hard rules)
  4. Pocket FM mode: end at the moment that hurts most. — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE)
  5. The last episode of a season in an ongoing series ends on a hard cliffhanger; finale rules do not apply to it. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §7)
  6. A closed series' finale answers the central question and resolves all major threads, with at most the one sequel thread its plan allows. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY ENDING-001; Story Production Spec §3.3; SERIES-NEMESIS-001)
  7. A standalone resolves its main conflict completely, shows the protagonist's moment of recognition, and its last narrator line feels conclusive. — Agreed (Bible r31 and Standalone Completion Standard, June 10)
  8. The climax happens on stage, the protagonist's own action decides it, and the ending never comes from coincidence, an offscreen rescue, a convenient confession, or a rule introduced at the end. — Agreed (STAGE2 map hard rules) with the flags In force (code) (run-next writer prompt "Ending hard rules")
  9. Open endings (the main question left hanging) are allowed only about 1 story in 5, only for authors whose style sheet calls for it, and only when built up to. — Agreed (STYLE-001 / ENDING-OPEN-001, Marc Nov 1) — see Conflict C8

F. Story clarity (drive-time listening)

  1. Every episode passes the seven-part clarity check before any voicing: three-sentence test, goal clear by minute 3, cast limit, no unexplained insider words, every scene has a purpose, recap line (Episode 2+), easy to follow by ear. A fail sends it back to the writer with the lines quoted. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY RULE, Nov 8)
  2. Cast limit, not counting Belle: at most 4 named speaking characters for a standalone or a series of 3 episodes or fewer; at most 6 for longer series; at most 2 new named characters per episode after Episode 1. — Agreed (STORY-CLARITY check 3) — see Conflict C6
  3. At most 3 voices in one scene. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4, Nov 7; Pocket FM rules)
  4. Acronyms, trade words, local places and organizations are explained in plain words the first time, or cut. — Agreed (STORY-CLARITY check 4)
  5. The narrator introduces every new character before or right after their first line, and names speakers often. — Agreed (STAGE2 "The Narrator"; Story Production Spec §3.4)
  6. Nothing exists only visually: if it matters, someone says it. — Agreed (Bible r9; Story Production Spec §3.4)
  7. Short sentences, plain modern words, big feelings said out loud (about a 10th-grade reading level). — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC v1.5)
  8. No two main characters have names that sound alike. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4)
  9. The story never points to its own events by episode or chapter number ("in episode two", "next episode"). Use "earlier", "that night at the lake", "soon". Only Belle says episode numbers. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §3.4) — see Q3
  10. Dialogue turns are 1–3 sentences; no speech over 5 sentences without a break. Narrator passages over 4 sentences are broken up. — Agreed (STAGE2 "Dialogue Turn Length", "The Narrator")

G. Script format

  1. Script order: header fields, CHARACTER GUIDE, BELLE B intro, [START AUDIO DRAMA SCRIPT], story body, BELLE B OUTRO. The resolution-map comment block may sit at the very top. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §5) — see Conflict C1
  2. Header fields: TITLE, SERIES, EPISODE, EPISODE_TITLE, SERIES_TOTAL_EPISODES, SERIES_IS_FINALE, AUTHOR, GENRE, DESCRIPTION, NARRATOR, ANNOUNCER: Belle B, NARRATIVE_VOICE, NARRATOR_IS_CHARACTER, SUNO PROMPT. — Agreed (Bible Part XII; STAGE2 header block)
  3. TITLE: 1–5 words, 28 characters or fewer, never "Episode N" or the series title. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §5)
  4. DESCRIPTION (story card): fits two card lines (at most 100 characters), present tense only, teases a question, never reveals the twist or outcome. — Agreed (Marc Nov 5 "fills two lines"; DESC-TENSE-001 Marc Oct 29; DESC-100-CHAR-001) — see Conflict C4
  5. NARRATOR header is the assigned narrator's voice name from the author's pairing, never a story character. — Agreed (STAGE2 lookup table) and In force (code) (HAL-SCRIPT-001; run-next narrator check)
  6. MARC DECIDES NARRATIVE_VOICE is declared (first_person, third_limited, third_omniscient) and held on every narrator line. second_person needs Marc's approval. — Agreed (Bible r22, r27)
  7. MARC DECIDES NARRATOR_IS_CHARACTER: true needs Marc's approval and a non-platform voice. — Agreed (Bible Part XIII)
  8. CHARACTER GUIDE lists every speaking character, starting with the exact speaker label, then age, gender, accent and a personality/tone note. — Agreed (STAGE2 "Character Guide"; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC v1.5) and In force (code) (CAST-GUIDE-001)
  9. Every spoken line in the body starts with a speaker label in CAPITAL LETTERS, exactly as in the guide, using the character's full canonical name from the series cast. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §5) and In force (code) (HAL-SCRIPT-002, SCRIPT-LABELS-001)
  10. A character has one label however they are addressed (John Smith, Mr. Smith, John → one label, one voice). — Agreed (CHARACTER-NAMES-001, Marc Oct 30)
  11. Belle never appears as a character; no character is cast with a platform voice. — Agreed (Bible r29)
  12. [SFX: …], [BEAT], [PAUSE:N], [MUSIC:OUT]/[MUSIC:IN] each sit on their own line, never inside a spoken line. — Agreed (Bible r4, r6; STAGE2)
  13. One character never speaks two lines in a row. Between them goes a NARRATOR line, a [BEAT], a [PAUSE], or another character's line. — Agreed (Dialogue Separation Rule, Marc June 10) — see Conflict C10
  14. Youngest speaking character is 14; a teen character must sound their age. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY CONTENT-002)
  15. Content: late-night cable standard. No graphic violence or explicit sex (romance heat through tension and kisses only). — Agreed (Bible r13; Pocket FM rules)
  16. Banned words: "fuck" and derivatives, "cunt", racial and other slurs of that weight. "Shit", "damn", "hell" are allowed. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY LANGUAGE-001; list awaits Marc's expansion)
  17. "Endless Tales presents" is never written anywhere. — Agreed (CANON_REGISTRY CONTENT-001)

H. Text the voices will speak

Every character in a spoken line is sent to the voice. Anything that is not a word to be said aloud must not be there.

  1. Write every number as words in every spoken line: times, ages, money, counts, addresses, codes, plates, serial numbers ("transaction zero zero one", "three twelve in the morning", "lane three"). This includes Belle lines and titles. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §5, Nov 7; memory profile "numbers spelled out") and In force (code) (numeral pre-TTS scan blocks, lib/numeralPreTtsScan.ts; simple numbers auto-spelled, lib/spokenNumerals.ts) — see Conflict C5
  2. A code with a separator is written the way it is said: "four four seven dash zero zero one nine". — Proposed (QC-SPOKEN-DASH-001 already accepts the spoken "dash", lib/transcriptQC.ts, Oct 26)
  3. No parentheses or stage directions in a spoken line: no "(quietly)", "(sighs)", "(to himself)". Tone goes in a NARRATOR line before the dialogue. — Agreed (Bible r5; STAGE2) and In force (code) (generate-voices refuses inline cues before voicing, findInlineProductionCues)
  4. A character's line holds only the words that character says aloud. Actions, reactions, movement and thoughts go under NARRATOR. — Agreed (STAGE2 "convey tone through narrator lines") and In force (code) (NARRATION-PRESENCE-001 blocks scripts with narration under character labels or no NARRATOR lines)
  5. A sound cue is never written as a speaker label ("SFX:", "SFX-001:"); the voice would read it aloud. Only [SFX: short description] on its own line. — In force (code) (SCRIPT-LABELS-001 blocks and auto-fixes, lib/scriptLabels.ts)
  6. A scene break is a blank line or a cue, never a spoken line like "NARRATOR: ---" or "NARRATOR: *". — Agreed (WORDLESS-LINE-001, Marc GO Sep 28: "---" was voiced as random words in Origin 2.0 EP03; code turns such lines into a 1.5-second pause)
  7. Finish each sentence on its own line. Never split one sentence across two lines with a dash at the end of the first. For a character who is cut off, end the line with "…". — Proposed (TRAILING-DASH-001, Marc Nov 7: line-final dashes garbled in Sunset Ep 8; the voice step now turns a final dash into "…", lib/speakableText.ts, but scripts still carry them — 59 in Sunset alone)
  8. No markdown in spoken lines: no asterisks, underscores, # headings, bold or italics. — Proposed (the voice step strips them, generate-voices generateVoiceLine; the writer should not rely on that)
  9. Never write the same line twice in a row, by the same or another speaker, unless the repeat is the point of the scene. A check flags any exact repeated spoken line in an episode. — Proposed (Sunset: "many characters spoke their lines twice", repeats cut by hand from the audio, memory sunset-of-competition.md; Marc's lead "double lines")
  10. Header lines, the CHARACTER GUIDE and anything before [START AUDIO DRAMA SCRIPT] (except the Belle intro) are never voiced. Nothing meant for the listener goes there. — In force (code) (lib/scriptLineIndex.ts parser)
  11. [LISTENER_NAME] never appears in the story body. — Proposed (the voice step replaces a stray token with "friend", generate-voices; Belle rules cover where the token may appear)
  12. Dialogue lines have at least 5 words, and never start with a one-word sentence ("Yes. He retired…"). — In force (code, prompt only) (HAL-SCRIPT-006, HAL-SCRIPT-007 in run-next standalone prompt; the Spec audit found the check is never called) — see Q4 and Conflict C10

I. Length

  1. Speaking rate for all estimates is 160 words per minute. — Proposed (Story Production Spec §8.2 conflict 7 resolution; code uses 160) — see Conflict C3
  2. A series episode must estimate at least 12.5 minutes before any voicing: 2,000 spoken words, Belle lines included. — Agreed (Marc Oct 26 "option 2", memory story-pipeline.md; Story Production Spec §5) and In force (code) (SCRIPT-RUNTIME-PREFLIGHT-001, lib/scriptRuntimeEstimate.ts)
  3. A series episode may not exceed the brief's length × 1.35 (at 160 wpm). — Agreed (Story Production Spec §5) and In force (code) (SERIES-RUNTIME-MAX-001)
  4. The writer aims at the brief length × 160 spoken words, within ±10%. — In force (code) (seriesSpokenWordTarget, WRITER-PROMPT-GATES-001)
  5. A standalone script estimates within ±15% of its brief before voicing; the finished mix must land within ±10%. — In force (code) (lib/scriptReadiness.ts RUNTIME-BRIEF; RUNTIME-GATE-001, lib/runtimeGate.ts)
  6. Pocket FM episodes: 12–15 minutes (2,000–2,400 spoken words). — Agreed (POCKET-FM-STYLE RULE)
  7. Length comes from real scenes and beats, never padding. — In force (code) (writer rewrite feedback, lib/scriptReadiness.ts)

J. Checks on the writer's work before voicing

  1. Writer self-check (free, every draft): card copy, narrator header, narration presence, numbers, labels, sound-cue format, stock phrases, runtime floor and ceiling, Belle line present, character guide. — In force (code) (SCRIPT-READINESS-001, WRITER-SELF-CHECK-001)
  2. MARC DECIDES Gemini reads the scripts before voicing (continuity, easy listening, logic, promise, credibility) and lists exact fixes. Report-only until Marc gives it power. — Agreed (Story Production Spec §6.3 and §9.2, Nov 7) and In force (code, report-only) (GEMINI-STORY-READ-001)
  3. The whole series is read together for contradictions (an event resolved twice, a character under two names, the dead returning), and every "my sister / my cousin" line is checked against the fact sheet. A failure rewrites that episode and every later one, at most 2 times. — Agreed (Marc Oct 29 "permanent"; SERIES-FACTS-001 Nov 7) and In force (code) (SERIES-CONTINUITY-001, SERIES-FACTS-001, SERIES-REWRITE-001)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 3: Hook length. The rules say 15 words; the code passes up to 30. Decided: 15 words, blocking, for every new Episode 1. The 5 live hooks keep their wording. (02 C2, 03 C2, 08 C1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 4: Episode length. Decided: standalones within ±10% of target; series episodes between the 12.5-minute floor and 1.35 × the brief; speaking rate 160 words per minute everywhere. Publish code uses the same numbers (today it only allows 15–20 minutes). (02 C5, 03 C3, 08 C2, 09 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 6: Cast size. Decided: the Nov 8 clarity rule wins: at most 4 named speakers (short stories), at most 6 (longer series). The code's 5/7 is changed. (03 C6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 7: Numbers. Decided: every number spoken is written in words, including years ("nineteen ninety-eight"). (03 C5, Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 8: Story card description. Decided: fills two lines, never a third (about 100 characters), checked in one place. The old 24-word and 70-character limits go. (03 C4, 12 C6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 9: Endings. Decided: about 1 in 5 standalones may end open; a series finale always answers its central question; one escaped villain is allowed; Belle never teases a sequel. (02 C6, 03 C8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 10: Spoken-text checks. Decided: two new blocking writer checks: (a) no sentence split across lines with a trailing dash; (b) no line said twice in a row. Drop HAL-SCRIPT-006 and the 5-word minimum per line. (03 C10, Q1, Q2, Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 11: "Chapter" and "episode" inside the story. Decided: characters never say "chapter" or "episode" in dialogue. (03 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 128 (narrows decision 11): Characters must not refer to the story itself as an episode or chapter ("next episode", "this chapter", "episode two"); ordinary uses are fine ("she had an episode", "chapter four" of a book). Same as rule 51. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026)
  • Decision 129: Reading level: the spoken story averages under 15 words per sentence and reads at about grade 6; over grade 8 goes back to the writer. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026)
  • Decision 130: Twist budget: at most one major twist or reveal per episode, each answering or sharpening the series' one main question; no twist opens a new mystery. Checked in the series plan and before voicing. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026)
  • Decision 131: At most 3 story questions open at the end of any episode; a fourth opens only after one is answered. Checked in the series plan and before voicing. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026)
  • Decision 133: Emotion palette. Emotion is built, never announced. The palette is a menu of 18 emotions (liking, worry, fear, stress, grief, love and warmth, hate of the villain, bad feeling at a villain win, glee, relief, hope, dread, longing, jealousy, betrayal, shame, awe, amusement), each with a setup and a trigger (full text in CANON-99 item 133). Characters and the narrator never name the listener's feeling for them. Every story builds liking for the protagonist in the first 3 minutes (a kind or brave act that costs them, a clear want, one small flaw). The clarity reviewer checks only the emotions the plan chose, listing each one's setup and trigger lines. MARC DECIDES Report-only until Marc reviews three stories with it; then Marc decides whether it blocks. — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026, CANON-99 item 133)
