title: CANON-04 — Belle Intro/Outro & Listener-Name Personalization
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: what Belle says at the start and end of every story and episode, where the sting sits, credits, time-of-day words, and how the listener's name is added (or left out).
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: what Belle says at the start and end of every story and episode, where the sting sits, credits, time-of-day words, and how the listener's name is added (or left out). Does not cover: Belle's voice settings and casting (CANON-05 Voices), story-body writing (writer canon), music under Belle and mix levels (sound/mixing canon), player behavior beyond the sting and the name (Player Rules, docs/PLAYER-RULES.md).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 19 MARC DECIDES: Broad time-of-day mood: see Conflict C3. Until Marc decides, writers use none.
  • Decision 72 MARC DOES: Turn the live name greeting on for everyone after Marc tests it on his phone.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Who Belle is

  1. Belle is the Endless Tales host. She never narrates a scene, never plays a character, and never replaces the narrator. — Agreed (docs/BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md and docs/INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md, May 2026; BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES is in the AGENTS.md canon index)
  2. In scripts, Belle's lines are labeled BELLE B: only. Never ANNOUNCER: or SANDY:. — Agreed (docs/PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.5, part of the June 10 canon set, memory /areas/story-pipeline.md)
  3. Belle never uses stock lines: "tonight's story", "today's episode", "are you ready", "for your listening pleasure", "I am pleased to present", "sit back", "relax and enjoy", "welcome back to another exciting…". — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md; INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md). Same list In force (code): lib/voiceBelleRules.ts BELLE_GENERIC_PATTERNS.
  4. Belle never asks a rhetorical question ("Are you ready to find out…?"). — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md)
  5. Belle never spoils a later episode or the ending. — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md). Words like "reveals", "turns out", "killer is" fail. — In force (code) lib/voiceBelleRules.ts
  6. "Endless Tales presents" is never said. — Agreed (CONTENT-001, Bible/CANON_REGISTRY_STORY_RULES.md)
  7. Belle's wording must vary from story to story. No copied template lines. — Agreed (INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md "Dynamic, non-repetitive language")

B. The sting and the opening order

  1. Every story and every episode starts with the Endless Tales sting, right at the start of Belle's intro. This holds for a first play, Start Over and autoplay. Resuming after a pause does not replay the sting. — Agreed (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md Playback basics 2, Marc Nov 8, 2026)
  2. The sting plays once per episode. Never before the outro, never mid-story. There is no closing sting. — Agreed (STING-001, Aug 28, 2026; memory /projects/…/areas/audio-pipeline.md, Nov 2026 mix plan "no closing sting")
  3. Belle starts speaking 1.2 seconds into the sting, and the sting fades under her. — Agreed (PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.5; memory /areas/audio-pipeline.md "Sting crossfade 1200ms")

C. Belle's intro

  1. The intro is one line: one sentence preferred, two short sentences at most. — Agreed (BELLE-001, Aug 28; BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md). Hard cap 38 words. — In force (code) lib/voiceBelleRules.ts
  2. Exception: a listener's very first episode reached through the signup funnel may use a longer, multi-sentence personal welcome. Never "correct" it back to one line. — Agreed (BELLE-002, Aug 6)
  3. Episode 1 of a series (and Episode 1 of each new season): the intro names the title and the author. — Agreed (BELLE-004, Aug 28; BELLE-006 season clause)
  4. A standalone intro names the story title. — In force (code) lib/publicationBelleGate.ts
  5. Every intro states the story's concrete hook: who it is about, what goes wrong, and the tension, in plain words. Mood or setting alone does not count. — Agreed (PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md "REQUIRED elements (June 10)"). In force (code): publicationBelleGate.ts "concrete narrative hook".
  6. The intro has no greeting words: "welcome", "settle in", "let's begin". — In force (code) lib/voiceBelleRules.ts
  7. Series intros after Episode 1: see Conflict C1 (name the series and episode number, or not).

D. Time of day and privacy

  1. Belle never says an exact time, a place, or anything that suggests she knows where the listener is ("It's 10:42", "you're driving near…"). — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md; INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md). In force (code) lib/voiceBelleRules.ts BELLE_EXACT_OR_CREEPY_TIME_PATTERNS.
  2. MARC DECIDES Broad time-of-day mood: see Conflict C3. Until Marc decides, writers use none.

E. Belle's outro, episodes that are not the last

  1. The outro has exactly two parts, in this order: (1) one sentence that recaps this episode, no more; (2) a promotion of the next episode that says its number and the series name, for example "In Episode 4 of 'Blackwater Mile,' the river gives up the name everyone buried." — Agreed (BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD RULE, docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md, Marc Nov 8, 2026; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md Playback basics 9; memory /projects/…/areas/story-pipeline.md Nov 8)
  2. Not allowed: two or more recap sentences, a tease that does not say the next episode's number, or ending on the recap. — Agreed (same source)
  3. No author name, no narrator name and no "an Endless Tales Original" in a non-final outro. No words that sound like the series is over ("end", "final", "concludes", "complete"). — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md "avoid credit/tag language that sounds final"). In force (code): run-next writer prompt; lib/publicationBelleGate.ts; lib/voiceBelleRules.ts.
  4. The next-episode promotion never spoils what happens. — Agreed (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md)
  5. The old non-final requirements (emotional "reflection", "companion presence", "briefly recap the cliffhanger") are replaced by rule 20. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD "Interactions"). Not yet true in code: see Conflict C2.

F. Belle's outro, the last episode and standalone stories

  1. Never point to another episode or another story. — Agreed (BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD RULE, Nov 8; PLAYER-RULES 9)
  2. Open with an emotional beat about how the story resolved. Never open with "That was…". One or two sentences. — Agreed (BELLE-005, Sep 6, 2026)
  3. Then the credit, in this form: "You've been listening to [title] by [author], an Endless Tales Original." — Agreed (BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD RULE, Nov 8; BELLE-005). In force (code): lib/voiceBelleRules.ts (author last name + "Endless Tales"), lib/publicationBelleGate.ts (title + author).
  4. The credit also names the narrator. — Agreed (BELLE-005, Sep 6: "Narrator credit (narrator name) is required"). In force (code): publicationBelleGate.ts; ATL-PIPE-012. See Q1.
  5. No spoken "please rate" request. The review screen handles rating. — Agreed (BELLE-005)
  6. Length: at most 42 words. — Agreed (BELLE-005). Code allows 55: see Conflict C6.

G. Listener-name personalization

  1. The listener's name never appears in Belle's outro text, on any episode. — Agreed (BELLE-003, Aug 13). In force (code): lib/belleStructureGate.ts BELLE-003.
  2. If a script carries [LISTENER_NAME], it appears once, only in Belle's intro line, at a natural pause, never as the first word. The line must sound complete with the name removed. — Agreed (BELLE-001; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.4; Marc approved the mid-sentence rewrite for Extraction EP1, Oct 16, memory /projects/…/areas/pipeline-dispatch-recovery.md). In force (code): lib/personalization/publishGuard.ts blocks the token anywhere else.
  3. Series: the name greeting is a separate, short Belle line that plays right after Belle's intro, before the story. — Agreed (memory /projects/…/areas/personalization.md, Oct 27–28: greeting "must come after a shared title/music opening"). In force (code): app/api/asc3/story-playlist/route.ts (announcement → greeting → story).
  4. In a series, only two places are personalized: the intro of the first episode the listener plays, and the finale. Not every episode. — Agreed (memory personalization.md, Oct 27). In force (code): lib/personalization/firstPlayedOpener.ts.
  5. The greeting plays every time the listener starts Episode 1 from the beginning. On a second or later listen it warmly says they came back. A first-ever play that starts at a later episode also gets the greeting. Resuming mid-episode never does. — Agreed (Marc Oct 29, chat "Clearing CEO series flag"; memory story-pipeline.md). In force (code): GREETING-REPLAY-001 in story-playlist/route.ts.
  6. Greetings are written live for each series (not stock lines). Stock lines are only the backup. — Agreed (memory personalization.md, Oct 28). In force (code): PERS-LIVE-001, lib/personalization/liveGreeting.ts.
  7. The finale ends with a personal sign-off by name. There is no gap between Belle's outro and the sign-off. — Agreed (BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD RULE and PLAYER-RULES 9, Nov 8). Order (before or after Belle's credits): see Conflict C4.
  8. Greeting text rules: exactly one name; 14 to 32 words; no digits; no quotation marks; no author or narrator names; does not say "Endless Tales"; no plot spoilers. Intro greetings put the name in the first six words. The sign-off never promises more episodes. — In force (code) lib/personalization/liveGreeting.ts validateGreetingTemplate
  9. Name clips and greetings are spoken in Belle's own voice and settings. — Agreed (docs/PERSONALIZATION_AND_SFX_IMPLEMENTATION.md "Decisions locked by Marc"; BELLE-007)
  10. The name used is what friends call the listener (display name), never the legal name. — Agreed (BELLE-001 clarification, Aug 28). See Conflict C5.
  11. A listener who arrived through the Belle invitation page and was already greeted there does not get the name opener on their very first play. — In force (code) story-playlist/route.ts (signup_source 'bell-invitation')

H. No-name fallback

  1. If the name can't be added for any reason, the no-name version plays. Playback is never blocked or delayed for this. — Agreed (PLAYER-RULES Playback basics 8, Nov 8; PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md)
  2. Every fallback is logged with its reason so silent failures can be counted. — In force (code) lib/personalization/fallbackTelemetry.ts (PERS-FIX-002)
  3. A story can't be published without its name-free Belle intro audio (announcement_url). — In force (code) lib/personalization/publishGuard.ts
  4. The intro must also exist as a complete no-name render, which must not sound cut short. — Agreed (PERSONALIZATION_AND_SFX_IMPLEMENTATION.md A6, Marc's QA gate)

I. Exceptions and fixes

  1. Author-written series (The Sunset of Competition): the pipeline never rewrites Belle lines and skips the Belle style checks. Technical checks still run. — Agreed (memory /projects/…/areas/sunset-of-competition.md, Nov 3)
  2. A story marked "No Belle B" (LANDING-STORY-001) has no Belle intro or outro by design. — Agreed (Marc ruling Jul 24, 2026, cited in app/api/admin/generate-voices/route.ts)
  3. A failing Belle line goes back to the pipeline writer with the exact reason. The voice step must not swap in a stock template line. — Proposed (the template in generate-voices/route.ts repairedBelleLine says "Next time on…" with no episode number, so it breaks rule 20; AGENTS.md says only the pipeline writer writes scripts)
  4. Every Belle rule above is checked by one shared check used by the writer, voice step, Belle quality step, ready-for-review gate and publish gate, so they never disagree. — Proposed (today five checks disagree; see C1, C2, C6)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 26: Series intros. Decided: every series intro says the series title, "Episode N" and the episode title. Retire BELLE-006. (04 C1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 27: Finale order. Today: story → listener-name sign-off → Belle's credits. Decided: keep that order. The Player Rule is reworded to "no gap between the story, the name sign-off and the credits". (04 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 28: Finale credit. Decided: "…by [author], read by [narrator], an Endless Tales Original." (04 Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 29: Time of day. Decided: Belle never mentions time of day ("late drive"), because people listen at all hours. (04 C3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 30: Outro length. Decided: at most 42 words. (04 C6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 31: Standalone stories. Decided: same as a finale: sting and intro, name greeting, story, name sign-off, credits. No "bridge line" to other series. (04 C7, Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 32: Sting and Belle. Decided: the sting is always the very first sound, and Belle starts 1.5 seconds in, over the sting's tail, on every path. You confirm by ear. (04 C9, Q4, 07 C3, Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 70: The listener's name comes from one field everywhere: the name they enter as "what friends call you". (04 C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 71: Belle names the author in Episode 1's intro (BELLE-004). (04 C8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 72: Turn the live name greeting on for everyone after Marc tests it on his phone. (04 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 73: Each added batch of episodes is a new season: its first episode gets the Episode 1 intro; the last episode of a season promotes the next season's first episode by number (it is not a finale). (04 Q5, Q6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 26, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Naming in series intros. BELLE-006 (Canon Registry, Aug 28) says episodes 2 to N−1 must NOT name the title or author. The writer prompt and the publish gate (run-next buildSeriesEpisodePrompt; lib/publicationBelleGate.ts) REQUIRE every series intro to say the series title, "Episode N" and the episode title, and lib/belleStructureGate.ts still checks BELLE-006 (as "inconclusive"). Recommendation: every series intro says the series name and episode number (a driver needs to know where they are), and never the author. Episode titles optional. Retire BELLE-006's title ban. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED: fact checked or done, Nov 9, 2026; see CANON-99 Part 2] Non-final outro content. BELLE-OUTRO-FORWARD (Nov 8) = one recap sentence + next episode by number. REFLECTION-RULE-UNIFICATION-001 (lib/belleValidation.ts, "Marc 2026-10-22, PERMANENT") plus FIX-BELLE-SERIES-TEMPLATE-001 still REQUIRE emotional reflection and "companion presence" ("you"/"we"), and the writer prompt requires the words "next episode", not the number. Recommendation: Nov 8 wins (newer, in canon). Retire the reflection and companion requirement for non-final outros; require the next episode's number. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 29, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Time-of-day. BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md and INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md (May) allow broad mood ("on this late drive"). The writer prompt templates and REFLECTION_RULE_PROMPT_FRAGMENT (Oct) say "no time-of-day reference". Recommendation: ban it. The audio is made once and heard at any hour, so "late drive" is wrong half the time. Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 27, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Finale sign-off order. Marc Oct 29 (FINALE-SIGNOFF-ORDER-001, in code): story → name sign-off → Belle's credits. Nov 8 rule and PLAYER-RULES: the finale "ends with the personalization statement… no gap between Belle's outro and the personalization", and keep it "exactly as it works today". These read as opposite orders. Recommendation: keep today's code order (sign-off, then credits) and reword PLAYER-RULES 9 to match; the no-gap rule applies either way. Marc decides.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 70, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Name source. BELLE-001 says display_name, not the legal first name. lib/personalization/signupEnsure.ts uses the account's first_name. Recommendation: confirm which field the app shows as "what friends call you" and use one field everywhere. Marc decides.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 30, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Finale/standalone outro length. BELLE-005 says at most 42 words. lib/voiceBelleRules.ts and the writer prompt allow 55. Recommendation: 42 (newer than the May docs, Marc-owned registry). Marc decides.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 31, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Standalone "bridge line". PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.4 lets a standalone outro add one sentence pointing to the author's other series. The Nov 8 rule says a standalone never points to another story. Recommendation: Nov 8 wins; drop the bridge line.
  • C8. [RESOLVED by decision 71, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Author in intros. PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md (June) says Belle's intro never names the author or narrator. BELLE-004 (Aug 28) says Episode 1 names the author. Recommendation: BELLE-004 wins (newer).
  • C9. [RESOLVED by decision 32, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Sting-to-Belle timing. PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC: Belle starts at 1.2 s. lib/personalizedFinalMix.ts uses 0.5 s. Recommendation: 1.2 s. Marc decides by ear.
  • C10. [RESOLVED: fact checked or done, Nov 9, 2026; see CANON-99 Part 2] Old docs still say "briefly recap the cliffhanger" / "Next time on…" (BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md, INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md, INTRO_OUTRO_PRODUCTION_RULES.md). Recommendation: update them to rule 20 or mark them replaced by this doc.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 28, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Does the finale credit still name the narrator? BELLE-005 (Sep 6) says yes; your Nov 8 example ("You've been listening to … by …, an Endless Tales Original") leaves it out. Suggested answer: yes, "…by [author], read by [narrator], an Endless Tales Original."
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 31, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Standalone stories: do they get a name greeting and a name sign-off, or only the stock name opener? Today the live greeting is series-only, and the stock opener plays BEFORE Belle's intro (story-playlist/route.ts), which puts the name ahead of the sting. Suggested answer: standalones get the same pattern as a series finale: sting + intro → greeting → story → sign-off → credits.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 72, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is the live greeting switched on for everyone? It is behind the LIVE_GREETINGS setting (off / allowlist / on). Suggested answer: "on", after your phone test.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 32, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Where does the sting go when a name opener plays first? Suggested answer: the sting is always the very first sound; any name clip comes after Belle's intro.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 73, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Hook-series episodes added after a series is live: does the Episode 1 "first season" intro rule (title + author) apply to the first episode of each added batch? Suggested answer: yes, treat each added batch as a new season.
  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 73, Marc Nov 9, 2026] When there are multiple seasons, does the last episode of a season (not the series) count as a finale (credits, sign-off) or as non-final (next episode by number)? Suggested answer: non-final, promote the next season's first episode by number.

title: CANON-05 — Voices & Voice Generation
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: Belle's voice, narrators, character casting, voice reuse, recasting, the checks at the voice step, ElevenLabs credits, and when audio must be re-made.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: Belle's voice, narrators, character casting, voice reuse, recasting, the checks at the voice step, ElevenLabs credits, and when audio must be re-made. Does not cover: what Belle says (CANON-04), how scripts are written (writer canon), voice loudness, EQ and mixing (sound/mixing canon), the gate order (CANON-08).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 1 MARC DECIDES: Belle's voice is ElevenLabs voice GMhgX8fCR9GUtd3kmlKC, settings: stability 0.49, similarity 0.51, style 0.0, speaker boost on, speed 1.0, model…
  • Rule 10 MARC DECIDES: After the first episode of each new series is voiced, Gemini listens. Only mismatches Gemini flags go to Marc.
  • Rule 47 MARC DECIDES: A published story is re-voiced only with Marc's approval, and the new version is delivered as a link first.
  • Decision 78 MARC DOES: Re-voicing a published story always waits for Marc's listen, even in Direct mode.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Belle's voice

  1. MARC DECIDES Belle's voice is ElevenLabs voice GMhgX8fCR9GUtd3kmlKC, settings: stability 0.49, similarity 0.51, style 0.0, speaker boost on, speed 1.0, model eleven_multilingual_v2. No one changes or tests a substitute without Marc's separate approval. — Agreed (BELLE-007, Bible/CANON_REGISTRY_STORY_RULES.md, Aug 29). In force (code): lib/voiceConstants.ts CANONICAL_BELLE_B_VOICE_ID; liveGreetingService.ts settings.
  2. Old Belle voices wewocdDkjSLm9ZwjO7TD and KWDD3Wyq30ZF5NEL01EJ are retired and never used. — Agreed (PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.5; memory /areas/audio-pipeline.md). In force (code): LEGACY_BELLE_B_VOICE_IDS (also blocks EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL).
  3. Belle's voice is never used for a narrator or a character. — Agreed (PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md v1.5). In force (code): lib/castCollision.ts CAST-COLLISION-001, checked before any spend.

B. Narrators

  1. Every Endless Tales author has one assigned narrator. — Agreed (AGENTS.md Data rules)
  2. No script is written for a narrator that is not in the voice list. — In force (code) WRITER-SELF-CHECK-001, run-next/route.ts
  3. A series keeps Episode 1's narrator voice for every episode. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3 Defaults: "Default narrator reference: Episode 1's locked voice")
  4. In a first-person story, the narrator voice's gender matches the main character's gender. Unknown gender blocks. — In force (code) generate-voices/route.ts narratorGenderCheck
  5. Nick Brennan always has his own voice, never a regular narrator's voice, even in first-person stories. Jack Malone's narrator voice is Nick's and is used only for Nick Brennan stories by that author. — Agreed (NICK-VOICE-001, Marc Oct 28 10:01 EDT; memory /projects/…/areas/story-pipeline.md Oct 28). In force (code): lib/reservedTalent.ts.

C. Casting characters

  1. Marc does not approve casts. Casting is automatic, from the screened voice list, with hard checks. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4, replaces his Oct 29 cast-approval rule; memory story-pipeline.md and audio-pipeline.md)
  2. MARC DECIDES After the first episode of each new series is voiced, Gemini listens. Only mismatches Gemini flags go to Marc. — Agreed (chat "Gemini sound replacement loop", Nov 4–5)
  3. The voice list is one grid that scripts and casting both use: code/number, name, gender, age, accent, accent strength, tone/personality, best use, status, reserved-for, Gemini clarity and accent scores. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4, memory audio-pipeline.md; chat Nov 4–5)
  4. Only voices with clear English. Accents are fine but never too strong to understand. No squeaky voices. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4)
  5. The list holds hundreds of voices, not a few dozen. Keep adding more. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4 and Nov 7)
  6. Once a voice is used, it goes to the bottom of the list. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4). In force (code): recency rotation on last_used_at, generate-voices/route.ts.
  7. A main character's voice is not reused for 30 stories or series. — Agreed (VOICE-REUSE-001, Marc Nov 7). In force (code): lib/voiceReuseWindow.ts.
  8. Main characters and narrators of ongoing series get custom-made voices that only Endless Tales can use, reserved for that series. — Agreed (memory audio-pipeline.md, Nov 4)
  9. One voice per character for the whole story or series. A character keeps that voice under every name form (John Smith, Mr. Smith, John). — Agreed (memory story-pipeline.md Oct 30; CASTING-ALIAS-001 approved, memory /areas/story-pipeline.md). In force (code): character_voice_assignments; series_character_roster.
  10. A character's gender must match the voice's gender. Gender is read from plain words in the description (grandmother, his, boy). — In force (code) lib/characterGender.ts CAST-GENDER-002; lib/voiceFallbackGate.ts
  11. A character's age must fit the voice. A two-band miss (old man → young voice) is not allowed. — In force (code) lib/castingVoiceFilter.ts CAST-BLOCK-001
  12. No speaking character under 14. A 14–17 character gets a voice that truly sounds that age. No voice cloning of anyone under 18. — Agreed (CONTENT-002, Aug 28; MINOR-VOICE-001, memory /areas/story-pipeline.md)
  13. Auto-casting never picks voices made for other jobs: social clips, ASMR, sleep, meditation, customer service, phone systems, assistants, tutorials, cartoon/novelty voices, or voices labeled in another language. — Agreed (CAST-BLOCK-001, Marc Oct 28). In force (code): lib/castingVoiceFilter.ts (CAST-VOICE-FIT-001).
  14. If no voice matches a character's accent, casting stops and says so. It never picks a random voice. — In force (code) lib/voiceFallbackGate.ts VOICE-FALLBACK-001
  15. Every speaking character is in the script's character guide with a description. A speaker missing from the guide is blocked; a missing description is auto-cast by the casting step. — In force (code) CAST-GUIDE-001 (lib/scriptReadiness.ts), CASTING-ALIAS-001 (generate-voices)
  16. Syncing voices from ElevenLabs never undoes our own decisions about a voice. — Agreed (VOICE-SYNC-KEEP-001, Marc Nov 7). In force (code): lib/voiceSyncKeep.ts.
  17. In one story, no two speaking characters share a voice, and characters in the same scene have clearly different voices. — Proposed (speaker identifiability; story-clarity check 7 asks for it, but no casting check guarantees distinct voices)

D. How text is spoken (checked at the voice step)

  1. Every number in a spoken line is written as words. Digits block voicing and send the script back to the writer (up to 3 tries). "Episode 4" in Belle's lines is allowed. — Agreed (numbers as words, PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY "Interactions"). In force (code): Gate 5, lib/numeralPreTtsScan.ts, run at voice_preflight; writer auto-fix NUMERAL-AUTOFIX-001.
  2. No stage directions inside spoken lines: no [brackets] and no (whispers)/(pause)-style notes. They block voicing. — In force (code) generate-voices/route.ts findInlineProductionCues
  3. Every story line has a speaker label. Unlabeled lines block voicing. — In force (code) generate-voices/route.ts
  4. A scene-break line ("NARRATOR: ---") is never sent to ElevenLabs. — In force (code) WORDLESS-LINE-001, generate-voices/route.ts
  5. Listener first names with tricky spelling use a pronunciation table (example: Sean → "shawn"). — In force (code) lib/personalization/nameKey.ts name_overrides
  6. Writer-only rules (dashes, "That was…", speaker naming in dialogue): not checked at the voice step. They belong in the writer canon.

E. Before spending credits

  1. Every free check runs before any ElevenLabs spend: narrator, numbers, labels, stage directions, Belle lines, runtime floor (12.5 minutes estimated at 160 words per minute), cast collision. A failure spends nothing. — In force (code) run-next voice_preflight / series_voice_preflight; generate-voices preflight. Runtime floor Agreed (Marc Oct 26, memory story-pipeline.md).
  2. ElevenLabs extra-usage (overage) cap: 200,000 credits. — Agreed (Marc Nov 5, memory audio-pipeline.md)
  3. Hook series may be voiced past the monthly quota. — Agreed (Marc Nov 5, memory hook-series.md)
  4. Credits are spent on the order of the production queue, and the 1.56 million credits expiring Nov 9, 2026 were to be used first. — Agreed (memory audio-pipeline.md). Expired today: see Q1.
  5. Spend is recorded per call so every credit can be traced to a story. — Proposed (Anthropic writer calls are metered in run-next; ElevenLabs billing is recorded only on success in generate-voices; no per-story credit report found)

F. Stale audio and re-making audio

  1. If a script is edited after its voices were made, the story fails as "stale audio" and can't reach review until it is re-voiced. — In force (code) lib/hookGate.ts HOOK-GATE-STALE-001, check 7
  2. A fresh voicing run first deletes the old voice files for that story, then checks none survived. — In force (code) HOOK-GATE-STALE-001 purge, generate-voices/route.ts
  3. When only a Belle line was edited, that Belle line is re-recorded and the story is re-stamped as current. — In force (code) BELLE-ONLY-FORCE-REGEN-001, BELLE-ONLY-STAMP-001
  4. Every recorded line must use the character's current voice. A line in an old voice blocks the mix. — In force (code) VOICE-001 and lib/voiceMapGate.ts
  5. A line whose audio doesn't match its words (over 40% word error) blocks the mix and is re-recorded, up to 2 times, then the story is parked. — In force (code) GARBLE-001; lib/unifiedGateEngine.ts
  6. A near-silent voice line (below −28 LUFS) blocks the mix and is re-recorded. — Agreed (LOUDNESS-001, Sep 7)
  7. Recasting a character re-records only that character's lines. Nothing else is touched. — Agreed (VOICE-ONLY-REPAIR-001 approved, memory /areas/story-pipeline.md). Tools: scripts/recast-character.js, recast-series-character.ts, recast-published.ts.
  8. An episode that has passed and locked is never re-voiced because of a later episode's problem. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3)
  9. Adding episodes to a series never re-voices the existing ones. — Proposed (SERIES-CONTINUATION RULE, PIPELINE-CANON, pending Marc sign-off)
  10. Author-written scripts (Sunset) are never regenerated. Only episodes missing audio are voiced. — Agreed (memory sunset-of-competition.md, Nov 3)
  11. MARC DECIDES A published story is re-voiced only with Marc's approval, and the new version is delivered as a link first. — Agreed (Episode Correction Loop, PIPELINE-CANON)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 33: Cast approval. Decided: retired (you said Nov 4 you no longer approve casts); one voice grid for all voices. (05 C1, C2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 34: ElevenLabs budget. The big credit block expired today. Decided: a monthly cap that you set, with a stop-and-ask at 80%. (05 Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 74: The voice-reuse rule is 30 stories (old 20-story logic removed). Ongoing-series leads get their own custom voice, reserved forever. (05 C3, C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 75: The writer adds a pronunciation hint for unusual names in the character guide; the voice step uses it. (05 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 76: Build Gemini's listen of each new series' Episode 1 before the next new series is voiced. (05 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 77: The weekly report shows the count of screened voices. (05 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 78: Re-voicing a published story always waits for Marc's listen, even in Direct mode. (05 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 33, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Cast approval. CAST-REVIEW-001 (lib/castReview.ts, Marc Oct 29: "let me listen to the voices… and approve") vs Marc Nov 4 (no longer approves casts). Code keeps it behind CAST_REVIEW, off by default. Recommendation: Nov 4 wins; retire CAST-REVIEW-001 and say so in lib/castReview.ts.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 33, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Two voice tables. The voice grid Marc asked for is narrator_voices (107 active, Nov 5). The character caster draws from character_voices (683 synced, memory /areas/audio-pipeline.md), and VOICE-FALLBACK-001 requires a voice to be in narrator_voices. Recommendation: one grid for all voices, as Marc asked on Nov 4. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 74, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Old reuse rule vs new. Code once excluded voices from "the last 20 stories" (never worked, per lib/voiceReuseWindow.ts). VOICE-REUSE-001 says 30. Recommendation: 30 wins; remove any remaining 20-story logic.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 74, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Custom voices vs screened library. Nov 4: custom voices for main characters/narrators of ongoing series. VOICE-REUSE-001 (Nov 7) assumes main characters come from the shared pool. Recommendation: custom voices for ongoing-series leads (reserved forever); the 30-story rule for everyone else.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 34, Marc Nov 9, 2026] The 1.56 million credits expired today (Nov 9). What is the monthly credit budget from now on? Suggested answer: set a monthly cap and a stop-and-ask point at 80%.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 75, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Character and place names that ElevenLabs mispronounces: is there a pronunciation list for story names? None found. Suggested answer: the writer adds a pronunciation hint to the character guide; the voice step uses it.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 76, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is Gemini's listen of each new series' Episode 1 built and running? Not found in code. Suggested answer: build it before the next new series is voiced.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 77, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is the "hundreds of voices" pool filled, and are the custom lead voices made for the five hook series? Unverified. Suggested answer: report the count of active, screened voices each week.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 78, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should a recast of a published story wait for your listen even in "direct" mode? Suggested answer: yes; a recast is a correction and follows the Episode Correction Loop.

Enforcement status

  • 1–3 → lib/voiceConstants.ts, lib/castCollision.ts (blocks before spend).
  • 4 → data rule; not checked in code. 5 → run-next WRITER-SELF-CHECK-001. 6 → not built as a check (Rule 3 implementation not authorized). 7 → generate-voices. 8 → lib/reservedTalent.ts, lib/voiceEq.ts.
  • 9 → code: CAST_REVIEW off by default. 10 → not found. 11–13 → partly (grid columns exist; fill level unverified). 14 → generate-voices last_used_at. 15 → lib/voiceReuseWindow.ts. 16 → not enforced in code. 17 → character_voice_assignments + series roster. 18–19, 21–22 → lib/characterGender.ts, lib/castingVoiceFilter.ts, lib/voiceFallbackGate.ts. 20 → not checked in code. 23 → lib/scriptReadiness.ts, generate-voices. 24 → lib/voiceSyncKeep.ts. 25 → not built.
  • 26–30 → lib/numeralPreTtsScan.ts, generate-voices/route.ts, lib/personalization/nameKey.ts.
  • 32 → run-next voice_preflight. 33–35 → ElevenLabs account settings, not code. 36 → not built.
  • 37–42 → lib/hookGate.ts, generate-voices, lib/voiceMapGate.ts, GARBLE-001, LOUDNESS-001 (core.ts).

title: CANON-06 — Sound Effects
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: where sound effects come from, the licence, the sound catalog, Gemini screening, the replace loop, when a sound plays, spot vs background sounds, the [SFX:] cue in scripts, what happens when a sound is missing, locked sounds, and never touching published episodes.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: where sound effects come from, the licence, the sound catalog, Gemini screening, the replace loop, when a sound plays, spot vs background sounds, the [SFX:] cue in scripts, what happens when a sound is missing, locked sounds, and never touching published episodes. Does not cover: music, levels of music and the final mix (CANON-07 Music & Final Mix); how writers write scenes and Belle (script-writing canon); voices; publishing; the player.

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 4 MARC DECIDES: Marc agreed to pay the one-time $500 API setup fee once Ron (Sound Ideas) confirms in writing that the key can search AND download, uses the…
  • Rule 5 MARC DOES: Soundsnap downloads are done by Marc by hand.
  • Rule 6 MARC DOES: API keys and logins are entered on the server by Marc himself. They are never pasted in chat or printed.
  • Rule 14 MARC DECIDES: A discarded take never comes back. Every discard runs as a dry run first and then needs Marc's explicit word.
  • Rule 19 MARC DOES: Gemini is a screen, not the final judge. Marc listens to the final test mix.
  • Rule 23 MARC DECIDES: The loop may not run until the library confirms in writing that automated search-download-check is allowed, and Marc approves the code on a branch.
  • Rule 44 MARC DECIDES: All sound effects stay off in every mix (SFX_OFF=on) until the professional library is in and Marc approves a test. Voices and music are not…
  • Rule 53 MARC DECIDES: A published episode is re-mixed for sound only on Marc's explicit word.
  • Rule 54 MARC DECIDES: The first test with the new library is one episode only (Rerouted EP1). Nothing else gets sounds until Marc approves that test.
  • Rule 55 MARC DOES: When sounds are added back to published episodes, it is done one series at a time: one test episode, Marc listens, then the rest.
  • Decision 80 MARC DECIDES: Once a week, Claude proposes new sound names from the "wanted" list; Marc approves the list.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Where sounds come from

  1. Only recorded sounds from a paid professional library may play in a story. Never ElevenLabs or other AI-made sounds. Never the old kept library (Sonniss, Soundly exports). — Agreed (SOUNDSNAP-ONLY-001, Marc Nov 3: "I do not want to use any old sounds or ElevenLabs sounds, only Soundsnap", quoted in lib/sfxSwitch.ts; widened to Sound Ideas Nov 5, memory /projects/…/areas/audio-pipeline.md)
  2. Sound Ideas (Complete Access, bought Nov 5, 2026) is the main library. Soundsnap (12-month plan, bought Nov 2, 2026) is the backup. — Agreed (chat "Apple App Store commission deals", Nov 5: "I want to use Sound Ideas API and we can use Soundsnap as a backup"; memory audio-pipeline.md)
  3. Sound Ideas sounds come in through the SourceAudio API only. No hand downloads from Sound Ideas while the API key is pending. — Agreed (same chat, Nov 5: "Wait for the API")
  4. MARC DECIDES Marc agreed to pay the one-time $500 API setup fee once Ron (Sound Ideas) confirms in writing that the key can search AND download, uses the 5,000-a-day limit, and has the same licence. Connecting it waits until after the Meta launch and the reliability fixes. — Agreed (chat "Cover story map pattern", Nov 7)
  5. MARC DOES Soundsnap downloads are done by Marc by hand. — Agreed (memory audio-pipeline.md, Nov 2)
  6. MARC DOES API keys and logins are entered on the server by Marc himself. They are never pasted in chat or printed. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "Agent rules (Marc, standing)"; Orion note Nov 5)
  7. Library downloads run one session at a time, at a normal human pace, never in bursts. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001 spec, Marc approved Nov 3; Sound Ideas terms: one user at a time)
  8. Library sounds are only ever mixed into finished episodes. They are never offered on their own and never used to train any AI model. — Agreed (Marc's licensing emails to Soundsnap and Sound Ideas, Nov 1–2; Ron's written reply Nov 2)

B. The sound catalog

  1. Claude may only use sounds from a closed catalog of fixed names. Draft v1 has 166 names. IDs start with ALL, CR, MY, WE, SF or RH; the prefix is only for sorting, so any story may use any name. — Agreed (SFX-CATALOG-001, Marc Oct 31; lib/sfxCatalogNames.ts)
  2. Each name is marked "spot" (plays once at a moment) or "background" (a place sound). — Agreed (SFX-CATALOG-001; lib/sfxCatalogNames.ts)
  3. Each name holds up to 3 takes. Different places in a story rotate takes. The same place gets the same take on every re-mix. — Agreed (Marc Oct 31, memory story-pipeline.md; SFX-ROTATE-001 Oct 30)
  4. A take is used in a published mix only if it is a licensed library sound and approved. A name goes live only when it has 3 approved takes. — Agreed (Marc Oct 31: "3 takes he approves by ear"); threshold In force (code) lib/sfxCatalog.ts liveNames()
  5. Test mixes use only licensed sounds (candidates are fine), never kept-library sounds. — Agreed (SFX-TEST-LICENSED-ONLY-001, Marc Nov 2; lib/sfxCatalog.ts)
  6. MARC DECIDES A discarded take never comes back. Every discard runs as a dry run first and then needs Marc's explicit word. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-001 Nov 2; replace-loop spec Nov 3; Orion discard run approved by Marc Nov 3 11:48)
  7. Downloaded files are filed in one folder per catalog ID (for example ALL-01/). The folder decides the name; no word guessing. — In force (code) (SFX-SOUNDSNAP-001, lib/sfxCatalog.ts catalogIdFromLibraryId)
  8. A background take is kept up to 60 seconds long at ingest, so a loop is not obvious. — In force (code) (scripts/sfx-library-ingest.ts)
  9. The catalog lives in storage as audio/sfx-library/catalog.json (library list: sfx-library/manifest.json). There are no sound tables in the database. Marc reviews sounds on the admin page /admin/sfx-library in large text. — Agreed (SFX-REVIEW-001, Marc Oct 30: "a list of sounds … that I can hear and approve"; app/api/admin/sfx-library/route.ts)

C. Gemini screening and the replace loop

  1. Gemini listens to every new candidate sound before it enters the catalog and marks it OK or BAD. — Agreed (SFX-GEMINI-CHECK-001, Marc Nov 3; scripts/sfx-gemini-check.ts)
  2. MARC DOES Gemini is a screen, not the final judge. Marc listens to the final test mix. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001 spec, Nov 3) — see Q2
  3. When Gemini marks a sound BAD, the loop downloads the next search result not tried before, and Gemini checks it again. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001, Marc Nov 3 11:33 ET)
  4. The loop stops after 5 tries per catalog name. If nothing passes, that name gets no sound, and the cue stays silent in mixes. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3: "5 tries and if nothing passes do not use a SFX and move on")
  5. The loop writes one report line per name: tries used (x/5), result (passed id, or NO SFX), and Gemini's reason for each BAD try. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001 spec)
  6. MARC DECIDES The loop may not run until the library confirms in writing that automated search-download-check is allowed, and Marc approves the code on a branch. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001 spec "Not allowed to start until")
  7. The loop runs against Sound Ideas (API) first and Soundsnap second. — Proposed (the Nov 3 spec names only Soundsnap; the Nov 5 decision made Sound Ideas the main library)

D. When a sound plays

  1. Motivated sound: a sound plays only when it truly happens in the scene, right now. No sound for metaphors ("like thunder"), negation, memories, plans, or thoughts inside a head. — Agreed (SFX-SOUNDMAP-001, Marc Oct 31; "motivated SFX", memory profile)
  2. Every sound is named or reacted to by a character or the narrator, right before or right after it plays. Never only described ("The door slams." plus a slam). A sound either plays or is not mentioned. — Agreed (SFX-NAMED-001, Marc Oct 31; memory story-pipeline.md)
  3. Every spoken line that names a sound gets a "play" or "skip" decision with a reason. Missing decisions are recorded. — Agreed (SFX-SOUNDMAP-001; lib/sfxSoundMap.ts)
  4. There is no fixed number of sounds per episode. The story and AI decide. A safety ceiling of 40 added sounds per episode stops a runaway plan; it is never a target. — Agreed (SFX-NO-CAP-001, Marc Oct 31: "let the story and AI determine"); 40 In force (code) lib/sfxOverlay.ts
  5. Action stories get many sounds (gunshots, engines, tyres, running, fights, breaking things), even where the script did not write a cue. — Agreed (Marc Oct 28, memory story-pipeline.md)
  6. One sound per cue. At most 2 sounds on one spoken line. — In force (code) (lib/sfxSoundMap.ts validateSoundMap)
  7. Every episode gets a sound report: where each sound plays, what the story asked for, which take was used, which lines were skipped and why, and which wanted sounds the catalog lacks. — Agreed (SFX-REPORT-001, Marc Oct 30; lib/sfxReport.ts)

E. Spot sounds and background sounds

  1. Spot and background sounds are separate tracks. The catalog decides which kind a sound is. — Agreed (Marc's 6-channel drawing, Nov 1; SFX-CATALOG-001)
  2. A spot sound that happens inside a line plays right after the exact words named for it, using word timing. If the words are not found, it plays just before the line. — Agreed (SFX-WORD-001, Marc Oct 31; lib/sfxAlign.ts)
  3. A spot sound never stops the story. The next line starts 0.3 seconds into the sound, and the rest of the sound drops to 0.45 of its level under the voice. — Agreed (MIX-V4-001, Marc approved live Nov 1); numbers In force (code) lib/sfxLayeredMix.ts
  4. When the next line reacts to the sound (gunshot, then "Get down!"), there is a short beat of 0.6 to 1.0 seconds before the line. Claude decides which sounds get the beat. — Agreed (MIX-V4-001, Nov 1); numbers In force (code) lib/sfxLayeredMix.ts spotGapSec, lib/mixPlan.ts
  5. A background is a short scene-setter of about 10 seconds that tells the listener where they now are. It fades in softly (2.5 seconds) and fades out. It does not run through the whole scene. — Agreed (BG-SCENE-SETTER-001, Marc Nov 2: "It should only be there to let the listener know where he is"); numbers In force (code) lib/sfxLayeredMix.ts
  6. A background is a soft undertone. It is never louder than its under-voice level (0.35 gain). — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "It is just a soft undertone"); 0.35 In force (code)
  7. A background plays only when the story moves to a new place that has a sound. Never at the start of the story (not in the first 6 spoken lines of the first scene). Never the same place sound twice in a row. At least 20 spoken lines apart. — Agreed (Marc Nov 2: "should not start at the beginning of the story", memory audio-pipeline.md); 6 and 20 In force (code) lib/sfxSoundMap.ts BG-SPACING-001
  8. Before mixing, each sound is set to a standard loudness: spot sounds −19 dB average, backgrounds −21 dB average, peaks no higher than −1 dB. — In force (code) (SFX-LEVEL-001, lib/sfxLayeredMix.ts)
  9. While a background plays, the music fades down. — Agreed, see CANON-07 (MUSIC-UNDER-BG-001)

F. The [SFX:] cue in scripts

  1. A script marks a sound as [SFX: <catalog name>] on its own line, never inside a spoken line. — Agreed (STAGE2 v2.3, Marc approved June 10; SFX-NAMED-001 rule text, Oct 31)
  2. Music is never written as an SFX cue. — Agreed (SCRIPT_VALIDATOR v1.2, Marc approved June 10)
  3. In catalog mode the script's own cue recordings (sfx_NNNN.mp3) are never used. Each script cue is filled from the catalog by ID, or left silent and listed as "wanted". It plays just before the next spoken line. — In force (code) (SFX-SOUNDSNAP-001, core.ts, lib/sfxSoundMap.ts)

G. Sounds off, missing sounds, locked sounds

  1. MARC DECIDES All sound effects stay off in every mix (SFX_OFF=on) until the professional library is in and Marc approves a test. Voices and music are not affected. — Agreed (SFX-ALL-OFF-001, Marc Nov 1: "turn the sounds off until we have a professional library")
  2. An episode mixed while sounds are off keeps its [SFX:] cues, so sounds can be added later by re-running the final mix. Voices are not re-recorded. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1, chat "Clearing CEO series flag")
  3. A missing sound is never replaced by a near match, an old sound, or an AI sound. The moment stays silent and is listed in the report. — Agreed (SFX-CATALOG-001, Marc Oct 31: "he does not go to a backup, he just eliminates that sound request")
  4. If a catalog take fails to download during a mix, that one sound is skipped and the mix continues. — In force (code) (lib/sfxOverlayRunner.ts)
  5. A story marked sfx_disabled (for example The Sunset of Competition) never gets sounds. — Agreed (SFX-DISABLED-001, Marc Sep 23; core.ts)
  6. A locked sound file is reused byte for byte. If a locked file is missing or its fingerprint (sha256) does not match the manifest, the mix stops and names the cue. It is never re-made. — In force (code) (SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001 Rule 3/8, validateManifestGate in core.ts); the rule set itself is still marked DRAFT (governance/drafts/SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001.md) — Proposed to declare canon, see Q6
  7. Before any clear or re-run of a story with approved audio, the approved files are archived and the copy is checked; if the archive fails, nothing is cleared. — Proposed (SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001 Rule 13, written by Marc but still draft; not wired into the production runner, see governance/drafts/ATL-SFX-LOCK-RULE13-GAP.md)
  8. A series may have a signature sound (for example the Falls Park bell) that every episode uses as the identical file. — Proposed (SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001 Rule 7, draft)

H. Published episodes

  1. Sound tests, discards, catalog builds and the replace loop never touch a published episode. Test mixes go only to asc3/<id>/preview/<tag>/. — Agreed (SFX-REPLACE-LOOP-001 spec "Never touch a published episode"; SFX-PREVIEW-001)
  2. MARC DECIDES A published episode is re-mixed for sound only on Marc's explicit word. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "Quiet the stories with the bad sounds"; MIX_SPEC.md listen-approval rule, Aug 21)
  3. MARC DECIDES The first test with the new library is one episode only (Rerouted EP1). Nothing else gets sounds until Marc approves that test. — Agreed (Orion note, Marc Nov 5)
  4. MARC DOES When sounds are added back to published episodes, it is done one series at a time: one test episode, Marc listens, then the rest. — Proposed (Marc wants old stories reprocessed with sounds, Nov 7; no method agreed)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 35: Sound library. Decided: Sound Ideas is the main library and Soundsnap the backup; the $169 Soundsnap upgrade is not bought; remove the old ElevenLabs sound-effect fallback. (06 C2, C3, C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 36: When sounds come back on (off since Nov 1). Decided: after Sound Ideas is connected and screened and you approve one Rerouted test mix. (06 Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 37: Who approves a sound. Decided: a Gemini pass is enough; you listen to one test mix per new batch. (06 C6, Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 38: Background sounds. Decided: about 10-second scene-setters only; retire whole-scene beds. (06 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 39: Rights in ads. Decided: no library sounds or music in paid ads until the license is confirmed in writing; record each story's music source. (06 Q3, 07 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 68: The old sound rules in the writer documents (3–6 anchor sounds, no beds, sounds 6 dB under voices) are removed; the sound and mix canons own sound. (03 C12, 06 C1, 06 C7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 79: A sound name may go live with 1 approved take; takes rotate once 3 exist. (06 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 80: Once a week, Claude proposes new sound names from the "wanted" list; Marc approves the list. (06 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 81: SFX-ASSET-LOCK becomes canon for voice locking and the manifest check. (06 Q6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 82: Each series' signature sound (like the Falls Park bell) is one catalog name, used by every episode. (06 Q7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 68, Marc Nov 9, 2026] STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT v2.3 and SCRIPT_VALIDATOR v1.2 (June 10) say 3–6 "anchor" sounds per story, fail above 8, "no continuous ambience beds", sounds only in a gap and never under speech. Marc's Oct 31 (no cap), Nov 1 (spot sounds under the voice, background track) and Nov 2 (short background scene-setters) decisions say otherwise. Recommendation: the Nov rules win; update STAGE2 and the validator in the script-writing canon. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 35, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Code rule SOUNDSNAP-ONLY-001 (Nov 3) and lib/sfxSwitch.ts say "only Soundsnap". Marc's Nov 5 decision makes Sound Ideas main and Soundsnap backup. The code has no Sound Ideas path yet. Recommendation: rename the rule to "licensed library only" and add Sound Ideas as a licensed source. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 35, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Memory (Nov 3) says Marc said yes to Soundsnap's $169 multi-device upgrade. The Nov 5 chat summary says he declined it and Claude advised "let the Soundsnap upgrade go". The replace loop (Nov 3) needs that upgrade. Recommendation: treat the upgrade as not bought; the loop runs on Sound Ideas. Marc confirms.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 38, Marc Nov 9, 2026] SFX-BED-SCENE-001 / SFX_V2 (Oct 31) let a background last its whole scene (up to 240 s). BG-SCENE-SETTER-001 (Nov 2) makes it about 10 s. Code applies 10 s only in catalog mode. Recommendation: Nov 2 wins everywhere; retire the whole-scene option. Marc decides.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 35, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Old code paths still contain an ElevenLabs fallback (lib/sfxLibrary.ts, lib/sfxGenerate.ts, SFX-LIBRARY-001 Oct 29). They are blocked only by the switch SFX_SOUNDSNAP_ONLY (default on; "off" brings them back). Recommendation: remove the fallback so rule 1 cannot be switched off by accident. Marc decides.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 37, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Marc wanted to approve each take by ear (Oct 31). Later he set up Gemini screening (Nov 3) and on Nov 7 asked to be left out of production. Recommendation: see Q2.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 68, Marc Nov 9, 2026] MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL v1.0 (April) says sound effects sit 6 dB under dialogue. SFX-LEVEL-001 sets spot sounds at about the same average level as voices (−19 dB vs about −20 dB). Recommendation: SFX-LEVEL-001 wins; update the protocol table (see CANON-07). Marc decides.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 36, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Sounds are off for every story since Nov 1. When do they come back on? Suggested answer: when the Sound Ideas API is connected, the catalog is filled and screened, and Marc approves the Rerouted EP1 test mix.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 37, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who approves a take before it goes live: Marc by ear, or a Gemini pass? Suggested answer: Gemini pass is enough for a take; Marc listens to one test mix each time a new batch of names is filled.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 39, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Sound Ideas never said yes to its sounds in paid Facebook/Instagram ads. Suggested answer: no library sounds in ads until Ron confirms in writing.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 79, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Names with only 1 or 2 good takes stay silent under the 3-take rule. Suggested answer: allow a name to go live with 1 approved take; rotate once 3 exist.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 80, Marc Nov 9, 2026] The "wanted" list shows sounds the catalog lacks. Who adds new names? Suggested answer: Claude proposes new names from repeated "wanted" entries once a week; Marc approves the list.
  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 81, Marc Nov 9, 2026] SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001 is still a draft, though part of it runs in code. Declare it canon? Suggested answer: yes for voice locking (Part B) and the manifest check; for sounds, the catalog already makes picks repeatable.
  • Q7. [RESOLVED by decision 82, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should the Falls Park bell and other series signature sounds be catalog names? Suggested answer: yes, one catalog name per series signature, used by every episode.

Enforcement status

  • 1 → enforced: lib/sfxSwitch.ts soundsnapOnly() (default on), core.ts; can be switched off by env (see C5).
  • 2–4 → not enforced yet (no Sound Ideas code path).
  • 9–13 → enforced: lib/sfxCatalog.ts, lib/sfxCatalogNames.ts, lib/sfxOverlayRunner.ts.
  • 14 → partly: discardTakes in lib/sfxCatalog.ts; the Marc-word step is process only.
  • 18 → script exists (scripts/sfx-gemini-check.ts); run by hand, not a gate.
  • 20–24 → not built (spec only).
  • 25–28, 30 → enforced in the planner prompt and validator: lib/sfxSoundMap.ts, lib/sfxOverlay.ts. 26 writer rule only when SFX_WRITER_RULE=on or SFX_V2=on.
  • 31 → enforced: lib/sfxReport.ts.
  • 33–39 → enforced: lib/sfxLayeredMix.ts, lib/mixPlan.ts, lib/sfxSoundMap.ts (only when SFX_LAYERED_MIX=on and the catalog planner runs).
  • 44 → enforced by env SFX_OFF=on (server .env.local).
  • 46 → enforced: lib/sfxSoundMap.ts, lib/sfxOverlayRunner.ts.
  • 48 → enforced: core.ts (stories.sfx_disabled).
  • 49 → enforced: core.ts validateManifestGate.
  • 50 → not enforced in the production runner (ATL-SFX-LOCK-RULE13-GAP).
  • 52 → enforced for previews (core.ts SFX-PREVIEW-001); process only for other tools.

Sources reviewed

  • Repo /tmp/dtt: lib/sfxSwitch.ts, sfxCatalog.ts, sfxCatalogNames.ts, sfxSoundMap.ts, sfxOverlay.ts, sfxOverlayRunner.ts, sfxLayeredMix.ts, sfxLibrary.ts, sfxPrefilter.ts, sfxReport.ts, sfxAlign.ts, sfxGenerate.ts, sfxAssetLock.ts, mixPlan.ts; app/api/asc3/render-final-mix/core.ts; app/api/admin/sfx-library/route.ts; app/admin/sfx-library/page.tsx; scripts/sfx-gemini-check.ts, sfx-library-ingest.ts, sfx-catalog-build.ts, sfx-preview.ts; supabase/migrations/20260914120000_add_sfx_disabled_and_corrections.sql; governance/drafts/SFX-ASSET-LOCK-001.md, ATL-SFX-LOCK-RULE13-GAP.md; docs/STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT.md, docs/SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, docs/MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md, Bible/ET_Story_Rules_v3_2_CANONICAL.md, Bible/MIX_SPEC.md, AGENTS.md. Git history is shallow (18 commits), so commit messages gave nothing.
  • Memory: /projects/01a177ad-…/areas/audio-pipeline.md, story-pipeline.md, business-expenses.md; /areas/audio-pipeline.md, /areas/story-pipeline.md, /profile.md.
  • Chats: "Clearing CEO series flag" (Oct 31–Nov 2), "Gemini sound replacement loop" (Nov 3–5), "Apple App Store commission deals" (Nov 5), "Cover story map pattern" (Nov 7).
  • Project docs (claude/sfx-replace-loop-spec.md, claude/soundsnap-download-lower-wacker.md, claude/orion-gemini-library-check-2026-11-03.md, chat-summary-soundsnap-setup): the Projects tool was not available to me. The replace-loop spec text was read from the chat where it was written; the other two were not read directly.

Replaces (once approved)

  • STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT v2.3 "Anchor SFX" section and SCRIPT_VALIDATOR v1.2 SFX count/ambience checks (sound parts only).
  • SFX-LIBRARY-001 (Oct 29) library-then-ElevenLabs flow; ATL-SFX-001 ElevenLabs generation rules.
  • SFX-BED-SCENE-001 / SFX_V2 whole-scene backgrounds.
  • claude/sfx-replace-loop-spec.md (folded into rules 20–24).
