title: CANON-07 — Music & Final Mix
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: the six mix channels from Marc's drawing, the sting, music levels, fades and timing, music under backgrounds and under Belle's outro, voice levels inside the mix, the music source, the final export, and how mix changes are tested.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: the six mix channels from Marc's drawing, the sting, music levels, fades and timing, music under backgrounds and under Belle's outro, voice levels inside the mix, the music source, the final export, and how mix changes are tested. Does not cover: which sounds play and when (CANON-06 Sound Effects); what Belle says (Belle writing canon); script writing; voices and casting; publishing; the player (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md).

Marc's channel drawing (Nov 1, 2026)

Marc drew six channels on Nov 1, 2026 (chat "Clearing CEO series flag"). Claude redrew it as "Episode mix: your plan vs. today". Marc corrected it the same day: no closing sting, the background channel is only a soft undertone, the music fades smoothly into the story, follows tension, crescendos, and fades to 0 three seconds after the outro. That version was built as MIX-V3-001 and MIX-V4-001 and is live.

TIME ->            INTRO           | STORY BODY                                  | OUTRO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 STING            ###\__          |                                             |  (no closing sting)
2 BELLE              [ intro ]     |                                             | [ outro ]
3 MUSIC            (none) ..../^^\_|_ ___--__--___---___--^^^/^^\                |\___________\__ 0
                          swell    | fade   bed follows tension   crescendo swell| soft bed   3 s fade
4 STORY (Hal/Claude)               |[====== one continuous story ======]         |
5 SFX SPOT                         |   |    |     |   ||   |  ||                 |
6 SFX BACKGROUND                   |      /~~\         /~~\          /~~\        |
                                   |   short soft scene-setters, own track       |
ChannelIntroStory bodyOutro
1 StingPlays once at the very start (gain 1.75). Fades as Belle starts.NeverNever
2 BelleIntro line. No music under it.—Outro, soft music under it
3 MusicSilent under Belle's intro. 2.5 s alone before the first line: fade in 1 s, swell, fade to the bed by 1.5 s into the first line.Bed 0.10–0.20, follows tension; dips under backgrounds; crescendo at the end; swell after the last line.Drops to 0.13 in 1 s, holds under Belle, fades to 0 over 3 s after her.
4 Story—One continuous story; only short beats after reaction sounds—
5 SFX spot—On the word, under the voice (CANON-06)—
6 SFX background—~10 s soft scene-setters (CANON-06)—

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 32 MARC DECIDES: Music is made at most 3 times per story or episode. After that the story is flagged for attention; only Marc can re-queue it.
  • Rule 39 MARC DOES: Every mix change goes behind an on/off switch. A test copy goes to a preview folder. Marc listens before it goes live. If it goes wrong, the…
  • Rule 43 MARC DECIDES: No corrected episode replaces a published final_mix.mp3 until Marc listens and approves.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Order and the sting

  1. Every episode runs: sting, Belle's intro, story, Belle's outro. — Agreed (STING-001, Canon Registry Aug 28; PLAYER-RULES #2, Marc Nov 8)
  2. The sting plays exactly once, at the very start, before Belle's first line. Never before the outro, never mid-story. There is no closing sting. — Agreed (STING-001 Aug 28; Marc Nov 1: "no sting at the end")
  3. The sting file is audio/sting/ET_Signature_Sting_v7.mp3.mp3, played at gain 1.75. — Agreed (MUSIC-002, Canon Registry Aug 31, as cited in core.ts); file In force (code)
  4. Belle starts 1.5 seconds into the sting. The sting fades out over 1.2 seconds from that point. — Agreed (Bible/MIX_SPEC.md, Marc canon Aug 24: BELLE_ENTER_SEC 1.5, STING_FADE_DUR 1.2) — see C3 and Q1
  5. No music plays under Belle's intro. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md Aug 24: "NO music bed under narration"; MUSIC-002)
  6. There are 0.75 seconds of silence between the intro block and the story body. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md Aug 24, SILENCE_PRE_STORY)

B. Music into and through the story

  1. The music plays alone for 2.5 seconds before the first story line. It fades in over 1.0 second to the swell level (1.30) and holds. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md 2.5 s pre-roll; MIX-V3-001, Marc's drawing, approved Nov 1); numbers In force (code) lib/mixV3.ts
  2. The music never drops suddenly when the story starts. From 1.2 seconds into the pre-roll it fades down to the bed, finishing 1.5 seconds into the first line. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "does not abruptly quit after the story starts … but fades smoothly"); numbers In force (code) lib/mixV3.ts
  3. One continuous piece of music plays under the whole story. It never restarts from 0:00. — Agreed (MIX-V3-001, approved Nov 1)
  4. The music under the story follows its tension. Claude rates each stretch 1 to 5 at mix time (usually 3–8 marks, at most 14). Levels: 1 = 0.10, 2 = 0.12, 3 = 0.14, 4 = 0.17, 5 = 0.20. Changes ramp over 5 seconds. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "fluctuate in volume based on the tension"; MIX-V4-001 approved live Nov 1); numbers In force (code) lib/mixPlan.ts, lib/mixV3.ts
  5. The music always stays under the voices. — Agreed (MIX-V4-001 plan Marc approved, Nov 1)
  6. If Claude's tension plan fails, the mix still runs with a flat bed at 0.13. — Agreed (MIX-V4-001, Nov 1); In force (code) lib/mixPlan.ts
  7. The music builds (crescendo) through the last 25 percent of the story, at most the last 45 seconds, to at least 0.22 at the last line. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "crescendo at the end"); numbers In force (code) lib/mixV3.ts
  8. After the last line the music swells to 1.30 over 1 second and holds 1 second. — Agreed (MIX-V3-001 / MUSIC-002 swell 1.30); In force (code)
  9. While a background sound plays, the music fades down to one tenth of its level over 3 seconds, then back up over 3 seconds after it. Close backgrounds (under 6 seconds apart) are joined so the music does not pump. This never changes the end swell. — Agreed (MUSIC-UNDER-BG-001, Marc Nov 2: "the music should go very quiet or silent but not abruptly"); numbers In force (code) lib/mixV3.ts bedDuckEnvelope

C. Belle's outro

  1. There is no silence between the story and the outro. The same music runs on from where the story music stopped. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md Aug 25: "Music transitions continuously from the story body into the outro"; MIX-V3-001)
  2. The music drops from the swell to 0.13 in 1 second, before Belle speaks. It holds at 0.13 under her whole outro. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "scales down under the outro"); numbers In force (code) lib/mixV3.ts outroMusicEnvelope
  3. After Belle's last word the music fades evenly to 0 over exactly 3 seconds. Then the episode ends. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1: "goes 3 seconds after the outro as it fades to 0")
  4. There is no gap between Belle's outro and the personalization statement. — Agreed (PLAYER-RULES #9, Marc Nov 8)

D. No dead air and safety checks

  1. The last 10 seconds of the final mix must not be silent. If the loudest point there is under −60 dB, the render fails and nothing is uploaded. — In force (code) (core.ts post-render check; OUTRO-MUSIC-WRAP-001 fixed a 20-second dead-air bug)
  2. Belle's outro must stay audible to the end. If its loudest point is under −35 dB, the render fails. — In force (code) (core.ts)
  3. A final mix shorter than 60 seconds fails. — In force (code) (core.ts)
  4. Every voice line ends with at least 0.3 seconds of quiet before the next line, so no line sounds cut off. — Agreed (ORION-MIX-TRAILPAD-001, Marc merge word Jul 15); In force (code) core.ts
  5. Gaps in the story come only from the script's [BEAT] and [PAUSE] marks, scene breaks, and the short beat after a reaction sound (CANON-06). — Proposed (states the current behavior as a rule)

E. Voices inside the mix

  1. Belle's voice sits at 1.5 times the level of the story's other voices. — Agreed (BELLE-008, Canon Registry Aug 29) — not applied in code today, see Enforcement
  2. Each character gets one fixed loudness change so all characters match. Only speakers more than 1.5 dB off are changed; at most +9 dB up or −6 dB down; peaks never above −1 dB. — Agreed (VOICE-LEVEL-001, Marc Nov 2: "make sure that all the voices have a volume loud enough to hear"); numbers In force (code) lib/voiceLevel.ts
  3. Any story voice line measured below −28 LUFS stops the render for a re-record. It is never boosted. — Agreed (LOUDNESS-001, Canon Registry Sep 7)
  4. The story body (voices and sounds) is levelled in one pass to −16 LUFS, true peak −1.5 dB. Belle's intro and outro are not levelled, only resampled. — In force (code) (core.ts loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=11)
  5. The intro, story and outro are matched in loudness: no section more than 2 LU louder or quieter than the story body. — Proposed (no check exists; the intro and story mixes may be halved by the mixer while the outro is not, see Q4)

F. Music source

  1. Every story has its own music file (background_music.mp3), made from the script's SUNO PROMPT (2–3 sentences: genre, instruments, tempo, mood) through Kie.ai (Suno). — Agreed (STAGE2 v2.3, Marc approved June 10; Marc understands music comes from Kie, memory audio-pipeline.md)
  2. If a story has no music file, the final mix stops. It never mixes without music. — In force (code) (core.ts "Missing story-specific background_music.mp3")
  3. MARC DECIDES Music is made at most 3 times per story or episode. After that the story is flagged for attention; only Marc can re-queue it. — In force (code) (MUSIC-CAP-001, run-next/route.ts)
  4. The music starts at a strong point in the track, not always at 0:00. — In force (code) (core.ts findStrongMusicOffset)
  5. audio/intro_outro_music.mp3 never plays under Belle's intro or outro. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md, Marc canon Aug 24)
  6. Only music Endless Tales has commercial rights to may be used, and its source is recorded for each story. — Proposed (no licence record found for Kie/Suno output or the shared music library in lib/music-library.json)

G. Export

  1. The final mix is MP3, 192 kbps, 44.1 kHz, stereo. — In force (code) (core.ts)
  2. Each render writes final_mix.mp3, story_body.mp3, story_body_with_outro.mp3 and outro_with_music.mp3 to asc3/<story_id>/. — In force (code) (core.ts)
  3. After every re-mix, the stored links get a new version (?v=<render time>), so phones fetch the new mix and personalized mixes rebuild. — Agreed (MIX-VERSION-001, Marc Nov 7, Rerouted EP1)

H. Testing and changing the mix

  1. MARC DOES Every mix change goes behind an on/off switch. A test copy goes to a preview folder. Marc listens before it goes live. If it goes wrong, the switch goes off. — Agreed (two-stage mix plan Marc approved Nov 1; MIX_SPEC.md listen-approval rule, Aug 21)
  2. MIX_V3=on and MIX_V4=on stay on in production. — Agreed (Marc approved Stage 1 and "Proceed with stage 2", Nov 1)
  3. A mix-only test reuses the published sound plan, so only the mix changes. — In force (code) (core.ts mixOnly)
  4. If a mix problem happens once, fix that mix. If it happens in 2 or more stories, change the rule. — Agreed (docs/MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md v1.0, owner Marc)
  5. MARC DECIDES No corrected episode replaces a published final_mix.mp3 until Marc listens and approves. — Agreed (MIX_SPEC.md, Marc Aug 21) — see Q5

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 12: Retire old manual documents as history: STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS v1.2, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, STORY_GRADING_RUBRIC.md, STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, NEDS scoring, character-attachment scoring, MASTER_RULES.md, DEPLOY.md, DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md, MIX_SPEC.md and MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md level tables, et_mix_assembly.py, ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001 Parts A, D, E. Decided: yes, all. (01 C1, 02 C4, Q5, Q6, 03 Q7, 07 C4, C6, 13 C9, 15 C3–C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 32: Sting and Belle. Decided: the sting is always the very first sound, and Belle starts 1.5 seconds in, over the sting's tail, on every path. You confirm by ear. (04 C9, Q4, 07 C3, Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 39: Rights in ads. Decided: no library sounds or music in paid ads until the license is confirmed in writing; record each story's music source. (06 Q3, 07 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 40: Outro music. Decided: music sits at 0.13 under Belle with a 3-second fade (your Nov 1 drawing); old numbers and the unused music-bed check are updated. (07 C1, C2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 41: Loudness. Decided: the whole episode measures −16 LUFS (±1), peaks no higher than −1 dB, and no section is more than 2 units off the story. (07 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 42: [MUSIC:OUT] / [MUSIC:IN] marks. Decided: build them (3-second fades, at most twice per story). (07 C5, Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 43: Re-mixing a published episode. Decided: Gemini checks the new mix and you're asked only when it flags a problem. (07 C7, Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 83: Belle sits about 3 dB above the story voices (replaces the unbuilt "1.5x" rule). (07 Q6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 40, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Bible/MIX_SPEC.md (Aug 24–25) and the MUSIC-002 header in core.ts give older outro numbers: music down to 0.019, then "rises to 0.50", a 2-second fade (Aug 25), and the code value set to 0 (Belle with no music). Marc's Nov 1 drawing rule is 0.13 under Belle and a 3-second fade. Recommendation: Nov 1 wins; rewrite MIX_SPEC.md and the core.ts header. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 40, Marc Nov 9, 2026] lib/musicBedGate.ts checks for MUSIC-002 levels (flat 0.13 bed, outro rise to 0.50). Today's mixes would fail it. It is not wired into any render. Recommendation: update it to MIX-V3/V4 shapes or retire it. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 32, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Four sting timings exist: core.ts (Belle at 1.5 s over the sting, 1.2 s fade), lib/personalizedFinalMix.ts (sting fades from 0.5 s, then 0.4 s silence, then the name opener), Bible/et_mix_assembly.py (sting v6, Belle at 1.2 s), and memory "sting crossfade 1200 ms". Marc's drawing showed the sting ending before Belle. Recommendation: one timing for both paths; see Q1. Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] docs/MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md (April) lists levels in dB (bed −28 dB, Belle −60 dB, beats −18 dB, swell −10 dB, sound effects −6 dB under dialogue). docs/INTRO_OUTRO_* (May) and the memory note "music ducks to 15%" are also older. Recommendation: replace those tables with this document's levels. Marc decides.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 42, Marc Nov 9, 2026] STAGE2 v2.3 (June 10) lets writers use [MUSIC:OUT] / [MUSIC:IN] (music to silence and back, "to its 15% bed", at most twice). The mixer ignores these marks, so nothing happens. Recommendation: either build it (fade to 0 over 3 s, back to the tension level over 3 s) or remove it from STAGE2. Marc decides.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Bible/et_mix_assembly.py targets −14 LUFS with an old v6 sting and an old Belle voice ID. core.ts targets −16 LUFS. Recommendation: core.ts wins; mark the .py file as history. Marc decides.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 43, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Rule 43 (Marc listens before a published mix is replaced, Aug 21) conflicts with Marc's Nov 7 wish for fully autonomous production. Recommendation: see Q5.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 32, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should Belle start over the sting (1.5 s in, today's main mix), or after the sting ends (your drawing, and the personalized path)? Suggested answer: keep 1.5 s over the sting for both paths, so every listener hears the same opening.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 39, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Which music do we have rights to? Kie/Suno output and the shared tracks in lib/music-library.json have no licence record. Suggested answer: confirm the Kie/Suno plan allows commercial streaming and ads, and record the source per story.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 42, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should [MUSIC:OUT] / [MUSIC:IN] work? Suggested answer: build it, at most twice per story, with 3-second fades.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 41, Marc Nov 9, 2026] There is no loudness target for the whole episode, and no check that intro, story and outro match. Suggested answer: measure the whole final mix; target −16 LUFS (±1), true peak no higher than −1 dB, and no section more than 2 LU off the story.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 43, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who approves a re-mix of a published episode now that production should run without you? Suggested answer: Gemini reviews the new mix for timestamped problems; you are asked only when it flags one.
  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 83, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is BELLE-008 (Belle at 1.5x) still wanted? The code does not apply it; Belle is only resampled. Suggested answer: measure Belle against the story voices and set her about 3 dB above them.

Enforcement status

  • 1–2 → enforced in core.ts assembly order; lib/stingDetectorGate.ts checks the sting but runs only in lib/assembleAndVerifyFinalMix.ts, not in the main render.
  • 3–6 → enforced: core.ts (BELLE_ENTER_SEC, STING_FADE_DUR, SILENCE_PRE_STORY). Personalized path differs (C3).
  • 7–18 → enforced when MIX_V3=on and MIX_V4=on: lib/mixV3.ts, lib/mixPlan.ts, core.ts. Unit tests: __tests__/mix-v3-001.test.ts, mix-v4-001.test.ts.
  • 15 → enforced unless MUSIC_BED_DUCK=off.
  • 20–22 → enforced: core.ts post-render validation (blocks upload).
  • 23 → enforced: core.ts MIN_TRAILING_SILENCE_SEC 0.3.
  • 25 → not enforced (core.ts resamples Belle only).
  • 26 → enforced unless VOICE_LEVEL=off: lib/voiceLevel.ts.
  • 27 → enforced: core.ts LOUDNESS-001 (unmeasurable lines are skipped).
  • 28 → enforced: core.ts.
  • 29, 35 → not enforced.
  • 31–33 → enforced: core.ts, run-next/route.ts.
  • 36–38 → enforced: core.ts.
  • 39, 42, 43 → process only.

Sources reviewed

  • Repo /tmp/dtt: app/api/asc3/render-final-mix/core.ts; lib/mixV3.ts, mixPlan.ts, sfxLayeredMix.ts, musicBedGate.ts, stingDetectorGate.ts, loudness-gate.ts, voiceLevel.ts, outroMusicClip.ts, personalizedFinalMix.ts, assembleAndVerifyFinalMix.ts, music-library.json; app/api/asc3/generate-music/route.ts; app/api/admin/production-jobs/run-next/route.ts; Bible/MIX_SPEC.md, Bible/et_mix_assembly.py, Bible/CANON_REGISTRY_STORY_RULES.md; docs/MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md, INTRO_OUTRO_PRODUCTION_RULES.md, STAGE2_SCRIPT_PROMPT.md, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, PLAYER-RULES.md; AGENTS.md; __tests__/mix-*.test.ts. Git history is shallow (18 commits), so commit messages gave nothing.
  • Memory: /projects/01a177ad-…/areas/audio-pipeline.md, player-rules.md, story-pipeline.md; /areas/audio-pipeline.md.
  • Chats: "Clearing CEO series flag" (Nov 1–2: the drawing, Marc's 4-point reply, Stage 1 and Stage 2 approvals, SFX off); "Cover story map pattern" (Nov 7).
  • The drawing itself: Marc's photo is not stored anywhere I could reach. Claude's redraw is the artifact "Episode mix: your plan vs. today" (claude.ai/artifact/QcCPFB47GnhteKZ2NzMAhh, file reports/mix-lanes.html in that session). The table above is rebuilt from Claude's reading of it and Marc's corrections.
  • Project docs: the Projects tool was not available to me.

Replaces (once approved)

  • Bible/MIX_SPEC.md (Aug 24–25), MUSIC-002 values (Aug 31), ATL-PIPE-007 "Production Standard v2" outro (June 10).
  • Bible/et_mix_assembly.py ("ET Mix Spec v2.3.67").
  • docs/MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md "Quick reference — mix level standards" table (the process steps stay).
  • docs/INTRO_OUTRO_PRODUCTION_RULES.md and docs/INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE.md mix parts.
  • STAGE2 "[MUSIC:IN] returns to its 15% bed" wording.

title: CANON-08 — Quality Gates & Marc's Review
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: every automatic check from brief to publish, in order; what each checks; pass, fail and retry; how failures are classified and fixed; what Marc reviews and how.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: every automatic check from brief to publish, in order; what each checks; pass, fail and retry; how failures are classified and fixed; what Marc reviews and how. Does not cover: the writing rules a check enforces (writer canon), Belle wording (CANON-04), voice casting (CANON-05), sound and mix (sound/mixing canon), publishing mechanics and visibility (publishing canon), the player (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 14 MARC DECIDES: Premise gate (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001), before writing → the premise is not a near-copy of another story → sent back for a new premise variant, up…
  • Rule 17 MARC DECIDES: validate_script → (a) story-card copy rules, (b) no duplicated passages (Gate 4), (c) AI validator. Failures go back to the writer, up to 2 times,…
  • Rule 35 MARC DECIDES: Final audio always needs Marc's ear before going live, except in "direct" mode, which waives it fully. Nothing may assume Marc catches bad audio…
  • Rule 36 MARC DECIDES: One publish switch, set only by Marc: "Review" (hold at ready for review) or "Direct" (go live without review). It is read at the moment a story…
  • Rule 39 MARC DECIDES: Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends corrections → the corrected version comes to him as a link, not published → Marc…
  • Rule 41 MARC DOES: Marc checks player changes on a real phone before they are accepted.
  • Rule 44 MARC DECIDES: A Gemini final read of the whole series decides publish / fix (2 rounds) / hold, and Marc gets one message only on hold.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. Standing rules for every gate

  1. Classify before fixing. Every stuck story is either (A) a pipeline defect: fix the code and add a guard so it can't recur, or (B) a story defect: send the story back for correction automatically and reprocess it automatically when fixed. Every block report says A or B. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 1, Oct 4; CLASSIFY-BEFORE-FIX LOOP, Oct 3)
  2. No fix work starts until the A/B call is written down. — Agreed (Rule 1 Defaults)
  3. Every check must be able to stop the run. A check never logs a warning and continues. New checks block by default. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 2, Oct 4)
  4. A check may warn instead of block only if its own definition says, in writing: what it checks, why warning is safe, and which later blocking check catches the problem. — Agreed (Rule 2)
  5. A failure record names the check, the field or line, and expected vs. actual, so it can be classified without re-investigating. — Agreed (Rule 2 Interactions)
  6. Series run one episode at a time. A failure holds only the current episode. Passed episodes stay locked and are never re-checked. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3)
  7. The publish setting never weakens or skips a check. All checks run before the publish decision. — Agreed (Rule 2 and Rule 4)
  8. A failed check command that couldn't run is "unverified", never a pass. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Defaults, several rules)
  9. Before any fix: a three-line root-cause note (the cause; every other place with the same cause, found by a search shown to Marc; why it won't come back). Without it, it is a patch. — Agreed (Marc PERMANENT RULE 1, memory /projects/…/preferences.md)
  10. A fix counts as done only when the success rate moves on real jobs. A merged PR doesn't count. — Agreed (Marc PERMANENT RULE 2, memory preferences.md)
  11. No job is dispatched before its fix PR is merged. — Agreed (Sequencing Rule, Marc Jul 22, PERMANENT, listed in PIPELINE-CANON)
  12. Text fixes are made by the pipeline writer. No agent writes or edits scripts by hand. — Agreed (AGENTS.md Agent rules; PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY Defaults)

B. The gates, in order (standalone story)

Each line: step name → what it checks → on failure.

  1. Brief guard (ATL-BRIEF-GUARD-001) → a missing brief never wipes an existing script → job fails, story flagged needs_attention. — In force (code) run-next/route.ts
  2. MARC DECIDES Premise gate (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001), before writing → the premise is not a near-copy of another story → sent back for a new premise variant, up to 2 tries, then parked. Override only by Marc's recorded word in the brief. A "similar cluster" only warns. — In force (code) run-next enforcePremiseGateBeforeStage2; lib/unifiedGateEngine.ts. Warn on clusters is Agreed (Marc ruling Jul 18, 09:47 EDT).
  3. generate_script (writer).
  4. validate_voice_conformance → the script matches the author's voice profile; skipped when the author has none. — In force (code)
  5. MARC DECIDES validate_script → (a) story-card copy rules, (b) no duplicated passages (Gate 4), (c) AI validator. Failures go back to the writer, up to 2 times, then parked. Author-written stories are never sent back; they fail to Marc. — In force (code) run-next validateStandaloneScript (MAX_RETRIES 2)
  6. validate_story_resolution → the story answers its main question. Failure → writer rewrite. — In force (code)
  7. Story clarity gate (7 checks: three-sentence test, goal clear in about 480 words, cast limit, no unexplained insider words, every scene has a purpose, recap line in Episode 2+, easy to follow by ear) → before any voicing → any failure sends the script back to the writer with quoted lines; nothing is voiced. Fail-closed. Until built, a reviewer applies it by hand before voicing. — Agreed (STORY-CLARITY RULE, PIPELINE-CANON, Marc Nov 8). Not built.
  8. voice_preflight, the last stop before spending → narrator voice exists, numbers written as words (Gate 5, back to writer up to 3 tries), runtime floor 12.5 minutes, Belle intro/outro rules, no stage directions in spoken lines, required fields. — In force (code) run-next ~4250–4420; generate-voices preflight. Runtime floor Agreed (Marc Oct 26).
  9. generate_voices → Belle line check (may block), cast collision, stale-file purge. — In force (code)
  10. generate_belle_assets → validate_belle_assets → validate_belle_quality → repair_belle_quality: failures are repaired automatically, up to 2 rounds, then parked. — In force (code) MAX_BELLE_BLOCKED_RETRIES = 2
  11. generate_music → render_final_mix. Before the mix: every audio line matches a script line (ORPHAN-001), uses the current voice (VOICE-001), and matches its words (GARBLE-001, 40% error limit); near-silent lines block (LOUDNESS-001); Belle structure check (BELLE-001 to 006). Failures re-record or re-render, up to 2 times, then parked. — In force (code); LOUDNESS-001 Agreed (Sep 7).
  12. complete_story_package, then four checks in this order:
    • ARTIFACT-GATE-002: final mix file exists. Missing cover only warns (cover can be added later). — In force (code)
    • HOOK-GATE-001: seven checks (hook early, sound-cue count, genre, Belle, audio, cover, stale audio). Failure → writer hook rewrite, up to 2, then parked. — In force (code) lib/hookGate.ts. Hook within 15 spoken words is Agreed (memory /areas/story-pipeline.md; Marc ruling Jul 24, 2026). See Conflict C1.
    • RUNTIME-GATE-001: finished length within ±10% of the brief. Mismatch → parked for a person (no automatic rewrite). — In force (code) lib/runtimeGate.ts. See C2.
    • QUALITY-GATE-001: AI scores the story out of 30. 24 or more passes. Under 24 → automatic rewrite, up to 3 times, then parked. If the scorer itself fails, the story is parked, never passed. — In force (code) lib/storyQualityGate.ts. See C3.
  13. ready_for_review gate → required fields present (including the eBook text), final_mix.mp3 really in storage, Belle position rules. Missing narrator credit is auto-fixed up to 2 times, then parked and Marc is told. — In force (code) verifyStandaloneReadyForReview; ATL-PIPE-012
  14. Every story needs a complete eBook before review and before publish. — Agreed (EBOOK-COMPLETENESS RULE, Oct 4)
  15. Publish checks (every publish path): publication hold off; Belle copy gate with no waiver; name-free Belle intro audio exists; episodes numbered 1..N with no gaps; all episodes of a release go live together. — In force (code) lib/directPublish.ts, lib/publicationBelleGate.ts, lib/personalization/publishGuard.ts. Numbering and all-together are Agreed (EPISODE-NUMBERING, EPISODE-ADDITION, Oct 4; Marc Nov 8).

C. The gates, in order (series)

  1. generate_episode_script → whole-series plan first (SERIES-OUTLINE-001); writer self-check (WRITER-SELF-CHECK-001) runs the same free checks the later steps run (format, numbers, runtime, Belle rules, cast list, stock AI phrases) and rewrites with the exact failures, at most 2 rewrites (3 drafts), then fails closed. At most 2 failed writer runs per episode before a person resets it (WRITER-SPEND-CAP-001). Every episode shares a cast with Episode 1 (SERIES-CAST-CONTINUITY-001). — In force (code). Whole-series plan and continuity check are Agreed (Marc Oct 29, permanent, memory story-pipeline.md).
  2. score_validate_package → earlier episodes unchanged since later ones were written (continuity pin); all episodes read together for contradictions (SERIES-CONTINUITY-001); facts checked against cast lists (SERIES-FACTS-001); package validator. Failures send the episode back for rewrite. A Gemini read of the whole series is stored as a report and does not block. — In force (code) scoreValidateSeriesPackage
  3. series_voice_preflight → same as rule 20, per episode. — In force (code)
  4. series_generate_voices → series_generate_belle_assets (Belle retries up to 3) → series_generate_music → series_render_final_mix (same pre-mix checks as rule 23) → complete_story_package → ready_for_review for the whole series → one publish decision for the whole series. — In force (code)
  5. Series must get the same final checks as standalones (hook, runtime, quality) per episode before review. — Proposed (today HOOK-GATE-001, RUNTIME-GATE-001 and QUALITY-GATE-001 run for standalones only; see C4)

D. When a check fails

  1. Story defect → automatic send-back to the writer or a metadata fix, then automatic reprocessing. No standing human step. — Agreed (Rule 1)
  2. Each automatic fix has a cap (usually 2, numbers 3, quality 3). After the cap, the story is flagged needs_attention and the job stops. — In force (code) lib/unifiedGateEngine.ts
  3. MARC DECIDES Final audio always needs Marc's ear before going live, except in "direct" mode, which waives it fully. Nothing may assume Marc catches bad audio after a direct publish. — Agreed (Rule 1 and Rule 4 option A, Oct 4, 10:34–10:35 EDT)

E. Marc's review

  1. MARC DECIDES One publish switch, set only by Marc: "Review" (hold at ready for review) or "Direct" (go live without review). It is read at the moment a story is ready to publish and stays until Marc changes it. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4; PLAYER-RULES "What listeners can see" 4, Nov 8)
  2. Marc's current choice: Direct. — Agreed (Rule 4 initial value; memory story-pipeline.md Oct 27). See Q1.
  3. A story waiting for review is hidden from listeners and shows in the admin Review tab. — In force (code) ATL-PIPE-014; Marc's M-1 rule (no manual visibility fixes).
  4. MARC DECIDES Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends corrections → the corrected version comes to him as a link, not published → Marc approves → only then it replaces or publishes. — Agreed (Marc Aug 21, PERMANENT, PIPELINE-CANON)
  5. A series is reviewed and published as one unit. No per-episode review holds. — Agreed (Rule 3, Rule 4)
  6. MARC DOES Marc checks player changes on a real phone before they are accepted. — Agreed (PLAYER-RULES Design 5)
  7. Status reports count only what was checked directly (database row, file line, command output). Relayed claims are "unverified". — Agreed (memory pipeline-dispatch-recovery.md, Oct 16; profile: "verified results over reported ones")
  8. Marc wants production to run without him; he steps in when he chooses. — Agreed (Marc Nov 7, memory story-pipeline.md)
  9. MARC DECIDES A Gemini final read of the whole series decides publish / fix (2 rounds) / hold, and Marc gets one message only on hold. — Proposed (Marc asked for it Nov 7, but the Story Production Spec is a draft he has not approved to build)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 3: Hook length. The rules say 15 words; the code passes up to 30. Decided: 15 words, blocking, for every new Episode 1. The 5 live hooks keep their wording. (02 C2, 03 C2, 08 C1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 4: Episode length. Decided: standalones within ±10% of target; series episodes between the 12.5-minute floor and 1.35 × the brief; speaking rate 160 words per minute everywhere. Publish code uses the same numbers (today it only allows 15–20 minutes). (02 C5, 03 C3, 08 C2, 09 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 18: Repairs. Decided: text problems go back to the pipeline writer automatically (never an agent); a whole failed production gets one repair pass, then cold storage. "Hal rewrite" in PIPELINE-CANON becomes "pipeline writer rewrite". (01 C2, C3, 08 C7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 21: Series skip three final checks (hook, length, quality). Decided: run them on every series episode too. (08 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 22: Quality score pass mark. Decided: 24 out of 30 (the code's stricter number). (08 C3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 23: Parked stories. Decided: one daily list; Orion sorts them and asks you only when no rule answers. (08 C6, Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 25: Story clarity check until it's built. Decided: a fresh AI reviewer (never the writer) runs it, and the result is saved with the episode. (08 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 84: Every check that only warns gets a written reason in its canon document, or it becomes blocking. (08 C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 85: The story clarity check runs before voicing. The Gemini read of the whole series stays report-only until decision 24's trial. (08 C8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 86: In Review mode, Marc gets one Telegram message per series with a play link per episode, plus the Admin Review tab. (08 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 87: The Belle structure check runs in the writer's self-check and before voicing (same check both places). (08 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 3, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Hook deadline. Canon says the hook lands within 15 spoken words (memory /areas/story-pipeline.md; Marc ruling Jul 24 "start at canon"; HOOK-001 note). lib/hookGate.ts passes up to 30 words (HOOK_PASS_WORD_LIMIT = 30), and its "warn" band is empty. Recommendation: 15 words, blocking. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 4, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Length tolerance. LENGTH-002 (Canon Registry, Aug 28): each episode within ±20% of the commissioned length. RUNTIME-GATE-001 (code, Oct 11 decision): ±10%. Writer self-check also uses ±10%. Recommendation: ±10% (newer, and the floor is 12.5 min). Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 22, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Quality score bar. June canon (memory /areas/story-pipeline.md): "30-point rubric gates publish at 22+, 26 gold". Code: 24 or more passes. Recommendation: 24 (newer code, stricter). Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 21, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Series skip three final checks. HOOK-GATE-001, RUNTIME-GATE-001 and QUALITY-GATE-001 run only for standalones; series episodes go straight to review or publish. Rule 2 says every check must be able to stop the run. Recommendation: run them per episode (rule 32). Marc decides.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 84, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Warn-only checks without written justification (Rule 2 requires one): hook-gate genre check, garble stop-line when its report is missing (continues), runtime gate when length can't be measured (continues), Belle structure "inconclusive" results, Gemini series read (report only). Covered: missing cover (COVER-PIPELINE-DECOUPLE-001), premise clusters (Marc Jul 18). Recommendation: each one gets its written justification or becomes blocking.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 23, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who hears about parked stories. Quality-gate exhaustion: "do NOT notify Marc" (code). Ready-for-review exhaustion: notify Marc (GAP2-NOTIFY). Nov 7: Marc wants to be left out. Recommendation: one daily list of parked stories, nothing else. Marc decides.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 18, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Hand-written fixes. Rule 1 and AGENTS.md: the pipeline writer makes text fixes. In practice Claude wrote replacement Belle outros for Orion → Hal to paste (Rerouted EP2–3, Nov 7). Recommendation: always route through the writer with the failure quoted.
  • C8. [RESOLVED by decision 85, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Where the AI read goes. Story-clarity rule (Nov 8): before voicing, blocking. Production Spec draft (Nov 7): Gemini read before publishing decides publish. Claude advised on Nov 7 that the read should come before voicing. Recommendation: clarity gate before voicing (approved); final Gemini read only after Marc approves the spec.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED: fact checked or done, Nov 9, 2026; see CANON-99 Part 2] Is the publish switch on Direct right now, and is the global publication hold on or off? It was turned back on Oct 23–24 during a test (chat "Clearing CEO series flag"). Suggested answer: report both values in every status report.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 25, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who runs the story clarity check by hand until the gate is built? Suggested answer: a fresh AI reviewer (not the writer), output stored with the episode.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 23, Marc Nov 9, 2026] After a story is parked (needs_attention), who clears it and how often? Suggested answer: Orion reviews the parked list daily, classifies A/B, and only asks Marc when a rule is unclear.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 86, Marc Nov 9, 2026] In "Review" mode, how does Marc get the play link: admin Review tab, Telegram, or both? Suggested answer: one Telegram message per series with one play link per episode, plus the Review tab.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 87, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Does the Belle structure check (BELLE-004 to 006) stay at assembly, or move to the writer self-check so it fails before spend? Suggested answer: writer self-check and voice preflight, both using the same function.

Enforcement status

  • Rule 3–5 → partly (see C5).
  • Rule 6, 40 → partly: one production job per series; per-episode locking not fully built (Rule 3 "implementation is a separate track").
  • Rules 7, 8, 13–18, 20–25, 27–31, 34 → enforced in code at the paths named.
  • Rule 19 → not built (manual).
  • Rule 26 → enforced at ready_for_review (prose_text required); publish side unverified.
  • Rules 9–12, 39, 41–43 → working rules, not code.
  • Rule 32, 44 → not built.

Sources reviewed

title: CANON-09 — Publishing & Release
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: the publish switch, when and how stories go live, episode numbering, hidden episodes, unpublishing, cold storage, the publication hold, the needs_attention flag, approval records and story history.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: the publish switch, when and how stories go live, episode numbering, hidden episodes, unpublishing, cold storage, the publication hold, the needs_attention flag, approval records and story history. Does not cover: the quality checks that must pass before publishing (CANON-08), covers and eBooks (CANON-10), or what the player does with live episodes (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 3 MARC DECIDES: Review: every story waits at Ready for Review until Marc listens and approves. Then it goes live.
  • Rule 5 MARC DECIDES: Only Marc changes the switch, with a one-line instruction or the Admin page switch. It stays until he changes it again.
  • Rule 9 MARC DECIDES: In Review, corrections follow the Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends fixes → the fixed version comes to him as a link, not…
  • Rule 11 MARC DECIDES: A story goes live complete, with all its episodes at once. A series stays hidden until every episode is finished and approved.
  • Rule 16 MARC DECIDES: Sunset of Competition goes live all 26 episodes at once. Marc's release of it counts as his approval of each episode.
  • Rule 34 MARC DECIDES: Only Marc releases the hold. Claude or Orion may turn it on to stop test content or a wrong publish, then must tell Marc at once.
  • Rule 42 MARC DECIDES: A live story with a problem stays live unless Marc says otherwise ("After the Last Train" stays up).
  • Rule 45 MARC DECIDES: A partly published series breaks rule 11. On finding one, do not publish more single episodes. Either finish all episodes and publish them…
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. The publish switch (Review or Direct)

  1. There is one publish switch with two settings: Review (rfr) and Direct (direct). There is no per-story setting and no per-story question. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4, Marc Oct 4, 2026)
  2. The switch is checked at the moment a story is ready to publish, not when it was started. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md "What listeners can see" 4, Marc Nov 8)
  3. MARC DECIDES Review: every story waits at Ready for Review until Marc listens and approves. Then it goes live. — Agreed (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md, Marc Nov 8)
  4. Direct: stories go live without Marc's review. There is no listen after going live either; nothing may assume Marc will catch bad audio. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4, option A, Marc Oct 4 10:34 and 10:35 EDT)
  5. MARC DECIDES Only Marc changes the switch, with a one-line instruction or the Admin page switch. It stays until he changes it again. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4; Admin Command Center switch, migration 20261031173118)
  6. The current setting is Direct (set Oct 11; Marc Oct 27: "publish stories directly to the app, not to Ready for Review"). — Agreed (memory /projects/…/areas/story-pipeline.md Oct 27; atlas_settings row read Nov 9)
  7. If the switch can't be read, hold at Review. If no setting exists, use Direct. — In force (code) (lib/publishMode.ts getPublishMode)
  8. No setting weakens a quality check. All checks pass first; the switch only decides whether Marc reviews. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rules 2 and 4)
  9. MARC DECIDES In Review, corrections follow the Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends fixes → the fixed version comes to him as a link, not published → he approves → only then it replaces or publishes. — Agreed (Episode Correction Loop, Marc Aug 21, 2026, PERMANENT; PIPELINE-CANON Rule 4 scope)
  10. The first story ever published by Direct mode is marked PUBLISH-MODE-DIRECT-FIRST-PUBLISH in the log so Marc can check it. — In force (code) (lib/publishMode.ts FIRST_PUBLISH_MARKER)

B. All episodes publish together

  1. MARC DECIDES A story goes live complete, with all its episodes at once. A series stays hidden until every episode is finished and approved. — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION RULE, Oct 4; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md, Marc Nov 8)
  2. No 1-episode series is ever live. — Agreed (Marc Nov 8, 2026, memory story-pipeline.md and hook-series.md)
  3. A series flips live once, after the finale passes, under the switch setting at that moment. It is never split (some episodes Review, some live). — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON Rule 3 and Rule 4 defaults)
  4. "Every episode" means the planned total (series_total_episodes). A series with fewer episode rows than planned does not publish. — Proposed (fills gap: publish code checks only rows that exist, see Enforcement)
  5. Hook-first ad series launch as a 7-episode Season 1, all 7 published together. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON HOOK-SERIES RULE, Marc Nov 5)
  6. MARC DECIDES Sunset of Competition goes live all 26 episodes at once. Marc's release of it counts as his approval of each episode. — Agreed (Marc Nov 3, memory sunset-of-competition.md; lib/story-gates.ts AUTHOR-WRITTEN-RELEASE-001, Nov 4)
  7. Adding episodes to a live series: new episodes are produced, then published together as one batch, after the last live episode. Original episodes stay locked. — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION RULE part 2; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md 5)
  8. One addition order = one batch. No early release of single new episodes. — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION defaults)
  9. If unclear whether an episode is part of the first release or an addition, treat it as the first release (publish together). — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION defaults)
  10. The old SERIES-RELEASE-RULE v2 (early release with a 3-episode buffer, July 11) is retired and is not canon. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON registry, retired Nov 9; docs/PLAYER-RULES.md open item)

C. Episode numbering

  1. Episodes are numbered 1, 2, 3 … N. Never 0, no gaps, no repeats. A single story is Episode 1. — Agreed (EPISODE-NUMBERING RULE, Marc Oct 4)
  2. Numbering is checked before publish and blocks. A bad sequence is fixed to 1..N first. — Agreed (EPISODE-NUMBERING defaults); In force (code) (lib/story-gates.ts assertSeriesContiguity)
  3. If an episode is cut before publish, the numbers close up so the live list has no hole. — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION and EPISODE-NUMBERING defaults)
  4. Additions continue from the last live number (N+1, N+2 …). Live episodes are never renumbered. — Agreed (EPISODE-ADDITION; EPISODE-NUMBERING)

D. Live, hidden and the publish record

  1. A story is live only when status = published, is_hidden = false and published_on is set. — In force (code) (lib/directPublish.ts isListenerVisible, PUBLISH-VISIBLE-001)
  2. Hidden episodes never appear in lists, navigation or autoplay. — Agreed (docs/PLAYER-RULES.md)
  3. Before going live, a story must have: title, author, genre, final audio, cover, description, length, Belle announcement audio, and pass the Belle copy, Belle freshness and name-personalization checks. — In force (code) (lib/story-gates.ts, lib/publishReadiness.ts, lib/publicationBelleGate.ts, lib/belleFreshness.ts, lib/personalization/publishGuard.ts)
  4. Going live is two recorded steps: ready_for_review → approved_ready → published. There is no shortcut. Each step writes an audit row (who, when, why). — In force (code) (lib/directPublish.ts; lib/workflowTransitions.ts; ORION-GOV-006)
  5. A packaging run never hides a live story. — In force (code) (complete-story-package/route.ts PACKAGE-NO-UNPUBLISH-001, after Nanny Cam EP5 and Chicago EP7, Oct 27–29)
  6. If a live story is re-hidden by a re-run, it is made visible again with its original publish date. — In force (code) (lib/directPublish.ts restoreVisibility)
  7. After any publish, check that every episode is live 5 minutes later, finale included, and say so with database proof. — Proposed (practice in "Clearing CEO series flag" chat; not written as a rule)

E. Publication hold (global stop)

  1. The publication hold stops every publish (Review or Direct) until released. Every publish path checks it right before writing. — In force (code) (lib/publicationHold.ts, PUBLICATION-HOLD-001, Marc Oct 23)
  2. If the hold can't be read, nothing publishes. — In force (code) (lib/publicationHold.ts)
  3. MARC DECIDES Only Marc releases the hold. Claude or Orion may turn it on to stop test content or a wrong publish, then must tell Marc at once. — Proposed (Claude set it Nov 2 to stop a test series and Marc was told; never written as a rule)
  4. Test content is never published. — Proposed (cited as "your brief says not to publish test content", chat "Clearing CEO series flag"; no written rule found)

F. Unpublish, rollback and cold storage

  1. Unpublishing a live story moves it to unpublished_library (hidden). It never deletes audio, cover or text. — In force (code) (lib/workflowTransitions.ts: published → unpublished_library)
  2. A series is unpublished as a whole, never one episode, so listeners never see a series with missing episodes. — Proposed (follows rule 11; no rule covers unpublishing)
  3. A live story goes to cold storage only by deliberate "retire" action. — In force (code) (lib/workflowTransitions.ts transitionAllowed retire flag)
  4. Cold storage means retired. A cold-storage story is never dispatched, produced or shown. Bringing it back goes only through the "recover from cold storage" action, which resets its review fields and sends it to Ready for Review. — In force (code) (lib/workflowTransitions.ts)
  5. Retiring stalled or outdated work goes to cold storage, not deletion (69 stalled stories, Oct 2026; early-October queue, Nov 1). — Agreed (Marc, memory /areas/story-pipeline.md; Nov 1 memory story-pipeline.md)
  6. Improving an old published story is a separate "Remaster" job. New production never touches a live episode. — Proposed (Marc Nov 7 asked for a way to pull and reprocess old stories; Story Production Spec §10 is a draft, "do not implement")
  7. MARC DECIDES A live story with a problem stays live unless Marc says otherwise ("After the Last Train" stays up). — Agreed (Marc Nov 8, PIPELINE-CANON STORY-CLARITY scope)

G. needs_attention flag

  1. needs_attention means a person must look. While set, the story or its whole series is not dispatched. It always carries a plain reason. — In force (code) (dispatch-queue/route.ts Gate A)
  2. Clearing needs_attention requires the cause to be fixed and the fix named in the reason field. — Proposed (fills gap: who may clear the flag is not written)

H. Partly published stories (rule breaks)

  1. MARC DECIDES A partly published series breaks rule 11. On finding one, do not publish more single episodes. Either finish all episodes and publish them together, or hide the live part. Marc chooses. — Proposed (Rerouted, Weekend Wife and other hook series had Episode 1 live alone, Nov 6–9; SERIES-CONTINUATION RULE rationale)
  2. The single-episode publish path must refuse series episodes unless it publishes the rest of the series in the same action. — Proposed (code today allows one episode once earlier ones are live: app/api/admin/publish-story/route.ts single path)

I. Approval records and story history

  1. Each story should carry an approval record: source job, version number and date, new or redo, redo reason, what changed, why it entered review, why it is blocked. — Proposed (docs/CONTENT_APPROVAL_PROVENANCE.md v1.0, planning only)
  2. The review screen shows the whole series, expected vs present episodes and missing numbers, never only the rows in one tab. — Proposed (docs/CONTENT_APPROVAL_PROVENANCE.md)
  3. Each story should carry a history label: legacy, canonical, experimental, incomplete, blocked, hidden, deprecated, redo or orphaned. A label describes history, not whether it is live. — Proposed (docs/STORY_LINEAGE_AND_CLASSIFICATION.md v1.0, planning only)
  4. A redo shows the version it replaces. The old version is kept for history. — Proposed (docs/STORY_LINEAGE_AND_CLASSIFICATION.md)

J. Checking it worked

  1. library-new is the place to check that a story is truly live. — Agreed (AGENTS.md "library-new is the current verification surface"; DONE_CHECKLIST.md "visible in library-new")

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 1: Hook series ads start when? Nov 6 said "after Episodes 2 and 3 are live"; Nov 8 said all 7 episodes publish together. Decided: ads start only after all 7 Season 1 episodes are live. (09 C1, 13 C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 2: Hook Episode 1s that are already live alone (Rerouted and the others). Decided: leave them up; publish Episodes 2 to 7 together; no more single episodes. (09 Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 4: Episode length. Decided: standalones within ±10% of target; series episodes between the 12.5-minute floor and 1.35 × the brief; speaking rate 160 words per minute everywhere. Publish code uses the same numbers (today it only allows 15–20 minutes). (02 C5, 03 C3, 08 C2, 09 C4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 20: One episode fails mid-series. Decided: the whole series holds and you're told; nothing in it publishes. (01 Q4, 09 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 24: Gemini's final read. Decided: report-only until it agrees with you on 9 of 10 series, then it must pass before a Direct publish. (01 Q2, 09 C2, Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 44: No episode goes live alone. Decided: every publish path refuses to publish part of a series (today the manual publish can). (09 conflict 1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 45: Who may unpublish. Decided: only you, except that Claude may hide a story with broken audio at once and tell you. (09 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 88: The old production process and Series Release Rule become history; PIPELINE-CANON's rule titles get corrected. (09 C3, C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 89: Test stories carry a "test" mark, and every publish path refuses them. (09 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

Marc Nov 5 HOOK-SERIES RULE and Nov 8: all 7 episodes publish together, no 1-episode stories live. Recommendation: Nov 8 wins; ads start only after all 7 are live. Marc decides.

Marc Oct 26 chose series episodes 12–18 minutes, and Pocket FM-style episodes are 12–15 minutes. Recommendation: the length rule belongs to CANON-03/08; publish code should read it from there. Marc decides the numbers.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 88, Marc Nov 9, 2026] PIPELINE-CANON Rule 2's cross-reference in EPISODE-ADDITION calls Rule 2 "no silent /tmp QC" and Rule 1 "no partial passes"; the real titles are "Quality Gates Block" and "Block Classification". Recommendation: fix the wording in PIPELINE-CANON.

title: CANON-10 — Covers, Images & eBooks
status: **APPROVED** (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)
summary: how cover art is made, checked, remade and paid for; author and narrator photos; the eBook text (`prose_text`) that goes with every story.
body:
Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: how cover art is made, checked, remade and paid for; author and narrator photos; the eBook text (prose_text) that goes with every story. Does not cover: ad images and ad creative (marketing canon), when a story goes live (CANON-09), story writing (CANON-03).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 13 MARC DECIDES: A cover darker than 100 out of 255 is remade once brighter. If still too dark, it is flagged for Marc.
  • Rule 20 MARC DECIDES: Bulk remakes need Marc's OK on the list and the cost first.
  • Rule 27 MARC DOES: Marc tops up image credits himself. No key or card number is ever sent in chat. Image spend is charged to the ET-R&D card, or ET-Marketing for ad…
  • Rule 33 MARC DECIDES: Applies to new production only. Stories published before Oct 4, 2026 are not forced back. Backfill is a separate order from Marc.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. When covers are made

  1. Every episode has its own cover (stories.cover_url). — In force (code) (app/api/asc3/regenerate-cover/route.ts writes per story id)
  2. Cover making never blocks audio work. Covers are made early and in parallel; a failed cover does not stop packaging. — In force (code) (COVER-PIPELINE-DECOUPLE-001, Marc directive Oct 8, 2026; COVER-PIPELINE-REGRESSION-20261008.md)
  3. No story goes live without a cover. — In force (code) (lib/story-gates.ts and lib/publishReadiness.ts require cover_url; READY-PUBLISH-URLS-001, Marc Oct 5)
  4. A failed cover retries up to 3 times; after 2 failures an alert is logged. — In force (code) (lib/cover/coverRetry.ts COVER_MAX_RETRIES = 3)

B. What a cover shows

  1. The cover shows this story. Its picture comes only from the story text (eBook text first, then script), the description and the brief. Never from hidden production notes such as the "STORY RESOLUTION MAP" block. — Agreed (COVER-STORY-OBJECT-001, PR #491 merged Nov 5 after Marc's map report; lib/coverPrompt.ts stripProductionNotes)
  2. No maps, charts, blueprints or survey papers unless the story names a map at least twice. — Agreed (Marc Nov 4–5 cover-map report and remake approval; COVER-NO-KEYS-001, PR #505; lib/coverPrompt.ts)
  3. No keys, key rings or a person holding up a key unless the story names a key at least twice. — Agreed (Marc Nov 6: "all the covers someone is holding a key … same problem"; COVER-NO-KEYS-001, PR #505)
  4. The story prop is picked by whole words only ("ring" never matches "during"). — In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts inferKeyObjectSymbol)
  5. No text, words, letters or numbers in the image. The app adds titles. — In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts; text overlay turned off in regenerate-cover)
  6. Keep the bottom-right corner clear of faces, text and focal points. — Agreed (memory /areas/story-pipeline.md "Cover art prompts: keep bottom-right corner clear"); In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts)
  7. Readable as a phone thumbnail (about 100 × 100 pixels): one clear subject, a visible face when there is a person, focal point in the center or upper half, square image. — In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts ENDLESS_TALES_COVER_STANDARD)
  8. Bright by default. Only Horror may be darker, and even Horror keeps the subject lit and readable. — In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts isDarkExceptionStory; docs/GENRE-ATTRIBUTES-SPEC-v1.0-DRAFT.md §3, a draft)
  9. MARC DECIDES A cover darker than 100 out of 255 is remade once brighter. If still too dark, it is flagged for Marc. — In force (code) (regenerate-cover/route.ts LUMINANCE_THRESHOLD)
  10. Genre styles: thriller = bright close-ups; mystery = moody but readable; horror = gothic with lit subject; romance = warm, intimate; sci-fi = big scale, clear forms; western = golden dust, strong foreground figure; heartwarming = cozy and warm; and so on per lib/coverPrompt.ts genreStyle. — In force (code) (lib/coverPrompt.ts)
  11. Sunset of Competition covers never show space suits or metal-looking robots. Its "robots" look human. — Agreed (Marc canon Nov 6, memory sunset-of-competition.md)
  12. Covers in one series should not all look alike, and should not repeat a prop or setting used on recent covers. — Proposed (fills gap: Marc's Nov 4 report "stories feel alike" and claude/cover-and-theme-repetition-2026-11-04.md; no rule exists)
  13. Remove "clue-objects" and "Da Vinci Code" from the mystery style, since that wording also draws maps. — Proposed (finding in claude/cover-and-theme-repetition-2026-11-04.md, seen via chat; not fixed in code)

C. Remaking covers (regenerate-cover)

  1. Covers are remade only through /api/asc3/regenerate-cover, with plain feedback (for example "No maps, charts or diagrams"). The feedback becomes the top instruction. — In force (code) (regenerate-cover/route.ts; lib/coverPrompt.ts coverFeedback)
  2. Keep every old cover file. A remake saves a new file; nothing is overwritten. — Agreed (Marc's remake approvals Nov 5: "Keep every old file"); In force (code) (time-stamped storage path)
  3. MARC DECIDES Bulk remakes need Marc's OK on the list and the cost first. — Agreed (Marc approved the 45-cover remake, about $6.77, Nov 5 10:26; chat "Apple App Store commission deals")
  4. After a bulk remake, Gemini checks each new cover; one more try if it still fails, then Marc is told. Send Marc before/after samples. — Agreed (Marc-approved cover cleanup handoff, chat "Cover story map pattern", Nov 5)
  5. A remade cover on a live story replaces it at once. Record the old cover link so it can be put back. — Proposed (code overwrites cover_url with no record of the old link)
  6. Claude cannot see images from its sandbox; any check of what a cover shows is done by Gemini vision and labeled as such. — Proposed (working practice Nov 4–5)

D. Image service and image credits

  1. The cover image model is gpt-image-1.5 through OpenAI. DALL·E 3 is retired. The model can be changed only by setting, not code. — In force (code) (lib/cover/imageRouter.ts COVER-GPT-IMAGE-DEFAULT-001, Oct 22)
  2. Belle is voice only; no image is ever made "by Belle". — In force (code) (lib/cover/imageRouter.ts assertNotBelleImageAgent)
  3. Every image call logs its cost for the finance report. — In force (code) (regenerate-cover/route.ts logDalleCall)
  4. MARC DOES Marc tops up image credits himself. No key or card number is ever sent in chat. Image spend is charged to the ET-R&D card, or ET-Marketing for ad images. — Agreed (Marc Nov 5, chat "Apple App Store commission deals"; AGENTS.md "Never open, print … tokens")
  5. Report 101 flags any image service that is low (under $10 or under 3 days left) with a link to add credits. — Agreed (Marc Nov 5, report-101 skill)
  6. Each image service the pipeline uses is named in writing (cover renderer, Hal's image tool), so credits can be found. — Proposed (Hal's image service was unknown on Nov 5)

E. Author and narrator photos

  1. Every pen-name author and narrator has a photo. They are invented people: the prompt says so and never names the real author they write like. — Agreed (Marc Nov 1, 2026, memory story-pipeline.md); In force (code) (lib/portraitPrompt.ts PORTRAITS-001)

F. eBooks (prose_text)

  1. Every story has a complete eBook before it is finished. It covers every episode in the release, not an excerpt. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON EBOOK-COMPLETENESS RULE, Marc Oct 4)
  2. A missing or incomplete eBook blocks both Ready for Review and publishing. In Direct mode the publish check is the last line of defense. — Agreed (EBOOK-COMPLETENESS)
  3. MARC DECIDES Applies to new production only. Stories published before Oct 4, 2026 are not forced back. Backfill is a separate order from Marc. — Agreed (EBOOK-COMPLETENESS scope)
  4. Added episodes need their eBook text before the batch can be reviewed or published. — Agreed (EBOOK-COMPLETENESS defaults)
  5. If it is unclear whether the eBook is complete, treat it as incomplete. — Agreed (EBOOK-COMPLETENESS defaults)
  6. The eBook reads as a real book, never a transcript: no speaker labels, episode markers, "[NARRATOR]" or "[LISTENER_NAME]" tokens, sound or music cues, or "previously on" recaps. The reader must never be able to tell the audio came first. — Agreed (PIPELINE-CANON EBOOK-STYLE RULE, Marc Oct 4)
  7. Same story as the audio: same plot, people and events. Only the form changes. — Agreed (EBOOK-STYLE scope)
  8. When an authored book already exists (for example Origin 2.0), use it as written. Do not rewrite it. — Agreed (EBOOK-STYLE use-the-original clause, Marc Oct 4 15:34)
  9. A transcript-style eBook fails and blocks, and goes back to the writer for a rewrite (Class B). — Agreed (EBOOK-STYLE defaults)
  10. The eBook text is remade whenever the script changes. Old text from an earlier script is never kept. — Proposed (code skips prose generation if prose_text already exists: complete-story-package/route.ts)
  11. The eBook writer is told to write book prose, not "keep dialogue … preserve the story" conversion. — Proposed (the current prompt in complete-story-package/route.ts generateProse asks for a cleaned script, which conflicts with rule 36)
  12. The eBook is checked for leftover script marks (labels, brackets, cue words) before review. — Proposed (fills the missing style gate for rules 36 and 39)
  13. The eBook is checked for length against the script (for example at least 70% of the script's spoken words) so a cut-off text fails. — Proposed (the generator caps output at 4,000 tokens; a long episode could be cut off with no check)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 46: Series cover. Decided: the Library shows one series cover (Episode 1's, unless you pick another). (10 C4, Q1) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 47: eBooks. Decided: rewrite the eBook prompt to produce real book prose, and make the publish check require the eBook. (10 C1, C2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 90: A missing cover blocks publishing, but not Ready for Review. (10 C3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 91: In Direct mode, Marc does not review covers; Gemini checks each one for maps, keys, text and darkness. (10 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 92: One eBook text per episode, shown as one book in the reader. (10 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 93: eBooks for stories published before Oct 4 are made only for stories that stay live, as a separate low-priority order. (10 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 94: Keep the old cover's link so Marc can switch back. (10 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 47, Marc Nov 9, 2026] EBOOK-STYLE (Oct 4) says the eBook must read as a genuine book. The code prompt (complete-story-package/route.ts) says "convert this audio drama script into clean readable prose … keep story meaning and dialogue … preserve the story", using a small model (claude-haiku-4-5, 4,000 tokens). Recommendation: canon wins; rewrite the prompt and add the style check (rules 41–42). Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 47, Marc Nov 9, 2026] EBOOK-COMPLETENESS says the publish gate blocks a missing eBook. The publish checks (lib/story-gates.ts _publishMissingFields, lib/directPublish.ts) do not check prose_text; only Ready for Review does. Recommendation: add prose_text to the publish check.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 90, Marc Nov 9, 2026] READY-PUBLISH-URLS-001 (Oct 5) made a missing cover block "publish-ready". COVER-PIPELINE-DECOUPLE-001 (Oct 8) made a missing cover only a warning at Ready for Review. They fit together only if the cover blocks at publish and not before; that is how the code works today. Recommendation: confirm that reading (rule 3). Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 46, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Covers are made per episode, but a series also has a series cover (Nov 5 handoff: "Re-upload The Third Key series cover"). No rule says where the series cover comes from or which one the Library shows. Recommendation: see Q1.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 46, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should a series show one series cover in the Library and episode covers inside? Suggested answer: yes; the series cover is Episode 1's cover unless Marc picks another.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 91, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should Marc see new covers before a story goes live in Direct mode? Suggested answer: no; Gemini vision checks for maps, keys, text and darkness, and fails the cover if found.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 92, Marc Nov 9, 2026] One eBook per series, or one per episode joined in the reader? Suggested answer: one per episode in the database, shown as one book in the reader.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 93, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Backfill eBooks for stories published before Oct 4? Suggested answer: only for stories that stay live, as a separate low-priority order.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 94, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Should an old cover be kept in the app's history so Marc can switch back? Suggested answer: yes, store the old link (rule 22).

Enforcement status

  • 1–4, 8–9, 11–14, 18, 24–26, 30 → enforced in code at the paths given.
  • 5–7 → enforced: lib/coverPrompt.ts (PR #491, #505). Old covers cleaned by the 45–56-cover remake, Nov 5 (count per chat; not re-verified).
  • 10 → enforced in prompt text only (image models may not follow it).
  • 15 → not enforced in code (no Sunset-specific cover rule found).
  • 16, 17, 22, 23, 29 → not enforced.
  • 19 → enforced (new time-stamped file each remake); old link not recorded.
  • 20, 21, 27, 28 → by practice and report-101 skill.
  • 31–32 → partly: blocks at Ready for Review (run-next missingReadyForReviewFields, complete-story-package missingReviewReadyFields); not at publish (C2). No series-wide completeness check.
  • 33–35 → not enforced as separate checks.
  • 36–39, 40–43 → not enforced (no eBook style or length gate exists).

Sources reviewed

  • /tmp/dtt: docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md (EBOOK rules), lib/coverPrompt.ts, lib/cover/coverRetry.ts, lib/cover/imageRouter.ts, lib/portraitPrompt.ts, app/api/asc3/regenerate-cover/route.ts, app/api/admin/complete-story-package/route.ts, app/api/admin/production-jobs/run-next/route.ts, lib/story-gates.ts, lib/publishReadiness.ts, app/api/story-publish/route.ts, COVER-PIPELINE-REGRESSION-20261008.md, docs/GENRE-ATTRIBUTES-SPEC-v1.0-DRAFT.md, docs/PUBLISHED_STORY_SPEC.md.

  • Chats: "Cover story map pattern" (Nov 4–8; contains the text of claude/cover-and-theme-repetition-2026-11-04.md), "Apple App Store commission deals" (Nov 5, cover remake and image credits).
  • Not reachable directly: Claude project docs (no Projects tool); claude/cover-and-theme-repetition-2026-11-04.md was read only as quoted in chat.
