Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: the Admin → Finance statement (revenue, expenses, plow back, cost per episode, LTV, Mercury reconciliation, profit suggestions, overview tiles); expense categories; Mercury cards; spending limits. Does not cover: ad approval, CAC test rules and ad creative (CANON-13 Marketing & Ads); agent roles and AI-credit alerts (CANON-15 Agents & Operations); story production (PIPELINE-CANON).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 52 MARC DECIDES: Susan may use the marketing card only with Marc's approval.
  • Rule 59 MARC DECIDES: No automatic profit transfers. Any transfer needs Marc's explicit word.
  • Decision 125 MARC DECIDES: What Marc reinvests from Part B (money outside operations), and when, is his choice.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. The statement page

  1. The financial statement lives in Admin → Finance → Statement and follows Marc's own template (SS1). — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  2. It has a Cash flow / Accrual selector. Cash counts money on the day it moved in Mercury. Accrual spreads money over the time it pays for. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; lib/finance/statement.ts)
  3. It has a period selector: 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, custom, and actual monthly (one column per month of operation). — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  4. Monthly history starts April 2026, the first Mercury month. Mercury history is copied into the app database. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  5. Every expense category has its own subtotal. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  6. Expense sections are: Operating, Production, Ad Spend, Marketing Services, R & D, plus Uncategorized. — Agreed (Nov 8: Ad Spend separate from Marketing Services, memory admin-finance-page.md; lib/finance/statement.ts)
  7. Ad Spend has a drop-down that shows each campaign's cost, dates, trials, subscriptions and CAC. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; code lib/finance/statement.ts campaigns)
  8. Stories published are shown apart from stories in the pipeline. A story counts as published only when all its episodes are live; partly published stories are flagged. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; commit a0d297d)
  9. Clicking "Stories published" lists the titles with their episode counts. Clicking "Production cost per episode" lists each AI or service and what Marc paid it. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  10. Clickable numbers, links and buttons are dark navy #002266, in light and dark mode. No light blue anywhere. — In force (code) (app/admin/finance/statement/page.tsx; commits ff58e8c, 2da8d81)
  11. A missing number shows "Unavailable", never $0. — In force (code) (app/admin/command-ui.tsx; CommandCenter banner "Unavailable never means zero")

B. Revenue

  1. All subscription money goes on two lines only: Annual subs and Monthly subs. There is no separate "Stripe payouts" revenue line. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  2. Subscription revenue comes from the Stripe ledger: every charge, refund and fee. — Agreed (Nov 8 finance session; commit 51fd5a2; lib/finance/stripe-sync.ts)
  3. Stripe payouts into Mercury are transfers, not revenue. They show below the statement only to reconcile. — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts)
  4. Marc's own test-account payments were real money, so they count as revenue. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  5. Refunds and disputes are negative, on their own line. On accrual they spread like the charge they reverse. — Agreed (refunds net, memory admin-finance-page.md); spreading In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts)
  6. Total revenue is net: subscriptions minus cancellations and refunds, plus interest income. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  7. Interest income is Mercury bank interest only. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  8. Card cashback rewards get their own revenue line. — Agreed (Nov 8 finance session; commit 51fd5a2, lib/finance/statement.ts CASHBACK_ITEM)
  9. "Other (not yet categorized)" holds incoming money with no rule yet, so it can be spotted and classified. Incoming money is never assumed to be revenue. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; lib/finance/statement.ts)
  10. On accrual, an annual charge spreads over 12 months and a monthly charge over 1 month. — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts)
  11. Owner deposits, loans, card payments and moves between Mercury accounts are not revenue or expense. — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts notes; app/admin/CommandCenter.tsx)
  12. Stripe fees are an Operating expense. — In force (code) (commit 51fd5a2)

C. Plow back (money for ads)

  1. Plow back = 75% of the previous calendar month's profit (positive cash flow). If that month lost money, plow back is $0. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; lib/finance/statement.ts "Marc, Nov 8 2026, revised")
  2. Plow back is shown as a memo line, "Available for ads." It is never revenue and never added to totals. — Agreed (same source)
  3. The current month shows the full plow back from day one (not spread by days). — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts; commit 10e3e0c)
  4. The other 25% of profit stays in the business. No money moves automatically. — Proposed (code shows "retained" = 25% but no rule says what it is for; profit transfers are locked in code)

D. Production cost

  1. Production cost per episode sits in the Volume & Productivity section. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  2. Cost is per FINISHED episode: voiced, published or not. Finished but unreleased episodes carry their own cost. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; commit d5f1095)
  3. ElevenLabs is a subscription, but each story's voice cost comes from the credits that story used × the plan price per credit. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  4. The ElevenLabs plan price is entered by hand ($330 a month) and beats the "next invoice" amount. — In force (code) (lib/finance/elevenlabs-sync.ts, commit 1f63aeb); the $330 value comes from the coordinator brief and sits in the database, not the repo.
  5. Sound Ideas ($1,500 a year) is charged as $125 a month ÷ that month's finished episodes. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  6. Other yearly purchases also spread over their term in cost per episode, on both bases. — In force (code) (commit a0d297d)
  7. Prepaid AI credits (Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google) count when bought, on both bases, until usage feeds exist. — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts notes)

E. LTV and other measures

  1. LTV is a measure, not an expense. It stays blank ("Unavailable") until there is a real CAC and real churn. No assumed figures. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  2. LTV = average monthly revenue per real subscriber ÷ monthly churn (real cancellations over the last 3 months). — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts; commit 6dce632)
  3. Test accounts never count in subscriber numbers, churn, LTV or CAC (they do count as revenue, rule 15). — In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts)
  4. Admin overview tiles: LTV comes right after churn, and LTV : CAC sits beside it. Both show only when real. — In force (code) (commits caf35d7, 1c5d621)

F. Matching the bank

  1. The statement must match Mercury to the cent. The "Unexplained" line must be $0.00. — Agreed (Nov 8: reconcile with Mercury, memory admin-finance-page.md); $0.00 check In force (code) (lib/finance/statement.ts recon)
  2. Reconciliation lists every Mercury dollar by kind (owner money, Stripe payouts, cashback, interest, uncategorized, refunds, expenses, owner withdrawals, internal moves) and the costs paid outside Mercury. — In force (code) (commit ad4a71c)
  3. Bart reconciles the books each month and reports anything in "Other" or "Unexplained." — Proposed (Bart is the finance agent, memory agent-fleet.md, but no task is set)

G. Profit suggestions

  1. Claude suggests ways to raise profit without lowering story quality: never cheaper or fewer voices, a weaker script model, shorter episodes, fewer checks or less sound design. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md; lib/finance/suggestions.ts)
  2. Each month Claude gives 5–7 suggestions, each tied to numbers on the statement, with a dollar estimate or what to measure. — In force (code) (lib/finance/suggestions.ts)
  3. Each suggestion has Up, Down and Delete buttons. These can reorder or remove, never add new text. — In force (code) (commit 709a1a8)

H. Spending categories and cards

  1. All spending falls in four groups: Story Production, Marketing, Operating Expenses, R&D. — Agreed (Nov 2, memory business-expenses.md, business-spending.md)
  2. Story Production: pipeline AI (Anthropic API for story writing, OpenAI for covers, DeepSeek R1 and V3), ElevenLabs, Sound Ideas, Soundsnap, Kie.ai music and similar. — Agreed (Nov 2, memory business-expenses.md, business-spending.md)
  3. Marketing: Susan, part of Strategos, Meta, later TikTok. Operating: subscriptions like Vercel and Supabase. R&D: Marc's own chats with Claude, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. — Agreed (same source; memory admin-finance-page.md)
  4. Anthropic use for R&D and for story writing are kept apart. — Agreed (Nov 2, memory business-expenses.md)
  5. Strategos (DeepSeek R1) is split between Marketing and Story Production. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory admin-finance-page.md)
  6. Mercury has one virtual card per spending group (4 made Nov 2), replacing one card per service. — Agreed (Nov 2, memory business-spending.md, business-banking.md)
  7. Marketing gets two cards: one for ad spend only, one for marketing services and tools. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory business-spending.md)
  8. MARC DECIDES Susan may use the marketing card only with Marc's approval. — Agreed (Nov 2, memory business-expenses.md, endless-tales-finances.md)
  9. The $4,000 Meta test money sits in its own Mercury marketing account with a Meta debit card. — Agreed (chat "Meta campaign testing plan", Oct 30)
  10. Every vendor charge must be billed to the card of its spending group, so the statement can sort it by card. — Proposed (card switch still in progress, claude/mercury-card-switch-checklist.md)

I. Spending limits

  1. No new expenses (for example, a cloud server for Orion) until the Meta test proves a CAC of about $30 or less. — Agreed (Nov 7, memory business-spending.md)
  2. Susan's Claude key for ad copy is capped at $25 a month. — Agreed (Nov 8, memory agent-fleet.md)
  3. ElevenLabs extra-use (overage) cap is 200,000 credits. — Agreed (Nov 5, memory audio-pipeline.md, project copy)
  4. No agent holds a tool that can send money. Bart's Mercury access is read-only. — Agreed for Bart read-only (memory /areas/endless-tales-platform.md); Proposed for all agents (Nov 5 Marc removed Mercury from Orion on Claude's advice)
  5. MARC DECIDES No automatic profit transfers. Any transfer needs Marc's explicit word. — In force (code) (app/admin/CommandCenter.tsx: transfer buttons locked)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 57: Plow back. Marc's decision: the plow-back percentage is a setting that starts at 75%; only Marc changes it, each change is recorded with its date and applies from the next month on. Plow back = that percentage of the previous month's profit ($0 after a loss month), shown as one number ("Available for ads"). The Command Center reads the same setting. The rest stays as reserve. Minimum cash reserve: $5,000 or 90 days of spending, whichever is larger. (13 C8, 14 C3, C4, Q1, Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 58: Revenue details. Decided: Test-account payments count as revenue but not in subscriber counts, churn, LTV or CAC. Sound Ideas cost is 1/12 of what was paid for the current year. Refunds count on the day they leave Mercury. (14 C1, C7, Q6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 111: Retire the old LTV numbers and the old $59.99 price everywhere. (14 C2, C6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 112: Five spending sections on the statement: Operations, Story Production, Ad Spend, Marketing Services, R&D. Replaced by decision 125 (Marc, Nov 9, 2026) for how the statement is laid out. (14 C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 113: In a month with no finished episodes, the $125 Sound Ideas charge shows as unassigned production cost. (14 Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 114: Bart closes each month (reconcile, clear "Other", report) by the 5th of the next month. (14 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 115: Show AI agent costs per agent once usage logging exists. (14 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 125: Statement layout. Part A, profit: (1) Revenue is sales only: monthly and annual subscriptions and one-time purchases, less refunds = net revenue. (2) Cost of revenue: story production (voices, the Claude story pipeline, Gemini screening, OpenAI voice checks and covers, music, sound effects), delivering audio to listeners (the AWS server and Supabase database and storage), and payment fees (Stripe, later Apple and Google). (3) Gross profit and gross margin %. (4) Operating expenses: Ad Spend, Marketing Services, R&D, Operations. (5) Operating profit. Plow back is the plow-back percentage of the previous month's operating profit. Part B, money outside operations, never profit and never in plow back: money put in by the owner or investors (one line per person with a running total), owner withdrawals, card cashback, Mercury interest, and money in with no category yet; total = "yours to keep or reinvest". MARC DECIDES What Marc reinvests from Part B, and when, is his choice. Replaces decision 112's five spending sections and rules 45–47 for how the statement is laid out; the Mercury cards stay as they are. (CANON-99 item 125) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 3)

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 57, Marc Nov 9, 2026] What happens to the 25% of profit not plowed back? Suggested answer: it stays as cash reserve until you move it by hand.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 113, Marc Nov 9, 2026] In a month with no finished episodes, where does the $125 Sound Ideas charge go? Suggested answer: show it as unassigned production cost that month.

  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 58, Marc Nov 9, 2026] When does a refund count on cash basis: the day issued or the day it left Mercury? Suggested answer: the day it left Mercury.

Status: APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve canon 01–15") · Owner: Marc · Changes only through CANON-99 (CANON-00 rules 10–16)

Covers: who the agents are and what each may do; approvals for merges, database changes and deploys; how Claude talks to Marc and to agents; Telegram; watchdogs and alerts; security of keys and routes; which documents are law. Does not cover: story production steps (PIPELINE-CANON and story rules); the player and listener app (PLAYER-RULES); ad approval (CANON-13); money and the statement (CANON-14).

Where Marc decides

Every rule in this document that needs Marc. MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). The same tag marks each rule below.

  • Rule 1 MARC DECIDES: Only the documents in the AGENTS.md "Canon index" are law. Everything else is history or reference. When two canon documents disagree, ask Marc.
  • Rule 2 MARC DECIDES: No agent declares canon. Canon changes only on Marc's explicit word.
  • Rule 3 MARC DECIDES: Never merge a pull request (PR) without Marc's explicit word.
  • Rule 5 MARC DECIDES: Never run a database migration or schema change without Marc's explicit OK.
  • Rule 8 MARC DECIDES: Stop and ask Marc when a step could overwrite or hide live content.
  • Rule 10 MARC DECIDES: No crontab hold line (#HOLD-…) or paused service is turned back on without Marc's word.
  • Rule 54 MARC DOES: Marc enters money-spending keys himself (for example Meta ads_management). Low-risk test keys may be passed through Orion.
  • Decision 118 MARC DECIDES: Orion's INCIDENT-RULE-001 is Proposed until Marc approves it.
  • Still open: nothing. Every conflict and question below is RESOLVED (CANON-99 Parts 1 and 2, Nov 9, 2026).

Rules

A. What is law

  1. MARC DECIDES Only the documents in the AGENTS.md "Canon index" are law. Everything else is history or reference. When two canon documents disagree, ask Marc. — Agreed (AGENTS.md; commit 2683da9, Nov 9)
  2. MARC DECIDES No agent declares canon. Canon changes only on Marc's explicit word. — Agreed (memory bell-meta-marketing.md standing rules; governance/ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001.md change control)

B. Approvals

  1. MARC DECIDES Never merge a pull request (PR) without Marc's explicit word. — Agreed (AGENTS.md agent rules) — see C1 for Claude's pipeline exception.
  2. Marc's merge word is separate from any later step (deploy, publish). — Agreed (Oct 11, 2026, chat "AWS EC2 setup for Endless Tales")
  3. MARC DECIDES Never run a database migration or schema change without Marc's explicit OK. — Agreed (AGENTS.md) — see C2.
  4. No agent approves its own merge, database write or production action. Orion, Atlas and Lyra are one agent with different names, so they cannot review each other. Claude is the independent reviewer. — Agreed (Oct 11, 2026, same chat)
  5. The builder never checks its own work. A separate fresh helper verifies. — Agreed (Oct 29–30, chat "Meta campaign testing plan")
  6. MARC DECIDES Stop and ask Marc when a step could overwrite or hide live content. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  7. Never patch the live production path without a restore point first. Never replace a working path with a simpler fallback. Keep what works before improving it. — Agreed (AGENTS.md hard guardrails)
  8. MARC DECIDES No crontab hold line (#HOLD-…) or paused service is turned back on without Marc's word. — Proposed (holds are used, e.g. HOLD-C9, but no rule says who lifts them)

C. Working rules for every agent

  1. One task at a time. One objective per work cycle. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  2. Check results field by field. Say "unverified" when unsure. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  3. "Verified" means only what the agent ran itself: a database SELECT, a file line, or command output in hand. A helper's report is not verification. — Agreed (Oct 16, Atlas/Orion standard Marc required; memory pipeline-dispatch-recovery.md)
  4. All story writing goes through the pipeline (Claude). No agent, including Hal, writes or edits scripts. — Agreed (AGENTS.md; memory agent-fleet.md, Nov 8)
  5. Hal never edits code. — Agreed (AGENTS.md)
  6. Before any fix PR, Claude gives Marc three lines: the cause (not the error message); every other place with the same cause, from a search shown to Marc; why it won't come back. Otherwise it is a patch. — Agreed (PERMANENT RULE 1, memory preferences.md)
  7. A pipeline fix counts as done only when the success rate moves on real jobs. A merged PR does not count. — Agreed (PERMANENT RULE 2, memory preferences.md)
  8. Agent replies use one line per item: DONE + proof, or BLOCKED + reason. — Proposed (used in handoffs since Nov 5; never set as a rule)
  9. If an agent is stuck for 30 minutes, it reports BLOCKED with the reason instead of retrying in silence. — Proposed (no timeout rule exists)

D. Code and deploys

  1. main is the only code line. Every change is a PR based on current main. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md, Nov 6)
  2. Sequencing Rule: no job that depends on a code change is sent until that change's PR is merged and deployed. — Agreed (Marc, 2026-07-22, PERMANENT; cited in docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md). The original wording was not found in the repo; this line restates it.
  3. Pre-Merge Check: a PR that renames or replaces a component must show a diff proving no logic was lost. — Agreed (Marc, 2026-07-23, PERMANENT; cited in docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md, applied in docs/atlas/ATLAS-GAP2-QC-20261011-1408.md). Original wording not found; this line restates it.
  4. Orion is the only one who deploys to the EC2 server. He deploys merged main from a handoff Marc pastes. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)
  5. Every deploy uses the zero-downtime script: build in the idle slot, wait for /api/version to show the new commit, switch Caddy, let the old slot finish (up to 20 minutes), then stop it. A failed build leaves the live app alone. — Agreed (ZERO-DOWNTIME-001, Marc 2026-11-02; scripts/ec2-deploy/zero-downtime-deploy.sh, README)
  6. Each deploy handoff: stop if a build is already running; confirm the commit comes after the current one; keep the old version as the restore point; report the commit, services running and public page 200; no database writes; leave dispatch, cron, render and pool workers alone unless told. — Proposed (the standard handoff used since Oct 28; make it the written checklist)
  7. Re-queue jobs that wait on a fix only after the new build is confirmed live. — Proposed (docs/DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md ATL-OPS-001, written by Atlas; covered by rule 21)

E. Who does what

  1. Orion — Chief Operating Officer. Telegram @OrionETCOO_bot, run through OpenClaw on Marc's Mac. Runs EC2 and database operations, deploys, relays agent work, verifies the ad approval system. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)
  2. Claude — writes all stories through the pipeline; builds the pipeline, app and player (since Nov 6); independent code reviewer; drafts every agent handoff. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md, Nov 6 and Nov 8)
  3. Hal — runs story delivery steps and cuts ad videos. No scripts, no code. — Agreed (AGENTS.md; memory agent-fleet.md; Nov 1 "Confirm Hal")
  4. Atlas — writes code as Orion's helper. — Agreed (Oct 29–30, chat "Meta campaign testing plan")
  5. Susan — Chief Growth Officer: ads, go-to-market, creative. Strategos — Chief Strategy Officer: audience, market, series blueprint (steps 1–2), runs on EC2 behind a server-side key. Details in CANON-13. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)
  6. Bart — finance agent, read-only bank access. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md, /areas/endless-tales-platform.md)
  7. Gemini — screens voices, sound effects and covers, and reads stories (report only). — Agreed (Nov 4–5, memory audio-pipeline.md project copy; chat "Apple App Store commission deals")
  8. ChatGPT ("Sam") no longer works on the app or player (moved to Claude Nov 6). — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)
  9. Codex: the May 2026 campaign spec names "Codex (Claude Code)" as the builder. It has no current role. — Proposed (see Q3)
  10. Other names in Admin (Vega, Maya, Lex, Lyra, Holly, Scribe) have no role Marc approved. — Proposed (see Q4)

F. AI models

  1. The agent fleet runs on DeepSeek, because Claude API costs were too high (Nov 8). Strategos on DeepSeek R1; Atlas on DeepSeek V3. — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md, Nov 5 and Nov 8; replaces Orion-on-Sonnet)
  2. Every agent has at least one fallback model, so one empty account never stops the fleet. — Proposed (Nov 5 Orion outage; in Claude's handoff, not confirmed by Marc)
  3. Model changes go through openclaw.json and the model-policy gate, with a backup and a dry run first. — Proposed (same handoff)
  4. Orion works in short sessions, one task at a time, with Ollama and Docker off and the Mac awake and plugged in. — Proposed (Nov 7 advice; Marc chose no cloud server for now, see CANON-14 rule 55)

G. How Claude talks to Marc

  1. Instructions to Marc are short, numbered and concrete. One step at a time. No bundled actions. Large, readable text. — Agreed (memory preferences; profile: low vision)
  2. If an agent can do a task, Claude writes a paste-ready handoff for Marc instead of walking him through terminal steps. Exceptions: physical Mac access, credentials only Marc holds, or Marc's judgment on audio or story quality. — Agreed (rule dated July 22, 2026, memory preferences)
  3. Give an honest view, not agreement. — Agreed (memory preferences.md)
  4. Time estimates assume AI pace, not human pace. — Agreed (memory preferences.md)
  5. "Report 101" = a table of every open item (what Marc sent, actual state checked in the database or GitHub, done / pending / not started / needs fix), then a numbered list of Marc's to-dos. — Agreed (memory preferences.md)

H. Telegram, watchdogs and alerts

  1. Watchdogs only detect and alert. They never restart anything, clear cooldowns or write the database. The recovery watchdog and the alert watchdog must never fight. — Agreed (Marc rule 2026-07-10; scripts/watchdog/ALERTING-WATCHDOG-SPEC.md)
  2. Alerts go straight to Marc through the Telegram Bot API, with no AI model involved, so they work when models are down. — Agreed (design locked 2026-07-10, same spec)
  3. "MARC ACTION" alerts (usage limits, billing failures, revoked keys) go out at once, then at most once per 30 minutes for the same problem. — Agreed (Marc directive 2026-07-11, same spec)
  4. Orion is "silent" after 45 minutes with no heartbeat. The check runs every 5 minutes, alerts at any hour, then every 30 minutes while still silent. A MONITORING_PAUSED file stops all alerts. — Agreed (Marc decisions Oct 11, 2026, same spec)
  5. Every AI service used by the pipeline and agents is watched. Report 101 alerts, with a top-up link, only for services running low enough to stop the pipeline, Orion or Telegram. — Agreed (Nov 5, memory agent-fleet.md)
  6. The progress alarm runs every 5 minutes from an EC2 timer. It only reads, apart from its own alarm notes. — In force (code) (scripts/ec2-deploy/endlesstales-progress-alarm.timer, ALARM-FIXES-4)
  7. Cast-review voice clips go to the "Voices Ready" Telegram group (Marc + Orion's bot). — Agreed (memory agent-fleet.md)

I. Keys and security

  1. Never open, print, copy or paste private keys, .pem files or tokens. Report env variable NAMES only, never values. — Agreed (AGENTS.md; Amendment 1 §11.4)
  2. MARC DOES Marc enters money-spending keys himself (for example Meta ads_management). Low-risk test keys may be passed through Orion. — Agreed (Oct 29–30, chat "Meta campaign testing plan")
  3. Admin and pipeline write routes (/api/admin, /api/asc3 writes) need an admin login or the internal key. — In force (code) (middleware.ts, ASC3-AUTH-001)
  4. The open /api/v2 routes (author-options, generate-script, load-story, produce-audio, save-revised-script, score-script, series-package, story-brief, validate-script) must get the same login gate. — Proposed (9 of 10 have no auth check; middleware lets /api/ through)
  5. Leaked or exposed keys are replaced, and the old ones revoked: Orion's Telegram bot (renamed by someone Oct 26), the "default" bot, and any key written in a repo document. Bot tokens move out of plain text in openclaw.json. — Proposed (todo list items 12–13; not yet decided or done)
  6. No key, token or password is ever written in a repo document or memory. — Proposed (see C6)
  7. Server security updates are installed in a planned window run by Orion. — Proposed (todo item 16a: 17 security updates pending)

Marc's decisions (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc answered CANON-99 on Nov 9, 2026. These decisions are Agreed and override any rule above that says otherwise. Each conflict or question below that they settle is marked RESOLVED.

  • Decision 12: Retire old manual documents as history: STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS v1.2, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, STORY_GRADING_RUBRIC.md, STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, NEDS scoring, character-attachment scoring, MASTER_RULES.md, DEPLOY.md, DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md, MIX_SPEC.md and MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md level tables, et_mix_assembly.py, ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001 Parts A, D, E. Decided: yes, all. (01 C1, 02 C4, Q5, Q6, 03 Q7, 07 C4, C6, 13 C9, 15 C3–C5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 59: Merging and database changes. Today, AGENTS.md says nothing merges and no database change happens without your word. Older rules (Oct 11 and Nov 2) let Claude merge low-risk pipeline PRs and apply add-only migrations. Decided: keep your word required for every merge and migration (today's rule). It's simple, and you've been giving it quickly. (15 C1, C2, Q1, Q2) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 60: Security, urgent. Rotate the three exposed secrets (Susan's API key and a Telegram bot token in repository documents, an email-service key in memory) and remove them from the documents. Put a login gate on the open /api/v2 production routes. (15 C5, C6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99)
  • Decision 116: All code goes through pull requests on GitHub; never written straight on the Mac. (15 C7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 117: Orion's model setting follows the latest fleet decision (Nov 8: DeepSeek), switched to a faster model when a task needs it. (15 C8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 118: Orion's INCIDENT-RULE-001 is Proposed until Marc approves it. (15 C10) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 119: Codex has no job now; Claude does that work. (15 Q3) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 120: Keep a one-line roster of active agents; retire names with no work (Vega, Maya, Lex, Lyra, Holly, Scribe). (15 Q4) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 121: Claude re-reviews the six self-merged PRs (#333–#338) and reports. (15 Q5) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 122: Orion runs on Marc's Mac only, until the CAC test passes. (15 Q6) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 123: The app runs on EC2; Vercel only builds preview copies. (15 Q7) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 124: An agent reports BLOCKED after 30 minutes without progress. (15 Q8) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 9, 2026, CANON-99 Part 2)
  • Decision 127: No agent edits OpenClaw settings without Marc's OK; after any edit it runs openclaw doctor, restarts the gateway and confirms a clean start and a Telegram reply before reporting done, restoring the backup at once if anything fails. A Mac watchdog restores openclaw.json.last-good after 3 failed starts in a row. A check outside OpenClaw confirms every 10 minutes that Orion is alive and alerts Marc if not. (Cause: Nov 9 settings edit took Orion down 12 hours.) — Agreed (Marc, Nov 10, 2026: "approve 127")

Conflicts found

  • C1. [RESOLVED by decision 59, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Merging. AGENTS.md (canon, Nov 9): never merge without Marc's explicit word. Oct 11: Claude may merge low-risk PRs after reading the diff, except billing, auth or data deletion. Nov 2 and memory agent-fleet.md: "Claude merges pipeline PRs" once tests, build and mergeability pass. Recommendation: AGENTS.md binds the OpenClaw agents; Claude keeps the pipeline-PR exception with the billing/auth/data-deletion carve-out. Write this into AGENTS.md. Marc decides.
  • C2. [RESOLVED by decision 59, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Database changes. AGENTS.md: no migration without Marc's OK. Oct 11: Claude may apply add-only migrations; destructive ones need Marc. Recommendation: same split as C1, written into AGENTS.md. Marc decides.
  • C3. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] MASTER_RULES.md (Jan 18, 2026) says: host on Vercel, commit straight to main from the Mac ("git add . && git commit && git push"), all text white, credits model, news briefings. These clash with the PR flow, EC2 deploys, admin light background, and news being removed. Recommendation: MASTER_RULES.md becomes history. Marc decides.
  • C4. [RESOLVED by decision 12, Marc Nov 9, 2026] DEPLOY.md (old Vercel setup, old price tiers and credit packs) and docs/DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md (wait 3 minutes for Vercel, drivetimetales.com) clash with rule 23–24 (Orion deploys to EC2, zero downtime). Recommendation: retire both; rule 25 becomes the runbook. Marc decides.
  • C5. [RESOLVED by decision 12, 60, Marc Nov 9, 2026] docs/HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md (April) gives Hal script-adjacent and publishing duties, points to retired ET_Story_Rules_v3, and its recovery steps open Telegram to everyone (allowFrom "*", dmPolicy open). It also contains a live-looking Telegram bot token in plain text. Recommendation: retire it, rotate that token. Marc decides.
  • C6. [RESOLVED by decision 60, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Secrets in documents break rule 53: docs/SUSAN-MARKETING-API.md shows Susan's API key in plain text; HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md shows a bot token; memory /areas/endless-tales-platform.md holds a Resend key. Recommendation: rotate all three and scrub them. Marc decides.
  • C7. [RESOLVED by decision 116, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Memory /areas/endless-tales-platform.md (Aug): "all code written directly on Mac via heredoc; commit immediately." Nov 6: PRs on main only. Recommendation: Nov 6 wins. Marc decides.
  • C8. [RESOLVED by decision 117, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Orion's model. Nov 5: Claude Sonnet, DeepSeek fallback. Nov 8: fleet on DeepSeek. Recommendation: Nov 8 wins (memory says it supersedes). Marc decides.
  • C9. [RESOLVED: fact checked or done, Nov 9, 2026; see CANON-99 Part 2] scripts/ec2-deploy/README.md says run-next has no auth. middleware.ts now gates all /api/admin routes. Recommendation: fix the README note. Marc decides.
  • C10. [RESOLVED by decision 118, Marc Nov 9, 2026] workspace-orion/governance/INCIDENT-RULE-001.md is owned by Orion (failure owners, 15-minute detection) with no sign Marc approved it. Recommendation: treat as Proposed until Marc approves. Marc decides.

Open questions for Marc

  • Q1. [RESOLVED by decision 59, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Who may merge what? Suggested answer: Claude merges pipeline/app PRs that pass tests and build, except billing, auth, data deletion and migrations that remove data; everything else needs your word.
  • Q2. [RESOLVED by decision 59, Marc Nov 9, 2026] May Claude apply add-only database migrations without asking? Suggested answer: yes, and report them in Report 101.
  • Q3. [RESOLVED by decision 119, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Does Codex still have a job? Suggested answer: no; Claude does that work now.
  • Q4. [RESOLVED by decision 120, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Which agents exist today (Vega, Maya, Lex, Lyra, Holly, Scribe)? Suggested answer: keep a one-line roster in this doc; retire names with no work.
  • Q5. [RESOLVED by decision 121, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Six PRs (#333–#338) were self-merged with no review on Oct 11–12. Revert, accept, or re-review? Suggested answer: Claude re-reviews them and reports.
  • Q6. [RESOLVED by decision 122, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Does Orion run on the Mac or the EC2 server? (OpenClaw was found on EC2 on Nov 5.) Suggested answer: Mac only, until the CAC test passes.
  • Q7. [RESOLVED by decision 123, Marc Nov 9, 2026] Is Vercel still used at all (crons dead since Oct 22)? Suggested answer: EC2 only for the app; Vercel only for preview test builds.
  • Q8. [RESOLVED by decision 124, Marc Nov 9, 2026] How long should an agent try before it reports BLOCKED? Suggested answer: 30 minutes (rule 19).

Enforcement status

  • Rule 1 → AGENTS.md (document only).
  • Rules 3, 5, 6 → not enforced in GitHub (no branch protection found); depends on agents.
  • Rule 9 → partly: zero-downtime script keeps the old slot as restore point.
  • Rules 21–22 → not enforced in code.
  • Rule 24 → enforced: scripts/ec2-deploy/zero-downtime-deploy.sh.
  • Rules 46–49 → scripts/watchdog/orion-liveness.sh, openclaw-watchdog.sh; alerting half was "SPEC (build pending)".
  • Rule 50 → not built (credit monitor is a todo).
  • Rule 51 → enforced: EC2 timer.
  • Rule 55 → enforced: middleware.ts.
  • Rule 56 → not enforced (open routes).
  • Rules 53, 57, 58 → broken today (C6).

Sources reviewed

  • Repo: AGENTS.md; DEPLOY.md; docs/DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md; scripts/ec2-deploy/README.md, zero-downtime-deploy.sh; MASTER_RULES.md; FLAG_RULES.md; DONE_CHECKLIST.md; docs/HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md; scripts/watchdog/ALERTING-WATCHDOG-SPEC.md; docs/PIPELINE-CANON.md; docs/Orders/ORION_WORK_ORDER_001_REVD.txt; workspace-orion/governance/INCIDENT-RULE-001.md; docs/atlas/ATLAS-GAP2-QC-20261011-1408.md; middleware.ts; app/api/v2/*; app/admin/CommandCenter.tsx; git log.
  • Memory: agent-fleet.md, preferences (snapshot), preferences.md (project), pipeline-dispatch-recovery.md, /areas/endless-tales-platform.md, audio-pipeline.md (project copy).
  • Past chats: "AWS EC2 setup for Endless Tales" (Oct 11); "Clearing CEO series flag" (Oct 28 deploys, "Claude merges pipeline PRs"); "Endless Tales financial obstacles" (Oct 16); "Apple App Store commission deals" (Nov 5, todo list, model outage); "Sunset episode 8 artifact" (Nov 7); "Cover story map pattern" (route security, Nov 4); "Meta campaign testing plan".
  • Project docs: not opened directly (Projects tool not available to this auditor).

Replaces (once approved)

  • MASTER_RULES.md; DEPLOY.md; docs/DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md; docs/HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md — history.
  • AGENTS.md "Agent rules" and "Hard guardrails" sections (moved here; AGENTS.md keeps the canon index and points here).
  • Memory agent-fleet.md role and merge lines; /areas/endless-tales-platform.md code and DB rules — history.
  • workspace-orion/governance/INCIDENT-RULE-001.md — until Marc approves it.

title: CANON-98 — Every Marc Decision Point
status: DRAFT for Marc's approval · Nov 9, 2026 · Owner: Marc
summary: one list of every place in the canon where Marc must decide or act himself, document by document.
body:
Status: DRAFT for Marc's approval · Nov 9, 2026 · Owner: Marc

Covers: one list of every place in the canon where Marc must decide or act himself, document by document. Does not cover: the rules themselves (each is in its own document) or the open decisions (CANON-99).

95 decision points across 15 documents (84 from the audit, 8 added by CANON-99 Part 2, 1 by item 125 on Nov 9, 2026, and items 132 and 133 on Nov 10, 2026). Every audit item in CANON-99 is answered; new requests appear in CANON-99 Part 3.

MARC DECIDES = Marc approves, chooses or gives his OK. MARC DOES = something only Marc does himself (tests on his phone, listens, enters a key). Agents never act in Marc's place on these.

CANON-01 — Story Production Process (the end-to-end map)

  • CANON-01 rule 14 MARC DECIDES: Publish switch. The switch is read at this moment. Review: Marc listens and approves. Direct: the story goes live with no review. Owner: CANON-09.
  • CANON-01 rule 20 MARC DECIDES: Marc decides: merges outside Claude's own pipeline PRs, every database migration, the publish switch, the release of the publication hold, and…
  • CANON-01 rule 32 MARC DECIDES: Adding episodes never re-plans or rewrites existing episodes. Use scripts/series/continue-series.ts (dry run, Marc approves the plan). Never run…
  • CANON-01 rule 35 MARC DECIDES: Never merge a PR without Marc's word (except rule 18), and never run a migration without Marc's OK.
  • CANON-01 rule 56 MARC DECIDES: Stop and ask Marc when any step could overwrite or hide live content.
  • CANON-01 rule 57 MARC DECIDES: Author-written series (Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten by the pipeline. On a failed check it stops and reports; only approved…
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-02 — Story Ideas, Series Planning & Briefs

  • CANON-02 rule 8 MARC DECIDES: No story is written for an author who lacks a style model or a complete style sheet. The job stops and asks Marc.
  • CANON-02 rule 19 MARC DECIDES: A colliding brief is bounced for rework, never retried automatically. Only Marc can let it through, by a recorded override with his name and…
  • CANON-02 rule 20 MARC DECIDES: A premise near a known-adjacent cluster gets a warning but proceeds. Only Marc adds or retires a cluster.
  • CANON-02 rule 28 MARC DECIDES: Preferred series lengths are 3, 5, 7 or 13 episodes. Any other length needs Marc's explicit approval.
  • CANON-02 rule 30 MARC DECIDES: Long Pocket FM series (e.g. 30 episodes) are allowed when Marc orders them, planned in arcs of 10, with one big turn every 10 episodes.
  • CANON-02 rule 31 MARC DECIDES: When Marc or Maya sets an episode count, the story has exactly that many episodes.
  • CANON-02 rule 39 MARC DECIDES: Pocket FM–style writing is used only when Marc says "use the rules for Pocket FM type stories."
  • CANON-02 rule 53 MARC DECIDES: After a series finale, the series is scored for character attachment (0–8); 5+ = recommend a new season to Marc. New seasons must raise stakes,…
  • CANON-02 rule 54 MARC DECIDES: Adding episodes never re-plans, rewrites, re-titles, re-hides or re-voices episodes that already exist. New episodes are planned only for the…
  • CANON-02 rule 63 MARC DECIDES: When Marc or Maya sets a per-episode length, each episode lands within ±20% of it.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-03 — The Writer (Script Rules)

  • CANON-03 rule 2 MARC DECIDES: Author-written series (today only The Sunset of Competition) are never rewritten or regenerated. On a failed check the pipeline stops and reports;…
  • CANON-03 rule 58 MARC DECIDES: NARRATIVE_VOICE is declared (first_person, third_limited, third_omniscient) and held on every narrator line. second_person needs Marc's approval.
  • CANON-03 rule 59 MARC DECIDES: NARRATOR_IS_CHARACTER: true needs Marc's approval and a non-platform voice.
  • CANON-03 rule 90 MARC DECIDES: Gemini reads the scripts before voicing (continuity, easy listening, logic, promise, credibility) and lists exact fixes. Report-only until Marc…
  • CANON-03 decision 133 MARC DECIDES: The emotion check is report-only until Marc reviews three stories with it; then Marc decides whether it blocks.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-04 — Belle Intro/Outro & Listener-Name Personalization

  • CANON-04 rule 19 MARC DECIDES: Broad time-of-day mood: see Conflict C3. Until Marc decides, writers use none.
  • CANON-04 decision 72 MARC DOES: Turn the live name greeting on for everyone after Marc tests it on his phone.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-05 — Voices & Voice Generation

  • CANON-05 rule 1 MARC DECIDES: Belle's voice is ElevenLabs voice GMhgX8fCR9GUtd3kmlKC, settings: stability 0.49, similarity 0.51, style 0.0, speaker boost on, speed 1.0, model…
  • CANON-05 rule 10 MARC DECIDES: After the first episode of each new series is voiced, Gemini listens. Only mismatches Gemini flags go to Marc.
  • CANON-05 rule 47 MARC DECIDES: A published story is re-voiced only with Marc's approval, and the new version is delivered as a link first.
  • CANON-05 decision 78 MARC DOES: Re-voicing a published story always waits for Marc's listen, even in Direct mode.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-06 — Sound Effects

  • CANON-06 rule 4 MARC DECIDES: Marc agreed to pay the one-time $500 API setup fee once Ron (Sound Ideas) confirms in writing that the key can search AND download, uses the…
  • CANON-06 rule 5 MARC DOES: Soundsnap downloads are done by Marc by hand.
  • CANON-06 rule 6 MARC DOES: API keys and logins are entered on the server by Marc himself. They are never pasted in chat or printed.
  • CANON-06 rule 14 MARC DECIDES: A discarded take never comes back. Every discard runs as a dry run first and then needs Marc's explicit word.
  • CANON-06 rule 19 MARC DOES: Gemini is a screen, not the final judge. Marc listens to the final test mix.
  • CANON-06 rule 23 MARC DECIDES: The loop may not run until the library confirms in writing that automated search-download-check is allowed, and Marc approves the code on a branch.
  • CANON-06 rule 44 MARC DECIDES: All sound effects stay off in every mix (SFX_OFF=on) until the professional library is in and Marc approves a test. Voices and music are not…
  • CANON-06 rule 53 MARC DECIDES: A published episode is re-mixed for sound only on Marc's explicit word.
  • CANON-06 rule 54 MARC DECIDES: The first test with the new library is one episode only (Rerouted EP1). Nothing else gets sounds until Marc approves that test.
  • CANON-06 rule 55 MARC DOES: When sounds are added back to published episodes, it is done one series at a time: one test episode, Marc listens, then the rest.
  • CANON-06 decision 80 MARC DECIDES: Once a week, Claude proposes new sound names from the "wanted" list; Marc approves the list.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-07 — Music & Final Mix

  • CANON-07 rule 32 MARC DECIDES: Music is made at most 3 times per story or episode. After that the story is flagged for attention; only Marc can re-queue it.
  • CANON-07 rule 39 MARC DOES: Every mix change goes behind an on/off switch. A test copy goes to a preview folder. Marc listens before it goes live. If it goes wrong, the…
  • CANON-07 rule 43 MARC DECIDES: No corrected episode replaces a published final_mix.mp3 until Marc listens and approves.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-08 — Quality Gates & Marc's Review

  • CANON-08 rule 14 MARC DECIDES: Premise gate (PREMISE-UNIQUENESS-001), before writing → the premise is not a near-copy of another story → sent back for a new premise variant, up…
  • CANON-08 rule 17 MARC DECIDES: validate_script → (a) story-card copy rules, (b) no duplicated passages (Gate 4), (c) AI validator. Failures go back to the writer, up to 2 times,…
  • CANON-08 rule 35 MARC DECIDES: Final audio always needs Marc's ear before going live, except in "direct" mode, which waives it fully. Nothing may assume Marc catches bad audio…
  • CANON-08 rule 36 MARC DECIDES: One publish switch, set only by Marc: "Review" (hold at ready for review) or "Direct" (go live without review). It is read at the moment a story…
  • CANON-08 rule 39 MARC DECIDES: Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends corrections → the corrected version comes to him as a link, not published → Marc…
  • CANON-08 rule 41 MARC DOES: Marc checks player changes on a real phone before they are accepted.
  • CANON-08 rule 44 MARC DECIDES: A Gemini final read of the whole series decides publish / fix (2 rounds) / hold, and Marc gets one message only on hold.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-09 — Publishing & Release

  • CANON-09 rule 3 MARC DECIDES: Review: every story waits at Ready for Review until Marc listens and approves. Then it goes live.
  • CANON-09 rule 5 MARC DECIDES: Only Marc changes the switch, with a one-line instruction or the Admin page switch. It stays until he changes it again.
  • CANON-09 rule 9 MARC DECIDES: In Review, corrections follow the Episode Correction Loop: Marc listens → approves or sends fixes → the fixed version comes to him as a link, not…
  • CANON-09 rule 11 MARC DECIDES: A story goes live complete, with all its episodes at once. A series stays hidden until every episode is finished and approved.
  • CANON-09 rule 16 MARC DECIDES: Sunset of Competition goes live all 26 episodes at once. Marc's release of it counts as his approval of each episode.
  • CANON-09 rule 34 MARC DECIDES: Only Marc releases the hold. Claude or Orion may turn it on to stop test content or a wrong publish, then must tell Marc at once.
  • CANON-09 rule 42 MARC DECIDES: A live story with a problem stays live unless Marc says otherwise ("After the Last Train" stays up).
  • CANON-09 rule 45 MARC DECIDES: A partly published series breaks rule 11. On finding one, do not publish more single episodes. Either finish all episodes and publish them…
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-10 — Covers, Images & eBooks

  • CANON-10 rule 13 MARC DECIDES: A cover darker than 100 out of 255 is remade once brighter. If still too dark, it is flagged for Marc.
  • CANON-10 rule 20 MARC DECIDES: Bulk remakes need Marc's OK on the list and the cost first.
  • CANON-10 rule 27 MARC DOES: Marc tops up image credits himself. No key or card number is ever sent in chat. Image spend is charged to the ET-R&D card, or ET-Marketing for ad…
  • CANON-10 rule 33 MARC DECIDES: Applies to new production only. Stories published before Oct 4, 2026 are not forced back. Backfill is a separate order from Marc.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-11 — The Player

  • CANON-11 rule 37 MARC DECIDES: All episodes publish together. A series stays hidden until every episode is finished and approved, then they all go live at the same time.
  • CANON-11 rule 40 MARC DECIDES: The publish switch on the Admin page decides who approves. It is checked when a story is ready to publish. On "Review", every story waits for Marc…
  • CANON-11 rule 46 MARC DOES: Marc checks it on a real phone before any player change is accepted.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-12 — The Listener App

  • CANON-12 rule 10 MARC DECIDES: The Founding Member plan is retired. No page may offer it without a new pricing decision from Marc.
  • CANON-12 rule 60 MARC DECIDES: A new landing story serves only after Marc adds it to the live list.
  • CANON-12 rule 68 MARC DECIDES: Push notifications are off until Marc approves what they say and when.
  • CANON-12 rule 73 MARC DOES: Marc checks every listener-facing change on a real phone before it is accepted.
  • CANON-12 decision 132 MARC DOES: Marc or a blind tester runs the core path with VoiceOver on a real phone before any release or outreach to blind or low-vision listeners.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-13 — Marketing & Ads

  • CANON-13 rule 1 MARC DECIDES: No ad spends money or goes live until Marc approves its creative and its budget.
  • CANON-13 rule 5 MARC DECIDES: Susan writes ad copy with Claude through her own key, capped at $25 a month. Marc approves the final copy.
  • CANON-13 rule 8 MARC DECIDES: Any new idea for an agent's role in ads (for example, Strategos sending his brief straight to Susan) needs Marc's word before it is used.
  • CANON-13 rule 12 MARC DECIDES: If Meta's preview won't load, the card says "INTERNAL SIMULATION — NOT META'S PREVIEW" and Approve stays off. Only Marc can override, in writing.
  • CANON-13 rule 16 MARC DOES: Marc tests every ad himself, on his phone, before it is uploaded or launched.
  • CANON-13 rule 19 MARC DECIDES: Approval covers only the exact version tested. Any change to video, headline, text, button, link, claims or spend ceiling makes a new version that…
  • CANON-13 rule 22 MARC DECIDES: LAUNCH appears only after Marc approves, and only for Susan and Orion. Each launch records who and when.
  • CANON-13 rule 25 MARC DOES: The Meta write key (ads_management) lives only on the server. Marc enters it himself. Susan never holds it; she calls the gated route.
  • CANON-13 rule 34 MARC DECIDES: Weekly spend never goes over the weekly plan without Marc's approval.
  • CANON-13 rule 41 MARC DECIDES: After the test, monthly ad spend may not go over that month's "Available for ads" amount (plow back, defined in CANON-14) without Marc's approval.
  • CANON-13 rule 51 MARC DECIDES: Low-cost video promo clips (one still image per scene, slow pan, story audio) are a future option only. No build until Marc approves a test, and…
  • CANON-13 rule 61 MARC DOES: TikTok ads use the same approval card, 6 checks, Marc's phone test and playbook read as Meta before any spend.
  • CANON-13 decision 105 MARC DECIDES: Meta's own phone preview never counts as approval, except as a written, dated, one-time override by Marc.
  • CANON-13 decision 107 MARC DECIDES: After the $4,000 test, the monthly ad budget is "Available for ads"; more needs Marc's approval.
  • CANON-13 decision 109 MARC DOES: "Owner tested personally" must be ticked before Approve works.
  • CANON-13 decision 110 MARC DECIDES: Amendment 1 is overridden only in writing on the approval card, with the date.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-14 — Finance & Reporting

  • CANON-14 rule 52 MARC DECIDES: Susan may use the marketing card only with Marc's approval.
  • CANON-14 rule 59 MARC DECIDES: No automatic profit transfers. Any transfer needs Marc's explicit word.
  • CANON-14 decision 125 MARC DECIDES: What Marc reinvests from Part B (money outside operations), and when, is his choice.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

CANON-15 — Agents, Code & Operations

  • CANON-15 rule 1 MARC DECIDES: Only the documents in the AGENTS.md "Canon index" are law. Everything else is history or reference. When two canon documents disagree, ask Marc.
  • CANON-15 rule 2 MARC DECIDES: No agent declares canon. Canon changes only on Marc's explicit word.
  • CANON-15 rule 3 MARC DECIDES: Never merge a pull request (PR) without Marc's explicit word.
  • CANON-15 rule 5 MARC DECIDES: Never run a database migration or schema change without Marc's explicit OK.
  • CANON-15 rule 8 MARC DECIDES: Stop and ask Marc when a step could overwrite or hide live content.
  • CANON-15 rule 10 MARC DECIDES: No crontab hold line (#HOLD-…) or paused service is turned back on without Marc's word.
  • CANON-15 rule 54 MARC DOES: Marc enters money-spending keys himself (for example Meta ads_management). Low-risk test keys may be passed through Orion.
  • CANON-15 decision 118 MARC DECIDES: Orion's INCIDENT-RULE-001 is Proposed until Marc approves it.
  • Open in this document: Nothing open in this document (CANON-99 answered Nov 9, 2026).

title: CANON-99 — Decisions Needed (Nov 9, 2026)
status: PART 1 ANSWERED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: all 60 decided; 57 changed by Marc) · PART 2 ANSWERED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "accept part 2", all 64 approved) · Owner: Marc
summary: every conflict and unanswered question found in the canon audit, with a recommendation for each.
body:
Status: PART 1 ANSWERED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: all 60 decided; 57 changed by Marc) · PART 2 ANSWERED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "accept part 2", all 64 approved) · Owner: Marc

Covers: every conflict and unanswered question found in the canon audit, with a recommendation for each. Does not cover: rules already agreed (those are in CANON-01 to CANON-15).

Marc's answer (Nov 9, 2026)

Marc: "I approve your recommendations with the one exception you fixed above." Every recommendation below is now an Agreed decision, written into its canon document. The exception is decision 57: the plow-back percentage is a setting that starts at 75% and only Marc changes.

How this list was answered

  • Reply "accept all" to approve every recommendation below.
  • Or reply "accept all except 4, 22, 43" and give your answer for those numbers.
  • Once you answer, Claude writes each decision into its canon document, marks it Agreed (Marc, date), and lists the code fixes it needs.

Each item names the canon document it belongs to, for example (03 C2) = CANON-03, conflict C2.

Story ideas, writing and production

  1. Hook series ads start when? Nov 6 said "after Episodes 2 and 3 are live"; Nov 8 said all 7 episodes publish together. Recommend: ads start only after all 7 Season 1 episodes are live. (09 C1, 13 C5)
  2. Hook Episode 1s that are already live alone (Rerouted and the others). Recommend: leave them up; publish Episodes 2 to 7 together; no more single episodes. (09 Q1)
  3. Hook length. The rules say 15 words; the code passes up to 30. Recommend: 15 words, blocking, for every new Episode 1. The 5 live hooks keep their wording. (02 C2, 03 C2, 08 C1)
  4. Episode length. Recommend: standalones within ±10% of target; series episodes between the 12.5-minute floor and 1.35 × the brief; speaking rate 160 words per minute everywhere. Publish code uses the same numbers (today it only allows 15–20 minutes). (02 C5, 03 C3, 08 C2, 09 C4)
  5. Series lengths. Recommend: 5, 7 or 13 episodes, or any length you order (like Altar's 30). 3-episode series only when you ask. (02 C3, Q1)
  6. Cast size. Recommend: the Nov 8 clarity rule wins: at most 4 named speakers (short stories), at most 6 (longer series). The code's 5/7 is changed. (03 C6)
  7. Numbers. Recommend: every number spoken is written in words, including years ("nineteen ninety-eight"). (03 C5, Q5)
  8. Story card description. Recommend: fills two lines, never a third (about 100 characters), checked in one place. The old 24-word and 70-character limits go. (03 C4, 12 C6)
  9. Endings. Recommend: about 1 in 5 standalones may end open; a series finale always answers its central question; one escaped villain is allowed; Belle never teases a sequel. (02 C6, 03 C8)
  10. Spoken-text checks. Recommend: two new blocking writer checks: (a) no sentence split across lines with a trailing dash; (b) no line said twice in a row. Drop HAL-SCRIPT-006 and the 5-word minimum per line. (03 C10, Q1, Q2, Q4)
  11. "Chapter" and "episode" inside the story. Recommend: characters never say "chapter" or "episode" in dialogue. (03 Q3)
  12. Retire old manual documents as history: STORY_PRODUCTION_PROCESS v1.2, SCRIPT_VALIDATOR.md, STORY_GRADING_RUBRIC.md, STORY_BRIEF_TEMPLATE v2.2, NEDS scoring, character-attachment scoring, MASTER_RULES.md, DEPLOY.md, DEPLOYMENT-RUNBOOK.md, HAL_SESSION_START_PROTOCOL.md, MIX_SPEC.md and MIX_NOTE_PROTOCOL.md level tables, et_mix_assembly.py, ACQUISITION-RETENTION-001 Parts A, D, E. Recommend: yes, all. (01 C1, 02 C4, Q5, Q6, 03 Q7, 07 C4, C6, 13 C9, 15 C3–C5)
  13. Author roster. Recommend: the database authors table is the only roster; remove the lists in the Bible and the writer prompt. (02 C1)
  14. Script order. Recommend: header, character guide, then Belle's intro (the Nov 7 spec; what the code reads). (03 C1)
  15. Description load. Recommend: 2 sensory details per scene for standard stories; one short detail for action and Pocket FM stories. (03 C7)
  16. Avoid-list of recent premises, places and names. Recommend: build it now, as a warning. (02 Q4)
  17. Series bible for a continued series. Recommend: the pipeline writes it; you approve it only for series running in ads. (02 Q7)
  18. Repairs. Recommend: text problems go back to the pipeline writer automatically (never an agent); a whole failed production gets one repair pass, then cold storage. "Hal rewrite" in PIPELINE-CANON becomes "pipeline writer rewrite". (01 C2, C3, 08 C7)
  19. Restarting failed jobs. Recommend: Claude or Orion may restart a job once with a written reason; a second restart needs you. (01 Q1)
  20. One episode fails mid-series. Recommend: the whole series holds and you're told; nothing in it publishes. (01 Q4, 09 Q5)

Quality checks and review

  1. Series skip three final checks (hook, length, quality). Recommend: run them on every series episode too. (08 C4)
  2. Quality score pass mark. Recommend: 24 out of 30 (the code's stricter number). (08 C3)
  3. Parked stories. Recommend: one daily list; Orion sorts them and asks you only when no rule answers. (08 C6, Q3)
  4. Gemini's final read. Recommend: report-only until it agrees with you on 9 of 10 series, then it must pass before a Direct publish. (01 Q2, 09 C2, Q3)
  5. Story clarity check until it's built. Recommend: a fresh AI reviewer (never the writer) runs it, and the result is saved with the episode. (08 Q2)

Belle and personalization

  1. Series intros. Recommend: every series intro says the series title, "Episode N" and the episode title. Retire BELLE-006. (04 C1)
  2. Finale order. Today: story → listener-name sign-off → Belle's credits. Recommend: keep that order. The Player Rule is reworded to "no gap between the story, the name sign-off and the credits". (04 C4)
  3. Finale credit. Recommend: "…by [author], read by [narrator], an Endless Tales Original." (04 Q1)
  4. Time of day. Recommend: Belle never mentions time of day ("late drive"), because people listen at all hours. (04 C3)
  5. Outro length. Recommend: at most 42 words. (04 C6)
  6. Standalone stories. Recommend: same as a finale: sting and intro, name greeting, story, name sign-off, credits. No "bridge line" to other series. (04 C7, Q2)
  7. Sting and Belle. Recommend: the sting is always the very first sound, and Belle starts 1.5 seconds in, over the sting's tail, on every path. You confirm by ear. (04 C9, Q4, 07 C3, Q1)

Voices, sound and mixing

  1. Cast approval. Recommend: retired (you said Nov 4 you no longer approve casts); one voice grid for all voices. (05 C1, C2)
  2. ElevenLabs budget. The big credit block expired today. Recommend: a monthly cap that you set, with a stop-and-ask at 80%. (05 Q1)
  3. Sound library. Recommend: Sound Ideas is the main library and Soundsnap the backup; the $169 Soundsnap upgrade is not bought; remove the old ElevenLabs sound-effect fallback. (06 C2, C3, C5)
  4. When sounds come back on (off since Nov 1). Recommend: after Sound Ideas is connected and screened and you approve one Rerouted test mix. (06 Q1)
  5. Who approves a sound. Recommend: a Gemini pass is enough; you listen to one test mix per new batch. (06 C6, Q2)
  6. Background sounds. Recommend: about 10-second scene-setters only; retire whole-scene beds. (06 C4)
  7. Rights in ads. Recommend: no library sounds or music in paid ads until the license is confirmed in writing; record each story's music source. (06 Q3, 07 Q2)
  8. Outro music. Recommend: music sits at 0.13 under Belle with a 3-second fade (your Nov 1 drawing); old numbers and the unused music-bed check are updated. (07 C1, C2)
  9. Loudness. Recommend: the whole episode measures −16 LUFS (±1), peaks no higher than −1 dB, and no section is more than 2 units off the story. (07 Q4)
  10. [MUSIC:OUT] / [MUSIC:IN] marks. Recommend: build them (3-second fades, at most twice per story). (07 C5, Q3)
  11. Re-mixing a published episode. Recommend: Gemini checks the new mix and you're asked only when it flags a problem. (07 C7, Q5)

Publishing, covers and eBooks

  1. No episode goes live alone. Recommend: every publish path refuses to publish part of a series (today the manual publish can). (09 conflict 1)
  2. Who may unpublish. Recommend: only you, except that Claude may hide a story with broken audio at once and tell you. (09 Q2)
  3. Series cover. Recommend: the Library shows one series cover (Episode 1's, unless you pick another). (10 C4, Q1)
  4. eBooks. Recommend: rewrite the eBook prompt to produce real book prose, and make the publish check require the eBook. (10 C1, C2)

Player and listener app

  1. Between episodes. Recommend: build the 2-to-3-second "Up next" screen; one button named Cancel (one time only, goes to the Library); lock-screen Stop acts as Pause; autoplay is always on (remove the unused toggle). (11 C1, C2, Q1, Q3)
  2. Next playlist story missing or hidden. Recommend: skip to the next live story; go to the Library only when none is left. This changes one Player Rule. (11 Q4)
  3. What a playlist is. Recommend: the listener's own "Add to Playlist" list, saved to their account; finished stories drop off. (12 Q1, Q2)
  4. Paywall. Recommend: the paywall never cuts audio mid-story; after a trial, Episode 1 of every series stays free. (11 Q5, 12 Q3, Q5)
  5. Prices and trial. Recommend: $9.99/month, $79.99/year; 14-day trial with a card required for ad traffic; refund once within 7 days of the first charge. Fix the old $7.99 numbers everywhere. (12 C1–C3, Q4, 13 C1, C2)
  6. Old models. Recommend: retire credits and Founding Member everywhere. (12 C4, C8)
  7. Readability and legal name. Recommend: 44-pixel buttons app-wide; legal pages name Endless Tales, LLC. (12 C5, C7)
  8. Settings page. Recommend: remove the controls that don't work; no speed control or sleep timer for now. (11 Q2, 12 Q7)

Marketing and finance

  1. Meta. Recommend:
    • Approve Strategos's stop rules as written.
    • Meta optimizes for Trial Start.
    • CAC goal is under $30; stop above $45.
    • Agents reach Meta only through the gated server routes.
    • Ads run from a new or renamed Endless Tales ad account.
    • (13 C3, C4, C7, Q1–Q3)
  2. Plow back. Marc's decision: the plow-back percentage is a setting that starts at 75%; only Marc changes it, each change is recorded with its date and applies from the next month on. Plow back = that percentage of the previous month's profit ($0 after a loss month), shown as one number ("Available for ads"). The Command Center reads the same setting. The rest stays as reserve. Minimum cash reserve: $5,000 or 90 days of spending, whichever is larger. (13 C8, 14 C3, C4, Q1, Q3) [CHANGED BY MARC]
    • 75% of the previous month's profit ($0 after a loss), shown as one number.
    • The Command Center is fixed to match.
    • The other 25% stays as reserve.
    • Keep a minimum cash reserve of $5,000 or 90 days of spending, whichever is larger.
    • (13 C8, 14 C3, C4, Q1, Q3)
  3. Revenue details. Recommend:
    • Test-account payments count as revenue but not in subscriber counts, churn, LTV or CAC.
    • Sound Ideas cost is 1/12 of what was paid for the current year.
    • Refunds count on the day they leave Mercury.
    • (14 C1, C7, Q6)

Agents and security

  1. Merging and database changes. Today, AGENTS.md says nothing merges and no database change happens without your word. Older rules (Oct 11 and Nov 2) let Claude merge low-risk pipeline PRs and apply add-only migrations. Recommend: keep your word required for every merge and migration (today's rule). It's simple, and you've been giving it quickly. (15 C1, C2, Q1, Q2)
  2. Security, urgent.
    • Rotate the three exposed secrets (Susan's API key and a Telegram bot token in repository documents, an email-service key in memory) and remove them from the documents.
    • Put a login gate on the open /api/v2 production routes.
    • (15 C5, C6)

Part 2 — Remaining items (added Nov 9, 2026, after Marc's answer to Part 1)

Marc's answer (Nov 9, 2026): "accept part 2." Every recommendation below (61–124) is now an Agreed decision, written into its canon document with its conflict or question marked RESOLVED. Nothing from the audit is still open; new rules arrive through Part 3.

Already settled (facts checked or done today; no decision needed)

  • 01 C5: The pipeline runner lives on the EC2 server (endlesstales-runnext, confirmed running Nov 9). Vercel only builds preview copies.
  • 04 C2: Settled by Marc's Nov 8 outro rule, now built into the writer and checks (PR #544).
  • 04 C10: BELLE_B_PROMPT_RULES.md updated to the Nov 8 rule (PR #544); INTRO_OUTRO_BIBLE and INTRO_OUTRO_PRODUCTION_RULES become history.
  • 08 Q1: Publish switch: Direct. Publication hold: ON since Nov 9 (to stop Rerouted publishing early). Every status report shows both.
  • 11 C6: Already replaced by the Player Rules (Nov 9).
  • 15 C9: run-next now requires admin login; the README note gets fixed.

Production, writing and voices

  1. (01 C4) Series checks run per episode once built (decision 21); until then, record it as not fully enforced.
  2. (01 Q3) The Nov 7 Story Production Spec: only the Gemini read (report-only) is approved; the rest is replaced by this canon.
  3. (02 C7) Each series carries its own "style" setting (standard or Pocket FM). The canon list of Pocket FM series is examples only.
  4. (02 Q2) Standalone single stories stay allowed. "No 1-episode stories live" means no series showing only some of its episodes.
  5. (02 Q3) A hook series is a "winner" when its cost per trial is at or under the $26–31 target and at least 40% of its trial users reach Episode 3.
  6. (03 C9) Story clarity: the goal is clear within about 480 spoken words (3 minutes at 160 words per minute).
  7. (03 C11) Drop the NEDS score header.
  8. (03 C12, 06 C1, 06 C7) The old sound rules in the writer documents (3–6 anchor sounds, no beds, sounds 6 dB under voices) are removed; the sound and mix canons own sound.
  9. (03 Q6) The Escalation Ceiling and the story-map acceptance checks become law.
  10. (04 C5) The listener's name comes from one field everywhere: the name they enter as "what friends call you".
  11. (04 C8) Belle names the author in Episode 1's intro (BELLE-004).
  12. (04 Q3) Turn the live name greeting on for everyone after Marc tests it on his phone.
  13. (04 Q5, Q6) Each added batch of episodes is a new season: its first episode gets the Episode 1 intro; the last episode of a season promotes the next season's first episode by number (it is not a finale).
  14. (05 C3, C4) The voice-reuse rule is 30 stories (old 20-story logic removed). Ongoing-series leads get their own custom voice, reserved forever.
  15. (05 Q2) The writer adds a pronunciation hint for unusual names in the character guide; the voice step uses it.
  16. (05 Q3) Build Gemini's listen of each new series' Episode 1 before the next new series is voiced.
  17. (05 Q4) The weekly report shows the count of screened voices.
  18. (05 Q5) Re-voicing a published story always waits for Marc's listen, even in Direct mode.

Sound and mixing

  1. (06 Q4) A sound name may go live with 1 approved take; takes rotate once 3 exist.
  2. (06 Q5) Once a week, Claude proposes new sound names from the "wanted" list; Marc approves the list.
  3. (06 Q6) SFX-ASSET-LOCK becomes canon for voice locking and the manifest check.
  4. (06 Q7) Each series' signature sound (like the Falls Park bell) is one catalog name, used by every episode.
  5. (07 Q6) Belle sits about 3 dB above the story voices (replaces the unbuilt "1.5x" rule).

Quality checks, publishing, covers and eBooks

  1. (08 C5) Every check that only warns gets a written reason in its canon document, or it becomes blocking.
  2. (08 C8) The story clarity check runs before voicing. The Gemini read of the whole series stays report-only until decision 24's trial.
  3. (08 Q4) In Review mode, Marc gets one Telegram message per series with a play link per episode, plus the Admin Review tab.
  4. (08 Q5) The Belle structure check runs in the writer's self-check and before voicing (same check both places).
  5. (09 C3, C5) The old production process and Series Release Rule become history; PIPELINE-CANON's rule titles get corrected.
  6. (09 Q4) Test stories carry a "test" mark, and every publish path refuses them.
  7. (10 C3) A missing cover blocks publishing, but not Ready for Review.
  8. (10 Q2) In Direct mode, Marc does not review covers; Gemini checks each one for maps, keys, text and darkness.
  9. (10 Q3) One eBook text per episode, shown as one book in the reader.
  10. (10 Q4) eBooks for stories published before Oct 4 are made only for stories that stay live, as a separate low-priority order.
  11. (10 Q5) Keep the old cover's link so Marc can switch back.

Player and listener app

  1. (11 C3, C5) No review screen in a playlist (the finished story's card gets the red Rate button). Outside a playlist, after the review screen the player always goes to the Library.
  2. (11 C4) The name greeting plays on the first episode a listener plays; replays get the normal intro.
  3. (11 Q6) The "Continue your story" mini-player stays on Home and Library only.
  4. (11 Q7) iPhone audio that gets quieter during calls is accepted for the web app and fixed in the future native app.
  5. (12 C9) An unknown ad link shows a clear error, never a different story.
  6. (12 Q6) No custom stories until after the Meta test.
  7. (12 Q8) Offer the annual plan at the end of the trial.
  8. (12 Q9) Keep the free guest stories (2 stories / 30 minutes).

Marketing, finance and agents

  1. (13 C6) Strategos sends his brief straight to Susan; Marc's gate is the approval card before launch.
  2. (13 C10) The Meta key lives in the EC2 server's settings (not Vercel).
  3. (13 C11) Meta's own phone preview never counts as approval, except as a written, dated, one-time override by Marc.
  4. (13 Q4) Retire the Airtable campaign system; keep its cash-floor test on the approval card.
  5. (13 Q5) After the $4,000 test, the monthly ad budget is "Available for ads"; more needs Marc's approval.
  6. (13 Q6) Decide what influencer/PR outreach is for after the Meta test.
  7. (13 Q7) "Owner tested personally" must be ticked before Approve works.
  8. (13 Q8) Amendment 1 is overridden only in writing on the approval card, with the date.
  9. (14 C2, C6) Retire the old LTV numbers and the old $59.99 price everywhere.
  10. (14 C5) Five spending sections on the statement: Operations, Story Production, Ad Spend, Marketing Services, R&D.
  11. (14 Q2) In a month with no finished episodes, the $125 Sound Ideas charge shows as unassigned production cost.
  12. (14 Q4) Bart closes each month (reconcile, clear "Other", report) by the 5th of the next month.
  13. (14 Q5) Show AI agent costs per agent once usage logging exists.
  14. (15 C7) All code goes through pull requests on GitHub; never written straight on the Mac.
  15. (15 C8) Orion's model setting follows the latest fleet decision (Nov 8: DeepSeek), switched to a faster model when a task needs it.
  16. (15 C10) Orion's INCIDENT-RULE-001 is Proposed until Marc approves it.
  17. (15 Q3) Codex has no job now; Claude does that work.
  18. (15 Q4) Keep a one-line roster of active agents; retire names with no work (Vega, Maya, Lex, Lyra, Holly, Scribe).
  19. (15 Q5) Claude re-reviews the six self-merged PRs (#333–#338) and reports.
  20. (15 Q6) Orion runs on Marc's Mac only, until the CAC test passes.
  21. (15 Q7) The app runs on EC2; Vercel only builds preview copies.
  22. (15 Q8) An agent reports BLOCKED after 30 minutes without progress.

Part 3 — New rule requests (rolling list)

New rules and rule changes wait here for Marc (CANON-00 rules 10–16). Each item names its canon document, the proposed rule, why it is needed, any conflict it settles, the code it would change, and Claude's recommendation. Marc replies "approve N", "change N: …" or "reject N".

  1. (14) Financial statement layout. APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve 125"). Marc asked for revenue from sales only, cost of goods directly under it, then gross profit, with cashback, interest and money he puts in kept separately as money he can keep or reinvest. Rule: Part A, profit: sales revenue → cost of revenue (story production, delivery hosting, payment fees) → gross profit and margin → operating expenses (Ad Spend, Marketing Services, R&D, Operations) → operating profit; plow back is based on operating profit. Part B, money outside operations (never profit): owner and investor money in (one line per person, running total), owner withdrawals, card cashback, Mercury interest, uncategorized money in; total "yours to keep or reinvest". Settles: decision 112 (five spending sections) and rules 45–47 for the statement's layout. Code: lib/finance/statement.ts, lib/finance/suggestions.ts, app/admin/finance/statement/page.tsx. Written into CANON-14 as decision 125.
  1. (00) Canon numbers file and guard test. APPROVED (Marc, Nov 9, 2026: "approve 126"). Rule: the canon's numbers live in lib/canon/numbers.ts, and the automatic test CANON-GUARD-001 fails whenever the code or a writer prompt file disagrees with them; a changed number is approved here first, then the canon document, numbers.ts and the code change together in one pull request. Why: on Nov 9 Rerouted stopped repeatedly on old code and settings that disagreed with the approved canon. Settles: nothing (new). Code: lib/canon/numbers.ts, __tests__/canon-guard-001.test.ts (PR #564). Recommendation: approve. Written into CANON-11 as decision 134.
  1. (15) Agent settings changes are checked, and Orion is watched from outside. APPROVED (Marc, Nov 10, 2026: "approve 127"). Rule: (a) No agent edits OpenClaw's settings (openclaw.json, the model gate, agent configs) without Marc's OK. After any edit the agent runs OpenClaw's settings check (openclaw doctor), restarts the gateway, and confirms a clean start and a Telegram reply before reporting "done"; if the check or the start fails, it restores the backup at once and reports the failure.
